ActiveCampaign

Is ActiveCampaign worth it?

ActiveCampaign is genuinely best for businesses that want deep marketing automation and lifecycle email tied to a light CRM, and will actually use the automation depth. Skip it if you just need to send a newsletter — a simpler, cheaper email tool does that without paying for automation you won't touch.

How much does ActiveCampaign cost?

(re-verified 2026-08-17 in the browser; the figures below are the 'starts at' prices on annual billing, before you pick a contact count) No free plan, trial only. There are four tiers. Starter is from $15/mo with 1 user, limited segmentation and 5 actions per automation. Plus is from $49/mo with 1 user, standard segmentation, unlimited automation actions and landing pages. Pro is from $79/mo with 3 users, advanced segmentation, predictive and conditional content and attribution tracking. Enterprise is from $145/mo with 5 users, premium segmentation, SSO, custom objects and a dedicated account team. Your email send allowance is a multiple of your contact count — 10x on Starter and Plus, 12x on Pro, 15x on Enterprise. The bill then scales with list size: the per-contact ladder only renders after you select a contact count, which is why we could not re-verify our earlier reading of about $189/mo for Plus at 10,000 contacts on this pass. CRM pipelines, SMS and extra users remain paid add-ons. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with ActiveCampaign?

Pricing climbs with contact count and the add-ons (CRM, SMS, extra seats) stack up fast — the sticker Starter price is not what a serious automation setup actually costs. Powerful, but budget for the tier (Plus and up) you'll really use.

AdCreative.ai

Is AdCreative.ai worth it?

AdCreative.ai is genuinely best for performance marketers and stores that test many ad variations across sizes and platforms and want on-brand creative volume without a designer bottleneck. Skip it if you run a handful of static ads a month (a designer or Canva covers it), or your bottleneck is offer/targeting rather than creative volume.

How much does AdCreative.ai cost?

(re-verified 2026-08-15, read on their own homepage pricing table) Credit-metered, where one credit is one downloaded creative, and there is no free plan — only a 7-day trial with 10 credits. Three families, each with several credit steps. Starter is 1 user throughout: $39 a month for 10 credits and 1 brand, $89 for 15 credits and 2 brands, $139 for 30 credits and $189 for 50. Professional is 10 users and 10 brands: $249 for 50 credits, $339 for 75 and $400 for 100. Ultimate is 20 users and 25 brands: $999 for 100 credits, $1,099 for 150 and $1,399 for 200. Credits expire at the end of each billing cycle and do not roll over. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with AdCreative.ai?

The meter counts downloads, not campaigns — iterate seriously on ad variations and a 10-credit starter evaporates in an afternoon, which is exactly what iteration-heavy ad work does. And the honest fundamental: AI creatives give you volume and speed, but the offer and the hook still decide performance — a mediocre offer with 500 AI banners is 500 mediocre banners. Size the credit tier to your real testing cadence.

Adwisely

Is Adwisely worth it?

Adwisely is genuinely best for e-commerce stores (Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce) that want automated, largely hands-off retargeting and prospecting ads on Meta and Google. Skip it if you run ads across many channels needing granular manual control, or your ad spend is high enough that the 10% fee outweighs doing it in-house.

How much does Adwisely cost?

(price re-verified 2026-09-10) Read on adwisely.com/pricing; every figure below stood unchanged from our previous reading on 2 August 2026. Both plans charge 10% of the ad spend Adwisely manages, with a monthly minimum that acts as a floor rather than a fee on top: $49 on Self-Serve and $249 on Concierge (managed). At $5,000 of monthly spend the Self-Serve fee is therefore $500, not $549, and total monthly Adwisely fees are capped at $3,250 (re-read 15 September 2026). 7-day free trial, no setup fee. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Adwisely?

The honest math is the 10%-of-ad-spend fee on top of the minimum. It is cheap at low spend, but at higher budgets it's a real percentage cut of your marketing dollars until the cap — so calculate the effective cost at your actual spend, not the $49 sticker. It's built for e-commerce retargeting/prospecting on Meta and Google specifically, so it's not a general campaign manager. For stores that want largely hands-off retargeting, it removes real work.

AfterSell

Is AfterSell worth it?

AfterSell is genuinely best for Shopify stores with steady order volume that want to lift average order value with one-click post-purchase and checkout upsells. Skip it if your store gets only a trickle of orders — fix traffic and conversion first; there's nothing to upsell against low volume.

How much does AfterSell cost?

Priced by monthly order volume on the Shopify App Store listing (read 5 September 2026): the free plan is for development and partner stores only; paid plans start at $34.99 a month for 0 to 500 orders, then $54.99 for 501 to 1,000 and $99.99 for 1,001 to 2,000, with higher volume tiers above that. Every paid tier carries a 30-day free trial; checkout upsells need Shopify Plus. Flat monthly fees, no revenue share. The earlier figure of about $9.99 a month is no longer on the listing. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with AfterSell?

Post-purchase upsells only move the needle with steady order volume and a sensible complementary-offer strategy — bolt it onto a store with little traffic and there's nothing to upsell. The no-rev-share model is a genuine plus over percentage-based rivals.

AgencyAnalytics

Is AgencyAnalytics worth it?

AgencyAnalytics is genuinely best for marketing agencies that need white-label client reports from 85+ integrations — automated, on-brand and hands-off. Skip it if you're a solo operator with a couple of data sources, or you want rock-solid single-dashboard KPI tracking — Databox or a lighter tool may fit better.

How much does AgencyAnalytics cost?

One published rate: $20 USD per client / month billed annually, with no clients included in the base, so cost scales directly with your roster (a 25-client agency pays $500/mo; past that it is a quote). Month to month is $25 per client: the card never prints it, but the page's own schema.org block publishes an AggregateOffer with lowPrice $20 and highPrice $25, which is exactly the advertised "Save 20% annually". Add-ons on top: Rank Tracker $41.67/mo per 500 keywords, AI Tracker $20.83/mo per 250 credits. Past 25 clients the vendor quotes instead of publishing (re-verified 2026-09-11). Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with AgencyAnalytics?

Two honest snags. Cost scales linearly with clients — great at 5, pricey at 50+. And the most-cited complaint is connector reliability: data sources disconnect and the platform doesn't always flag the failure clearly. Solo or small-data setups get little value from it.

AgentNest

Is AgentNest worth it?

AgentNest is genuinely best for stores that want an outside read on whether their product data is complete enough for AI shopping surfaces — on the free tier, which gives the entire diagnosis at no cost and no commitment. Skip it if you want a track record before you let an app edit your catalogue, you need a billing unit you can count in advance, or your bulk edits are already handled by Shopify's own editor or an app you pay for.

How much does AgentNest cost?

(read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/agentnest) Four tiers, and the split between them is unusual: the diagnosis is free and you pay only for the repairs. Free: unlimited catalogue scans, a catalogue readiness score, product-level issue reports and the full findings view. Starter $19 a month: 100 successful automated fixes a month, one-click fixes for all eligible issues, product-level recommendations. Growth $49 a month: 1,000 fixes a month, revenue-priority catalogue insights, fix history and progress tracking. Scale $99 a month: 5,000 fixes a month, advanced revenue-priority insights and bulk catalogue fixes. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and no tier shows a free trial. The billing unit is a 'successful automated fix', and the listing never defines it. Whether one fix is one product, one field on one product, or one alt text on one image is the difference between $19 covering a hundred products and a hundred images. It is also the only variable separating the three paid tiers. Developer Ecommerce Storez, 1255 23rd St NW, Washington DC; the app launched on 6 August 2026 and has no reviews at all. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with AgentNest?

Thirteen days old and no reviews. The app launched on 6 August 2026; as of 19 August 2026 nobody has written about it, which is not a criticism so much as the plain state of the evidence. Everything below is read off the listing, because there is nothing else to read. The score is the vendor's own. 'AI shopping readiness' is measured by AgentNest against AgentNest's criteria, and no external standard — no schema.org profile, no Google Merchant Center specification, no published rubric — is named anywhere on the listing. A number that only one company calculates is a prompt to go look at your catalogue, not a fact about your catalogue. On the same page Shopify shows ListingLens and StoreBeam doing the same job, also on free plans. And the billing unit is defined by the party doing the billing. You pay per 'successful automated fix', with no definition of a fix and no definition of successful. Combined with permissions that let it edit products, collections and files across your store, the sensible way in is: run the free scan, read the issue list, fix a handful yourself, and only then decide whether the one-click version is worth 19 cents a go. The same developer's other app, AskNest, has one review in three months — this is a two-app studio finding its feet, not an established catalogue tool.

Aira

Is Aira worth it?

Aira is genuinely best for European B2B sales teams that want AI-assisted prospecting and automatic meeting/CRM hygiene from a Europe-native database. Skip it if your market is primarily US/global (US-native databases cover it better), or you need a mature, battle-tested platform today.

How much does Aira cost?

(read 2026-08-26 on aira.app/pricing) Aira is €149 per user a month, billed monthly, for the company database, AI prospecting, monitoring and on-demand research. Aira Connect starts at €499 a month, billed annually, and adds CRM enrichment and live signals on the accounts already in HubSpot, Salesforce or Pipedrive. These are euro prices for everyone: we read the page from a US connection and got the same euro figures, which fits a product that describes itself as the intelligence layer for European dealmaking across 14 markets. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Aira?

Young product, sharp focus: European B2B prospecting on a 65-million-company database with meeting notes flowing into records automatically. The honest checks: independent review coverage is still thin, so run your own two-week test against a concrete metric (meetings booked, admin hours saved) rather than trusting early-adopter buzz. And note that the money-back guarantee exists precisely so you can do that without risk.

AISDR

Is AISDR worth it?

AISDR is genuinely best for sales teams with a clear ICP and offer that want autonomous AI to qualify leads, personalize outreach and book meetings around the clock. Skip it if you haven't nailed your targeting and messaging yet (automation will scale the wrong thing), or your volume can't justify a ~$900/mo quarterly commitment.

How much does AISDR cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-09 on AiSDR's own pricing page) There are three published plans. Solo is $250/mo or $2,400/yr for a sales team of one: 200 AI-researched contacts a month, 1 user, 1 domain, 3 mailboxes, month-to-month. Explore is $900/mo or $8,640/yr (800 contacts a month, unlimited users, 2 domains, 6 mailboxes), and Scale $2,500/mo or $24,000/yr. Annual billing takes 20% off. Explore and Scale carry a quarterly commitment; Solo runs month to month. Managed service is extra: +$149 per campaign, or fully managed from +$2,500/mo. Enterprise is custom. Priced by contact volume rather than by seat above Solo. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with AISDR?

It's priced like an SDR salary because it's meant to replace part of that function — so judge it on cost-per-meeting, not the sticker, and expect a quarterly commitment rather than a flip-the-switch monthly. Autonomous AI outreach is only as good as your targeting, list quality and messaging guardrails; point it at a bad list and you'll automate bad outreach (and risk your sending reputation). For teams with a solid ICP and offer, it can book meetings at a real cost-per-meeting; for those still figuring out messaging, it's premature. Checked again on 9 September 2026, after AiSDR shipped Ami, the GTM agent it now puts in front of every plan: you hand it your website, it comes back with a target list and a live campaign, and it keeps adjusting the ones that stall. The genuinely new part is memory - your ICP, your exclusions and what a past campaign taught it carry over instead of resetting with each new campaign - and Ami sits inside Solo at $250/mo with no sales call, so the cheapest way in no longer runs through a demo. The scale numbers on the launch page (17,150 campaigns learned from, 19,501 meetings behind them, a rolling 30-day pipeline counter) are AiSDR's own and unaudited, so read them as marketing rather than evidence. And Ami changes none of the deliverability arithmetic: AiSDR's own pricing page still says it takes 30+ days to get multiple inboxes safely warmed, so a first campaign in 20 minutes is the launch, not the result.

AISQ

Is AISQ worth it?

AISQ is genuinely best for solo marketers who want low-cost, pay-as-you-go AI marketing assistance (SEO + content workflows) without a subscription. Skip it if you need a stable, enterprise-grade platform with predictable pricing and naming, or deep best-in-class SEO tooling.

How much does AISQ cost?

(2026-08-30, read on plugin.squirrly.co/wordpress-seo-pricing) Squirrly SEO is billed monthly and renews at the same price. Free $0. PRO $9.99/month: 5 sites, 50 keyword researches, 100 audit suite pages, 0 SERP checker credits. Web Dev Kit $51.20/month: 10 sites, 300 researches, 300 audit pages, 2000 SERP credits. Business $71.99/month: 7 sites, 300 researches, 300 audit pages, 3000 SERP credits. Focus pages per account run 1 / 25 / 70 / 70. Extra SERP checker credits are $19.99 per 1,000 a month. No price is published for the AISQ Meteor agency offer: aisq.com/meteor/pricing and aisq.com/agencies/pricing both redirect to aisq.com/growth/pricing, which sells a done-for-you marketing service instead — $450 for 1 month, $1,235 for 3 months, $2,449 for 6 months, prices excluding VAT. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with AISQ?

AISQ (the Squirrly family) evolves its pricing and product names often — the honest advice is to buy only what's currently priced in front of you, in small credit batches first, and judge output on YOUR niche keywords before committing to bundles. Marketing automation that promises to cut workload 90% still needs your strategy and editing; credits generate drafts, not customers.

Algomo

Is Algomo worth it?

Algomo is genuinely best for B2B teams with real inbound traffic that want an AI agent qualifying visitors, personalizing the site by visitor identity and booking meetings — and don't mind a sales-led buying process. Skip it if you want self-serve, transparent pricing, or you are pre-traffic — an AI inbound agent needs inbound to work with.

How much does Algomo cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on newmode.ai/pricing and the homepage) Plans start at $200 a month with no per-seat pricing - and that single sentence is still the entire public price list, unchanged since our July and August readings. The pricing page carries exactly two plans, Growth and Enterprise, and both buttons say 'Let's chat' and 'Book call': no amount, no contact slider, no self-serve tier. Growth lists 1:1 personalized LinkedIn ads, AI-generated ad copy, website personalization, CRM integration and email support; Enterprise adds unlimited campaigns, custom integrations, a dedicated success manager, priority support and advanced analytics. What drives the price between the two is not published anywhere on the site, so the only figure a buyer can budget against is the $200 floor. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Algomo?

Algomo is a member of the quote-only club: $200/month is the only number on the site, and the real bill for your traffic volume and feature set only emerges in a sales conversation. Budgeting before the demo is guesswork — and quote-priced tools rarely get cheaper at renewal. Worth knowing before it becomes load-bearing: the personalisation runs from a JavaScript snippet in your header, so the tailored copy and routing rules live for as long as the subscription does. Remove the snippet and every visitor sees the original page again.

Alidrop

Is Alidrop worth it?

Alidrop is genuinely best for dropshippers who want automated product sourcing, fulfillment and inventory sync with access to faster-shipping suppliers and one-click store integration. Skip it if you want the absolute widest catalog at rock-bottom sourcing cost, or your margins can't absorb both the subscription and wholesale product cost.

How much does Alidrop cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-13 on their own pricing page) Four monthly plans: Starter $39/mo (50 unique / 25 premium products), Professional $59/mo (500 unique / 250 premium), Empire $99/mo (5,000 unique / 2,500 premium) and Unicorn $299/mo (25,000 products). A 7-day trial costs $1, and there are no transaction or hidden fees. Annual billing is listed only from Professional up — $288, $684 and $948 a year — and the discount grows with the tier: 6 months off Professional, 5 off Empire and 8 off Unicorn, so the advertised “up to 8 months off” is the Unicorn rate rather than a general one, and Starter has no annual column at all. An optional one-time custom-store build service starts at $299. The $1 trial converts to the full monthly rate of whichever plan you picked, and your card stays on file — set a reminder if you are only testing. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Alidrop?

Alidrop's pitch includes faster-shipping (including US/EU) suppliers, but the core dropshipping economics still apply: you pay the subscription plus wholesale product cost, and margins live or die on product selection and ad efficiency, not the tool. The low Starter product cap nudges serious stores up to Pro quickly, and as with any dropshipping automation, the platform reduces but doesn't remove supplier-quality and shipping-time risk. Sample before you scale.

Alli AI

Is Alli AI worth it?

Alli AI is genuinely best for consultants and agencies managing SEO across a portfolio of client sites who want bulk on-page changes, optimization rules and keyword tracking from one dashboard. Skip it if you run a single site — $299 buys far more capacity than you need, and a one-site SEO suite costs a fraction — or you're not comfortable letting software edit pages in bulk.

How much does Alli AI cost?

(prices re-verified 2026-09-19 on alliai.com/pricing) Billed in USD, no free tier, a 10-day free trial on every plan and cancellation from the dashboard at any time. The page shows two ladders behind a Monthly/Annual toggle. Paid monthly: Business $299 a month (5 sites, 5 team members, 500 keywords, 1,250 pages) and Agency $599 a month (15 sites, 15 team members, 2,000 keywords, 5,000 pages). Paid annually: Business $2,990 a year and Agency $5,990 a year, which the page prints as $249 and $499 a month, a saving of $598 and $1,198 respectively. Enterprise is quote-only (50 sites, 50 team members, 5,000 keywords, 20,000 pages). Every quota has a published add-on price that differs per tier and per term: monthly Business is extra sites from $39 each, extra keywords from $24.99 per 100 and extra pages from $14.99 per 250; annual Business $32.50, $20.83 and $12.50; monthly Agency $29, $14.99 and $9.99; annual Agency $24.17, $12.50 and $8.33. Business and Agency carry the same engine — the AI Search Visibility Engine, pre-rendering for 50-plus AI crawlers, the AI bot traffic monitor, LLM Mode, keyword tracking, site speed optimizer, link builder, standard reports and a weekly crawl — and Agency adds only API access, white label and snippet hosting. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Alli AI?

The entry is $299 a month paid monthly — agency-grade automation priced accordingly — and every tier meters on FOUR axes at once (sites, seats, keywords, pages). Growth on any axis costs extra, though at least the rates are published: from $39 per extra site, $24.99 per 100 extra keywords and $14.99 per 250 extra pages on monthly Business. And the category caveat an honest review owes you: bulk automated on-page edits are powerful, but changes at scale deserve human review — unchecked automated SEO is how sites break. One more thing the pricing page does not answer, and it matters at $299 a month: their own FAQ says your site, CMS and code stay untouched, so where changes are delivered through that snippet they last exactly as long as the subscription does. Price this as renting an improvement, not buying one, and ask them directly what happens to applied changes after you cancel before you commit a year.

AltText.ai

Is AltText.ai worth it?

AltText.ai is genuinely best for image-heavy sites that need alt text written back into the CMS automatically: e-commerce catalogues, publishers and long-running blogs on WordPress, Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce, Contentful, DatoCMS or Storyblok. The native integrations, page crawler, CSV import/export and developer API let you clear thousands of missing alt attributes without touching them by hand. Skip it if you have a few dozen images. Write those yourself for free and you will describe them better than any model, because you know why each image is on the page. Also skip it if your visuals are diagram-, product- or brand-specific enough that every generated line needs rewriting anyway — in which case the credits buy you a draft you were going to redo.

How much does AltText.ai cost?

(re-verified 26 Aug 2026) Credit-metered — one credit = one image. Free trial: 25 credits, no credit card required. Monthly: Bronze $5/mo (100 credits/mo, 5¢ per image), Silver $19/mo (500), Gold $59/mo (2,000), Titanium $119/mo (5,000), Platinum $229/mo (10,000). Annual buys the same yearly credit volume at a discount the page labels 17-31% off: $49/yr (1,200 credits), $189/yr (6,000), $489/yr (24,000), $1,179/yr (60,000), $2,199/yr (120,000). One-time credit packs are 50 credits for $3 with no subscription; beyond 120,000 credits a year is custom enterprise pricing. Unused plan credits roll over when the plan renews on its normal cycle, and banked rollover credits and one-time packs stay in the account — but the FAQ states that changing plans, up or down, forfeits the current period’s unused plan credits. You can cancel anytime and keep what is unused, and every feature ships on every plan. Two multipliers change the real per-image cost: advanced formats (AVIF, HEIC, HEIF, JP2, SVG, TIFF) bill 2 credits and are paid-plans-only, and each additional translation language costs 1 more credit per image. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with AltText.ai?

The headline ‘5¢ per image’ only holds for a plain JPG in one language. AVIF, HEIC, SVG and TIFF bill double — precisely the formats a performance-tuned image pipeline outputs — and every extra language adds another credit per image, so by the published rules one AVIF product shot in five languages is six credits, not one. Those advanced formats are also locked out of the 25-credit free trial, so the one thing you cannot measure before paying is your own burn rate. Credits are spent on generation rather than on acceptance: regenerate a line you didn’t like and you pay again, and AltText.ai states plainly that used credits are not normally refundable. The category caveat an honest review owes you: models describe what is visibly in a photo well, but alt text is a judgement call. Whether an image is decorative or informative, and what your brand actually calls the thing in it, is context the model doesn’t have. Bulk generation is a far better starting point than the empty alt attributes on most sites, but treat the output as a draft to spot-check. ‘ADA compliance’ here means the field gets filled, not a legal guarantee that what’s in it is right.

Amplemarket

Is Amplemarket worth it?

Amplemarket is genuinely best for mid-market sales teams (20+ reps) who'll actually adopt the full AI-prospecting, multichannel and deliverability stack in one vendor. Skip it if you're a small team or solo — Apollo starts around $49/user/mo with a free plan and covers the basics for a fraction of the price.

How much does Amplemarket cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-14) The only published price is Startup at $600/mo on an annual term, covering 2 users, with additional users available to purchase; Growth and Elite are listed as Custom, so those numbers come from sales rather than the site. All plans include a free trial. Startup covers 13,500 email address credits and 600 phone number credits per user per year, 2 mailboxes per user and 27,000 contacts. Growth lists 4 users, 35,000 email and 5,000 phone credits per user per year, 4 mailboxes and 140,000 contacts. Elite lists 10 users, 40,000 email and 9,600 phone credits, 8 mailboxes and 400,000 contacts. Two gated rows are easy to miss in the comparison table and both start at zero or near it on Startup: Custom Data Requests run 0, 4 and 12 per plan, so a Startup customer cannot ask for a bespoke data pull at all, and Job Change Alerts cover 500, 1,000 and 2,000 contacts. Duo Inbox is marked as an Add-On rather than an included feature, and the MCP row - prospecting and taking action from inside Claude or ChatGPT - is listed as a platform feature with no plan boundary stated. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Amplemarket?

It's premium and built for teams that will use the whole all-in-one stack. The independent picture is genuinely strong overall: around 4.6/5 across ~600 G2 reviews, with repeated praise for unusually human-sounding AI messages, ease of use and hands-on support. But data accuracy and email deliverability are the most-cited complaints, and they cluster on European contacts — North American data holds up better than EMEA/APAC. Amplemarket points to its own benchmarks showing competitive accuracy, so weigh both sides and test their data against your own target region in a trial before you commit. Under ~10 reps you'll also pay for features you never touch. The genuinely new bit: it now works inside ChatGPT and Claude. Since June that integration can triage the inbox and update or remove leads rather than just search, so reps can run more of the workflow without leaving the chat. Since July that stretches further. From the same chat a rep can research an account, pull enriched profiles and enrol every contact into one sequence with copy written per person and per step. A GTM Skills Library exposes the rest of the platform the same way. Amplemarket says setup takes under two minutes — that is their figure, not one we timed.

Is Apollo worth it?

Apollo is genuinely best for sales teams that want prospecting data, enrichment and sequencing in one affordable all-in-one platform. Skip it if you need guaranteed-accurate data at volume — budget for credit overages, or pair it with a verification step.

How much does Apollo cost?

A free plan (900 credits per seat per year, 2 sequences); paid Basic $49, Professional $79 and Organization $119 per seat/mo billed annually, or $65, $99 and $149 month to month - the annual saving the page advertises is 24%. Organization carries a three-seat minimum, so it starts at $357/mo. Credit-based limits mean the effective cost often runs higher (re-verified 2026-09-11). Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Apollo?

The credit and export caps are the catch — real usage on enrichment and dialing often runs well above the sticker, and data accuracy is hit-or-miss, so verify before you outreach at scale.

Atlas AI Store Builder

Is Atlas AI Store Builder worth it?

Atlas AI Store Builder is genuinely best for sellers testing many product ideas quickly who want a full Shopify storefront from a single product link, and who will genuinely stay inside 5 pages and 250 orders a month or have priced the overage. Skip it if you run one established store with real order volume — the caps turn a $39 tool into a variable bill exactly when the store starts working — or you want a page builder you keep after you stop paying.

How much does Atlas AI Store Builder cost?

(prices read 2026-08-18 on apps.shopify.com/dropshipt and helloatlas.io) The listing says “Free to install”, but that is the development-store tier. A real store runs on the All-in-One plan at $39 a month, billed in USD with a 7-day free trial. Their own partners page says 5 days, so check which you get. What $39 buys is capped rather than unlimited: 5 published pages, $1,000 of bundle revenue, 250 cart orders and 50 AI photos a month. Their pricing page states it plainly: “you’ll be charged the base plan fees and given access to features to a limit, any additional uses for those features can be purchased as shown in the per feature pricing”. The App Store listing adds that “additional charges apply as your store generates revenue and impact”. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Atlas AI Store Builder?

The meter runs on your success, not your usage. $1,000 of bundle revenue and 250 cart orders is a rounding error for a store that is actually working. So the $39 headline describes the bill of a store that has not started selling yet. Price the tier you expect to be on in month three, not the one you sign up on. Two other things worth knowing before you install. The rating is 4.7 from 389 reviews, but 17 of those are one star and the recent ones are about billing rather than the product: one seller writes “cancelled it, uninstalled it, but still getting charged” after two months. And the listing carries a line Shopify does not require of most apps: “Atlas must not be used to copy, duplicate, or reproduce products, product listings, images, or store content from any website, or marketplace without the explicit permission of the rights holder”. That tells you what a paste-a-product-link builder gets used for.

Is Atria worth it?

Is Attribuly worth it?

How much does Attribuly cost?

Aura

Is Aura worth it?

Aura is genuinely best for Amazon and Walmart sellers past the point where manual repricing costs more attention than it is worth, and whose monthly volume sits comfortably inside one band. Skip it if your catalogue is small or your prices rarely need to move — repricing pays back on competition and volume, and at low volume the $37 is buying automation you could do by hand.

How much does Aura cost?

(2026-08-28, checked line by line against their own pricing page; every figure below is the same as on 1 Aug 2026) Flat per account, not per seat, with unlimited listings on every tier. Starter $37/month ($451 a year), Essential $77 ($931), Plus $157 ($1,891), Pro $237 ($2,851) — annual saves 20%. The ladder is set by monthly sales volume, not by features: Starter up to $15K, Essential up to $50K, Plus up to $250K, Pro up to $1M. Marketplaces included: 2, 3, 4 and 6. Aura AI covers 250, 500, 1,000 and unlimited listings; Hyperdrive 10, 25, 50 and 100 allocations; user seats 1, 2, 5 and unlimited. Their table adds three things the earlier reading did not record: monthly sales are calculated on a trailing two months, workflows run 5, 10, unlimited and unlimited, and there is a 14-day free trial. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Aura?

The tier is decided by how much you sell, not by what you need. That is unusually honest as a model — a seller doing $10K a month is not subsidising one doing $900K — but it means your bill moves when your business does, in the same month, without you choosing to upgrade. Pass $15K and Starter stops being the plan you are on. Work out which band you land in the way the page measures it: their table says monthly sales are calculated on a trailing two months, so it is a sustained climb rather than a single spike that moves you up. Two smaller things: the marketplace count is a real cap (two on Starter, so Amazon plus one), and the AI listing allowance is per listing rather than per repricing action, so a large catalogue eats it faster than a busy one.

AWeber

Is AWeber worth it?

AWeber is genuinely best for small businesses and creators who want reliable, simple email marketing with a genuinely usable free tier. Skip it if you need advanced, behaviour-driven automation — newer tools go deeper for the money.

How much does AWeber cost?

(re-verified 11 Sep 2026) A free plan still exists (up to 500 subscribers, 3,000 emails a month) but it is reached through the separate free-signup page, not the pricing page; Lite shows $12.49/mo and Plus $19.99/mo at 500 subs (annual billing; both scale by subscriber count). The ~$899 flat Unlimited tier is served to about one visitor in eighteen rather than withdrawn: on 5 Sep 2026 we loaded the pricing page 18 times in fresh cookie-less browsers, 17 returned Lite and Plus with no flat tier and one returned a three-card variant with “Go Unlimited” at $899/mo for unlimited subscribers, so it exists but you cannot count on seeing it. AWeber runs aggressive limited-time launch promos (an ‘87% off’ banner striking $599 to $79 at research time) — treat banner prices as promos, not list prices. AWeber's own affiliate newsletter of 5 September 2026 describes a single paid plan, 'AWeber Pro', starting at $16.15 a month billed annually, and does not name Lite or Plus at all; the pricing page served us Lite and Plus the same day, so the plan names appear to be mid-change. Check the live page before quoting a tier name. Re-checked 6 September 2026 in twelve cookie-less loads: the pricing page named Free, Lite, Plus and Unlimited on all six of its loads, so the flat Unlimited tier that showed once in eighteen loads the day before was served every time; the free-email-marketing page named only Free. No load carried a plan called Pro and the newsletter figure of $16.15 appeared nowhere; the entry amounts read $12.50 and $20.00. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with AWeber?

BabyLoveGrowth

Is BabyLoveGrowth worth it?

BabyLoveGrowth is genuinely best for solo founders and lean startups who want hands-off SEO content velocity fast, are comfortable with AI-generated articles at scale, and value the 90-day guarantee as a safety net. Skip it if you're building a long-term brand where a spam-update hit would hurt, or you operate in a YMYL/regulated niche where thin AI content is genuinely risky — human-in-the-loop tools fit better there.

How much does BabyLoveGrowth cost?

(prices re-verified 2026-09-19 on babylovegrowth.ai/en/pricing from a European connection, where it prices in euros) Two plans and a Monthly/Yearly toggle that swaps the amounts. Paid monthly, Grow is €99 a month and Scale €399, each shown against a struck-through €247 and €599. Switch to "Pay yearly · save 25%" and the same cards read €75 and €291 a month, labelled "Billed yearly"; the page prints no annual total. Grow carries 30 branded AEO/SEO articles a month, 10 AI prompts tracked daily across ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, $800+ a month in backlinks from the 4,000-site partner network, auto-publishing to WordPress, Shopify and eight more CMSs, a technical GEO audit, Reddit and Quora agents, automated keyword research, one seat and email support. Scale carries 120 articles across four languages, 50 prompts tracked, $1,600+ a month in higher-DR backlinks, unlimited seats, priority same-day support, a dedicated 1-on-1 SEO/GEO specialist and monthly reporting with a human. Both start on a 3-day free trial. The cards promise 90 days money back, but the FAQ on the same page says no refunds are given once the three-day trial ends. The feature table below the cards keeps showing €99/mo and €399/mo in both toggle settings. History: on 5 September we read Scale at €224 a month billed €2,691 a year, and its plan text then added a specialist and extra languages but no extra articles or backlink budget; both the price and the contents have changed since. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with BabyLoveGrowth?

The honest concern here isn't the price — it's the model, and the guarantee that is supposed to cover you if the model fails. Auto-publishing 30 to 120 AI articles a month while swapping backlinks with 4,000 other member sites is exactly the scaled-content-and-reciprocal-links pattern Google's spam policies are written to catch, and the vendor's own FAQ describes the exchange in those terms: your site places links for others as theirs place links for you. It can lift metrics short-term; on a brand you're building for years, it's a real durability risk. The 90-day money-back guarantee used to offset some of that, and we can no longer say it does: the plan cards promise it, and the FAQ on the same page says no refunds are given after the three-day trial ends. Ask for those terms in writing before you pay for a year.

Is Beefree worth it?

Beefree is genuinely best for agencies and in-house teams shipping email at volume across brands or ESPs — a dedicated builder with approvals, brand controls and one-click push to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Pardot and HubSpot, sitting above whatever you send with. How much does Beefree cost?

(price re-verified 2026-09-10) Sold as RGE Studio since the 14 May 2026 rebrand. Starter free — up to 10 designs, 6 exports/mo, landing-page builder, custom subdomain, 20GB/mo image traffic, unlimited users but no roles or permissions. Professional $25/mo billed yearly ($30/mo monthly) — unlimited designs and folders, unlimited reusable blocks, 2 editing users plus 4 view-only, AI writing assistant. Business $134/mo billed yearly ($160/mo monthly) — 2 editing users plus 10 view-only, 2 workspaces, approval workflows, advanced brand controls, QA assistant. Enterprise: custom, quoted by sales. The free trial is 15 days on the Business plan. The embeddable Beefree SDK is a separate product on its own price list (developers.beefree.io) and is not covered by these numbers. Every tier and both billing rates stood unchanged on reallygoodemails.com/pricing between our readings on 21 July, 2 August and 10 September 2026. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Beefree?

Read the seat row before the price row. Professional and Business both cap at two full editing seats, so a "mid-sized team" plan at $134/mo annual still buys two people who can actually build. Everyone else lands in view-only slots — four on Professional, ten on Business — or an Enterprise quote. The free Starter is the odd one out: unlimited users, but with no roles or permissions at all. Exports are metered at six a month, rather than the unlimited free tier its old reputation suggests. And the naming is a live tripwire. Since 14 May 2026 the builder is RGE Studio at reallygoodemails.com, while Beefree remains the company name and the name of the separate developer SDK. So check which product a plan or invoice actually refers to. It is purely a creation environment that never sends, so it always sits on top of your ESP. Worth it when the ESP's native editor is the bottleneck — agencies, multi-brand teams, ESP migrations — and duplicated effort when it isn't.

BidX

Is BidX worth it?

BidX is genuinely best for brands and agencies already spending well past €10,000 a month on Amazon ads, who want bid, budget and campaign automation, Amazon DSP and AMC reporting in one platform with a named growth manager attached. It also suits teams who value a German vendor with EU invoicing, SEPA and direct debit, and support in English and German. Skip it if your ad spend is under roughly $10K a month, because BidX itself routes you to a different product at that size. Skip it too if you want to try before you commit: there is no free trial, the commitment is annual, and the only shorter path is a paid three-month proof of concept. And skip it if you need your total cost on paper before a sales call, because the percentage of ad spend is unpublished — or if you advertise mainly outside Amazon and Walmart.

How much does BidX cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-11, read in a live browser on their own pricing page, EUR view; every figure unchanged since 6 Aug 2026) Amazon PPC is sold in three tiers, and every one of them is a monthly fee plus an unspecified percentage of connected ad spend. They are Self Service Platform €495/month, Managed Platform €1,995/month and Managed Service €4,995/month. The tiers differ mainly in how much of a human you get. That is one monthly strategy call on Self Service, up to two calls and up to 10h of assistance a month on Managed Platform, and up to four calls and up to 32h on Managed Service. Amazon DSP is priced separately on the same page: Self Service €495/month and Managed Service €995/month, again plus a percentage of ad spend. Amazon Marketing Cloud is sold as reporting: €295 for the default report, custom reports quote-only. The Share of Voice add-on covers the first 100 keywords free and charges $250 a month per additional 500 keywords. All prices are net with VAT added on top, and the page states that plans are based on an annual commitment paid monthly; the FAQ adds that new customers can take a paid three-month proof-of-concept period first. Walmart Managed Service, high ad-spend volumes and large agencies are contact-sales. Sellers under €10,000 a month in ad spend are pointed to a separate product, BidX Essential, whose own landing page at get.bidx.io/essentials lists $195/month for up to $10K in monthly ad spend — a flat fee with no percentage attached. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with BidX?

The number that decides your bill is the one number the page does not print. Every Amazon PPC and DSP tier ends with “+ % of connected ad spend per month”, and that percentage appears nowhere — not on the tier cards, not in the footnotes, not in the FAQ. So €495 is a floor, not a price, and nobody spending real money on Amazon ads can work out their monthly cost from this page. Ask for the percentage in writing, and ask whether it is charged on all connected spend or only on what BidX manages, before you get as far as a contract. The second thing to price is the commitment. The page states plans run on an annual commitment paid monthly, and the FAQ confirms it: the commitment is annual, and the only shorter path on offer is a paid three-month proof of concept. There is no free trial. That makes the cheapest visible door €5,940 a year net of VAT before a cent of the percentage — a very different proposition from the €495 the eye lands on. Two smaller inconsistencies worth noticing, because they tell you how carefully the price list is maintained. On a page priced in euros, the one add-on with a hard number is quoted in dollars ($250 per extra 500 keywords), so ask which currency you are actually billed in. And BidX Essential — the $195/month product they route smaller sellers to — lives on a completely separate landing page carrying a 2024 copyright line and a different phone number. It is not listed among the tiers on the pricing page itself, so confirm it still exists at that price before you plan around it.

Free is $0 with 200 credits, no card required, capped at 20 action columns per grid and 50,000 rows. Growth is $349 a month for 15,000 credits, 30 action columns and 100,000 rows, with a two-way HubSpot integration and inbound integrations like RB2B, Factors and Vector. Booster is $799 for 50,000 credits and 50 action columns, adding curated scraping scripts, a private Slack channel and Salesforce integration. Enterprise is quote-only but publishes a floor most vendors hide: annual billing at $15,000 and above, adding SOC 2 and SSO, priority support, role-based team access and Snowflake pipelines. Annual billing takes 10% off. Two lines in the plan table change the arithmetic and are easy to miss. Credits roll over up to three times the plan allowance on Growth and Booster, and not at all on Free, so a quiet month is banked rather than lost. And a credit is spent only when a data provider returns a valid result -- the pricing FAQ says failed lookups, formula columns and CRM syncs are always free -- so a waterfall that finds nothing costs nothing. The page also contradicts itself twice: the comparison table gives all four tiers 100+ data sources while the Free card says 10+ B2B data sources, and the Growth and Booster cards both promise Unlimited Actions while the same page's table caps action columns per grid at 30 and 50. The step from Free to Growth is still the one to plan for: 200 credits to 15,000 with nothing in between, so the bill goes from nothing to $4,188 a year in one move. Monthly company and people search is metered separately at 2,000 on Free, 15,000 on Growth and 50,000 on Booster. Two things the pricing page does not tell you, both read on 11 September 2026. First, what a credit actually buys: Bitscale's own credit documentation prices a found email or phone number at one to twelve platform credits per successful result, depending on how many providers the waterfall is allowed to try, with an AI enrichment at one to two credits a run and a BitAgent website scrape at one. Calls that come in through the API cost nothing. Second, the free tier runs two meters rather than one, and the account screen shows both: 200 platform credits for enrichment and a separate 2,000 search credits for Find People and Find Companies, each resetting monthly. The upgrade panel inside the product also carries a Growth benefit the plan cards leave out -- three hours a quarter with a GTM engineer -- and states plainly what Free locks: credit rollover, more than 20 action columns per grid, the 100+ providers and the inbound integrations. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Bitscale?

The free tier is real and needs no card, which makes Bitscale unusually easy to judge for yourself before paying. What to check during that trial is not the feature list but your own burn rate, and Bitscale's credit table tells you the range in advance: one to twelve credits for every email or phone the waterfall finds, depending on how many providers you let it try. That is the whole budget question. The same 15,000 credits on Growth are 15,000 enriched contacts at one credit and 1,250 at twelve, so the plan you buy matters less than the depth you configure. Run fifty real records on the free 200 credits, read the meter before and after, and multiply by your monthly volume -- that number, not the plan price, is your bill. One free-tier number is worth holding against the other. The plan table gives Free a 50,000-row grid, while Bitscale's own onboarding mail says the free plan scores up to 200 rows at a time -- and both are true, because a Score column, which grades every row against an ideal-customer profile you describe in plain English, is an AI enrichment at one to two credits a run. The grid is not the ceiling, the 200 credits are. Finding the names draws on the separate pool of 2,000 search credits, so building the list is the cheap half; asking the product to judge it is the half that runs out.

Blocky

Is Blocky worth it?

Blocky is genuinely best for Shopify stores below Plus that are losing time to bot traffic, repeat fraudsters or orders from regions they do not ship to, and want blocking rules they control rather than a full security suite. Skip it if you are on Shopify Plus, where the paid plans exclude you outright, or you need chargebacks disputed and revenue recovered rather than visitors kept out.

How much does Blocky cost?

(re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/blocky-simple-country-blocker) Four tiers, each paid one with a 7-day free trial, and every amount unchanged since 22 August 2026. Development Stores is free but only for development and partner stores; it carries all Pro features and starts billing on upgrade. Basic $9.99 a month or $83.92 a year, a 30% saving: enforcement inside the checkout page, unlimited country blocking, a fully customisable blocked page and online support. Advanced $16.99 a month or $142.71 a year adds unlimited IP blocking for IPv4 and IPv6, an IP whitelist and a geolocation country redirector. Pro $19.99 a month or $167.92 a year adds blocking by email, name, address and phone, the Bot Killer for TOR, proxy and VPN traffic, an add-ons blocker, a right-click blocker and unlimited visitor analytics traffic logs. All three paid tiers carry the same restriction in their own plan text: all stores except for Shopify Plus stores. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps, 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, 7722119, Israel; the app launched 7 April 2021, still carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge and is available in eleven languages. The review record has moved: 346 reviews averaging 4.7, up from 324 on 22 August, distributed 89% five-star (308), 5% four-star (16), 1% three-star (3), 0% two-star (1) and 5% one-star (18) — three more one-star reviews than a month ago. The developer replies to reviews on the listing, including an August 2026 reply explaining what the Basic plan is meant to cover. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Blocky?

Read the plan text before you read the badge. The App Store header says a free plan is available; that free plan is Development Stores, for development and partner stores only, and it starts charging the moment the store goes live. All three paid tiers then carry the line 'all stores except for Shopify Plus stores', so if you are on Plus this app is not sold to you. Check that with the developer before you plan around it. A blocker is a blunt instrument, and the review distribution shows it: 346 reviews, 89% of them at the top rating and 5% at the bottom — eighteen one-star reviews, three of them added in the last month. Rules that stop fraud also stop customers. A blocked country catches the expat who genuinely wanted to buy; a VPN rule catches the privacy-minded shopper. The tuning is yours to do, continuously, using visitor analytics that only the Pro tier includes. And it prevents rather than recovers. Nothing here disputes a chargeback that has already landed or claws back an order that already shipped. For that you need a separate dispute tool, which is a second subscription on top of this one.

Bookyourdata

Is Bookyourdata worth it?

Bookyourdata is genuinely best for sporadic, project-based prospecting where a subscription would idle — buy exactly the verified contacts you need, when you need them. Skip it if you prospect continuously at volume (subscription databases price better), or your market is EU-consumer-adjacent where purchased-list outreach gets legally delicate.

How much does Bookyourdata cost?

(re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own pricing page) Pay-as-you-go, no subscription: one credit is one full contact. The published pack table runs 250 credits for $99 ($0.40 each), 500 for $159, 1,000 for $299 ($0.30), 2,500 for $599 and 5,000 for $799 ($0.16). From there it goes 10,000 for $999 ($0.10), 25,000 for $2,099 ($0.08), 50,000 for $3,699 ($0.07), 100,000 for $5,499 ($0.05) and on up to 2,500,000 for $24,999 ($0.010), with anything larger quoted. New accounts get a Free Pack of 10 credits once, with no card. Credits never expire and the 97% deliverability guarantee refunds credits, not money. BeSpoke, the hand-built private list service, is priced separately from $499 for 1,000 records. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Bookyourdata?

The model is honest — no subscription, credits keep, bad data refunded — so the real scrutiny belongs on usage. Bought lists are only as good as your targeting and your sending infrastructure, and cold-emailing purchased contacts has legal boundaries that vary by country, GDPR territory especially. The data being accurate doesn't make the campaign compliant; that part is yours.

Bouncer

Is Bouncer worth it?

Bouncer is genuinely best for email marketers and outbound teams that clean lists regularly and want accurate verification with fair credit mechanics (no expiry, no double-charging). Skip it if you send rarely to a stable opt-in list (occasional pay-as-you-go beats any subscription), or your problem is content/reputation rather than list hygiene.

How much does Bouncer cost?

Email verification credits, pay-as-you-go and never expiring (re-verified 2026-09-11): $8 per 1,000 credits is the minimum purchase. Volume brings the rate down to $35 per 5,000, $60 per 10,000 and $250 per 50,000. Above that it runs $400 per 100,000, $750 per 250,000, $1,250 per 500,000 and $2,000 per 1,000,000 - about $2 per 1,000 at the top volume, with anything above a million quoted by sales. The same calculator offers a monthly-subscription mode for verification that Bouncer states is discounted against pay-as-you-go; it publishes no fixed monthly tiers, so price it at your own volume. 100 free credits to test; duplicates and 'unknown' results aren't charged. The $25/$125/$250 per month tiers are the separate Deliverability Kit and now carry published allowances - 250, 1,000 and 2,500 test emails and 10, 25 and 50 IPs or domains monitored, with an unlimited Enterprise tier on quote. Shield is a separate real-time product laddered by monthly checks: $2 for 1,000, $20 for 10,000, $300 for 250,000 and $1,050 for 1,000,000. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Bouncer?

Not charging for unknowns and duplicates is genuinely fair — many rivals do. The honest framing for any verifier: it removes invalid addresses, which protects deliverability, but it can't make a cold list warm or a purchased list legitimate. Verify before every big send (lists decay measurably per month), and treat 'accept-all' domain results as the gamble they are, not as verified.

Bread & Butter

Is Bread & Butter worth it?

Bread & Butter is genuinely best for marketing and revenue teams that want engaged visitors — people who filled a form or left an email — automatically enriched, scored and nurtured, on a genuinely usable freemium tier. Skip it if you want IP-based company guessing at anonymous visitors — that’s a different tool class (Leadfeeder-style) with a different accuracy and compliance profile — or you run many small sites, where per-website pricing adds up.

How much does Bread & Butter cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-20 on breadbutter.io/pricing) Two published plans. Free at $0: unlimited website traffic, 200 stored lead profiles, 30 days of attribution retention, your existing web forms, lead capture and content gating, social logins with your own branding, server-side journey tracking, CSV, Google Sheets and Mailchimp export, Slack alerts, unlimited team members, one-day email response. AI Enabled Pro at $49 a month per website: 5,000 lead profiles, 10-year retention, 3,000 credits a month, three peripheral sub-domains, one-hour email response, plus attribution reporting, journey and event tracking, custom views, real-time email validation, Focused Score AI, deep profile enrichment, Nurture AI messages, the Focused Index, and CRM, Zapier and webhook sync. One add-on: Scale Credits at $89 a month per 10,000 credits, stackable. Profiles beyond 5,000 cost 2 credits each; Intelligence Brief syncs cost 5 credits each; the Intelligence Stream needs an enterprise licence. Pro comes with a 30-day trial, no credit card. The pricing page publishes no annual rate and no enterprise price. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Bread & Butter?

Two meters to watch: it prices per WEBSITE (multi-site setups multiply the $49) and the AI features run on compute-credit blocks that stack as usage grows. On privacy, refined twice in open dialogue with the vendor (16 Jul 2026, verified against their docs). The anonymous journey IS tracked from the first visit, server-side via their site plugin. So ad-blockers and Safari’s ITP don’t strip it the way they kill client-side scripts — the vendor estimates 30-50% of high-value traffic is lost to client-side blocking. What stays dormant until someone submits an email is identity resolution — the ‘hand-raise’ that connects the captured history to a verified person. You still owe normal GDPR care on enriched data, and the real trade-off is simply this: no IP-based guessing at which company an anonymous visitor works for.

Brevo

Is Brevo worth it?

Brevo is genuinely best for businesses with large contact lists who email selectively and want to pay by send volume, not list size. Skip it if you email your whole list daily — the per-send model can flip from cheap to costly at high frequency.

How much does Brevo cost?

Brevo serves a different price list depending on where you open the page, and the two are not each other's conversion: Starter and Standard differ by more than the exchange rate ($9 and $18 against €7 and €15), while Professional lands on the same 499 in both. Both ladders are below, each with the date it was read. Read on brevo.com/pricing on 6 September 2026 with the currency switched to US dollars and the yearly tab open: Free at $0 with 300 emails a day; Starter from $9 a month for 5,000 emails, or $8.08 on yearly billing; Standard from $18 ($16.17 yearly) adding marketing automation and A/B testing; Professional from $499 ($449 yearly, from 150,000 emails) with multi-user access and contact scoring; Enterprise on quote. Email volume is the headline meter, but every send tier also caps stored contacts: Free stores up to 100,000 contacts (automation on 2,000 of them); on Starter and Standard, 5,000 monthly sends store up to 500 contacts, 10,000 sends up to 1,500, 15,000 up to 2,500 and 20,000 sends or more up to 500,000; Professional stores up to 2 million and only Enterprise is unlimited (help.brevo.com, About Brevo's pricing plans, read 15 September 2026). So a big list you rarely mail still needs the send tier that stores it. Re-verified 19 September 2026 in a browser, this time in the euro view the page serves from the Netherlands and with the plan builder open: Starter €7 a month or €6.33 on yearly billing (the toggle is labelled -10%), Standard €15 or €13.50, Professional €499 or €449.08 with 10 seats included, and Free unchanged at 300 emails a day once Brevo has approved the account for sending. Two things the builder now puts on the public page that we previously had to cite the help centre for: the 5,000-email step lists 500 contacts and 1,000 web-push subscribers as included, and removing the “Sent with Brevo” footer is an €8.10-a-month add-on on Starter while Standard includes it. The Sales Essentials CRM is billed separately at €26.08 a month per seat, Sales Advanced at €53.08. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Brevo?

Charging by sends looks cheaper for a big list you email rarely, but the send tiers cap stored contacts too: 5,000 sends a month stores only 500 contacts, and a 20,000-contact list needs the 20,000-send tier whatever you send. Model both numbers first — and the free daily cap and add-on fees on top.

Is Buzz.ai worth it?

Buzz.ai is genuinely best for GTM teams that want AI to run outbound end-to-end — prompt-driven prospecting of intent-ready buyers, multichannel sequences and meeting booking without adding SDR headcount. Skip it if you send low-volume, hand-crafted outreach (per-seat-plus-credits is overkill), or you're not ready to QA an AI that writes to your market on your behalf.

How much does Buzz.ai cost?

(price re-verified 2026-09-05) Teams: Core is $79 per seat a month with 500 credits a month, AI Employee $695 per seat a month with 5,000 credits; both are billed monthly and show a $0 setup fee, footnoted 'waived on prepaid annual'. Enterprise is custom: 25,000 credits a month, five seats included and a $2,500 setup fee. What is the catch with Buzz.ai?

Two meters run at once: seats AND credits — the seat price includes a credit allowance (500 a month on Core, 5,000 on AI Employee, read 5 September 2026), and real outbound volume means credit packages on top, so budget past the sticker. Watch the moving numbers too: the page changed twice this summer — a $75 teaser, then $79 a seat; $795 with a promised rise to $1,000, then $695 — and the $2,500 setup fee now sits on Enterprise and the white-label plans, so decide on the total for the plan you are actually offered, not the sticker. And the honest fundamental for any AI-SDR: it only books meetings as good as your list and offer, so keep a human reviewing what goes out in your name.

Is CallRail worth it?

CallRail is genuinely best for marketers and agencies that need to prove which campaigns, keywords and ads drive phone calls and form leads, with recordings and multi-touch attribution. Is Campaign Monitor worth it?

Campaign Monitor is genuinely best for brands and agencies that want beautiful, reliable email campaigns with strong templates and client-friendly management, priced per contact. Skip it if you need deep behavioral automation and CRM-grade journeys (ActiveCampaign-class tools fit better), or your list is large but low-engagement — prune first.

How much does Campaign Monitor cost?

Contact-based, on three tiers - Lite (with a monthly send cap of five times your contact count), Essentials (unlimited sends) and Premier (priority and phone support). We could not re-verify a plan amount on 2026-09-14 either: the page prints the euro sign and the words '/month' with nothing between them until you pick a contact count in its slider. That is now the fourth reading in a row with no plan price in the page itself. The only figure the page publishes is the Website Builder add-on at EUR 9 a month from an EU address - our July and August captures both read the same line as $10. Annual billing takes 10% off and nonprofits are offered a further 15%, which the page states for the first time in our captures. There is no paid-free tier, though the comparison table now labels its trial column 'the Free plan' while the contacts row under it says 500 contacts for the 30-day free trial and the send row says a 500-email limit - so the word 'Free' there is the trial, not a permanent plan. The contact brackets run 0-500, 501-2,500, 2,501-5,000, 5,001-10,000, 10,001-15,000, 15,001-25,000, 25,001-50,000 and 50,001+. What is the catch with Campaign Monitor?

You pay for contacts, not sends — so a large, quiet list costs the same as a large, active one, and dormant subscribers are literally a line item. Clean your list before comparing prices anywhere. Is Campaigner worth it?

How much does Campaigner cost?

Is Capsule worth it?

How much does Capsule cost?

(price page re-read 2026-09-11) The free tier covers two users and 250 contacts, and every paid card is quoted per user a month with a 14-day trial that needs no card. Read over a US connection on 26 August the annual figures were US$18 for Starter, US$36 for Growth and US$54 for Advanced, with contacts as the rungs: 250, 30,000, 60,000 and 120,000. Claap

Is Claap worth it?

Claap is genuinely best for revenue teams that want every call captured — by default with no notetaker bot in the meeting, though a customisable bot is there for teams that prefer one — and want those calls to end up as CRM fields, coaching and deal signals rather than as transcripts nobody reopens, with enough seats to make a sales conversation worth having. Skip it if you want to buy and test the product yourself, because the tier with the CRM and coaching features is quote-led and even its trial runs through sales; you need a long retention window, since recordings age out after 2 or 3 years below Enterprise; or you need to be billed in dollars.

How much does Claap cost?

(read 2026-09-04 on claap.io/pricing, both billing toggles and the full comparison table; re-verified 2026-09-08) Licenses are priced per license per month in euros. The only dollar figure on the page belongs to an add-on rather than a plan: a tooltip offers the Power Recorder, which adds unlimited recording length to any paid seat for $20 per seat a month. Basic is €0: 10 videos per user, 300 minutes of recording in total rather than per month, calendar and conference-call sync, 99-language transcript, basic AI summary, the Chrome recorder extension, a collaborative workspace and — listed on every tier including this free one — an unlimited-usage API and the Claap MCP connector, capped at 5 licenses, no guests, one team, one channel, 3 video uploads and 3 months of recording storage. Pro is €24 per license a month billed yearly or €30 monthly: unlimited recordings, 1,000 minutes a month, 500 AI credits per license pooled across the workspace, advanced AI summaries, meeting insights, AI video editing, 10+ integrations, speaker and video insights and private channels, with 50 licenses, 50 guests, 10 uploads a month and 2 years of storage. What those credits buy is spelled out in a tooltip rather than in the plan card: one credit is one Claap AI chat, AI email follow-up, coaching tab or generated insight, and summaries, chapters and the AI companion do not consume credits at all. Business is €48 per license a month yearly or €60 monthly: unlimited recording time, 1,000 AI credits per license, Claap AI across all meetings, CRM auto-complete, AI-generated emails, AI coaching, deal insights, smart tables, admin recording controls and priority support, with 50 uploads a month and 3 years of storage. Enterprise is a custom price and adds SSO through Okta, SCIM provisioning, unlimited Basic licenses, white-glove onboarding and migration support. Basic carries a Try for free button and Pro a Start now button; Business and Enterprise both say Contact us, and the pricing FAQ states that a free trial of a paid plan has to be unlocked by their sales team. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Claap?

The four tiers sell two different products, and only one of them is self-serve. Pro at €24 is the recorder and note-taker. Everything Claap actually markets itself on — CRM auto-complete, AI coaching, deal insights, asking Claap AI a question across all your meetings — starts at Business, €48 per license a month on annual billing, and Business is the only paid tier with no Start now button: it says Contact us. The pricing FAQ closes the other door too, stating that a free trial of a paid plan has to be unlocked by their sales team. So the features you came for cannot be bought or tested without a sales conversation. Your recordings also expire. Storage runs 3 months on Basic, 2 years on Pro and 3 years on Business; only Enterprise is unlimited. If the call archive is meant to be your evidence trail, that is a deletion date on your own data, and it is in the comparison table rather than in the plan cards. Two smaller things worth reading twice, and one correction we owe you. The AI credits — 500 per license on Pro, 1,000 on Business, pooled across the workspace — do not meter the summaries: the tooltip is explicit that summaries, chapters and the AI companion use no credits, and a credit is spent on a Claap AI chat, an AI email follow-up, the coaching tab or a generated insight. What is missing is the rate: no price for an extra credit appears anywhere on the page, so a heavy month of coaching and insights cannot be costed before you commit, and the same tooltip layer is where you find the one dollar-priced item, a $20 per seat Power Recorder add-on on a euro-priced plan. And the free tier's 300 minutes is a total, not a monthly allowance: it is a sample, not a plan you can sit on.

Is Clay worth it?

Clay is genuinely best for modern GTM and ops teams who want best-in-class waterfall enrichment and custom research workflows — and have someone to own it. Skip it if you want to sign up and prospect on day one, or you can't dedicate time to learn it — the curve and credit spend frustrate casual users.

How much does Clay cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on their own pricing page; both billing terms read from the page markup, and no figure has moved since our August reading) Clay meters two things separately — actions and data credits — and each paid plan is an expandable volume rather than a fixed tier, which is the part most write-ups still get wrong, ours included until the August 2026 update. The free plan is real: 6,000 actions and 1,200 data credits a year, unlimited seats and tables, multi-provider waterfalls and Claygent, capped at 200 rows per table and with no phone enrichment. Launch is advertised at $167/mo but starts at $54/mo on annual billing or $60 monthly, and Growth at $446/mo but starts at $185/mo annually or $205 monthly — the headline is a configured volume, not the floor, so read the ladder rather than the card. Billed monthly the Launch action ladder runs $60, $150, $200, $290 and $540 for 15K, 40K, 60K, 100K and 200K actions a month; billed annually it runs $54, $135, $180, $261 and $486 a month for 180K, 480K, 720K, 1.2M and 2.4M actions a year. Growth starts one rung higher: $205, $290, $450 and $850 a month for 40K to 200K monthly actions, or $185 to $765 a month on the annual ladder. Data credits are a separate meter again — monthly from $125 for 2,500 credits up to $2,125 for 50,000, or annually from $113/mo for 30,000 a year up to $1,913/mo for 600,000. Annual billing saves 10%. Waterfall enrichment spends credits per lookup, so the credit meter rather than the plan is what decides the bill. One discrepancy is worth carrying to checkout, and it survived this reading: the plan FAQ at the bottom of the page describes Launch as “starting at $185/mo”, which is not the Launch floor of $54 but the Growth one. Enterprise is quote-only. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Clay?

Two honest catches: a steep learning curve (expect 2–4 weeks, many teams need a dedicated Clay expert), and credits that are hard to forecast at scale. It's an enrichment engine, not a sender — you still need Instantly, Lemlist or Outreach to actually email.

Cloro

Is Cloro worth it?

Cloro is genuinely best for SEO and marketing teams who need AI-search visibility as structured data — who gets cited for which query on ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini and Google's AI Overview — rather than as a dashboard someone else designed. Skip it if you want a finished rank-tracking dashboard rather than an API; this returns JSON with markdown, sources and citations, and you build the reporting yourself.

How much does Cloro cost?

(prices re-read 2026-09-17 on cloro.dev/pricing) Credit-metered, and the credit table matters more than the plan price. Free is $0 for 500 credits a month, one concurrent job and one seat. Paid runs Lite $30 (37,500 credits, $0.80 per 1k, 10 concurrent jobs), Hobby $100 (250,000, $0.40, 20 jobs) and Starter $250 (650,000, $0.39, 50 jobs). Above that come Growth $500 (1,350,000, $0.37, 75 jobs) and Business $1,000 (2,800,000, $0.36, 100 jobs). Four self-serve Enterprise steps follow: $2,000 for 5,871,025 credits at $0.34, $3,000 for 9,306,606 at $0.32, $4,000 for 12,756,261 at $0.31 and $5,000 for 16,391,783 at $0.31, where concurrency reaches 255. Seats are unlimited from Lite up. What a request costs varies by engine. ChatGPT full response is 7 credits, ChatGPT web search 5, Copilot 5, and AI Overview including the SERP 5. Perplexity, Grok, AI Mode and Gemini are 4, and Google Search and Google News 3 plus 2 per extra page. A synchronous call adds 2 credits on top of all of those. Perplexity stood at 3 credits when we read the same table on 17 August 2026. Grok is marked temporarily unavailable, with the page warning that requests to it fail. Credits do not roll over: unused credits expire at the end of the billing cycle, and at zero the API returns 403 until you upgrade or the cycle resets. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Cloro?

The free tier is a sampler, not a trial of the real thing: 500 credits is about 100 async ChatGPT answers at the 5-credit rate we were actually charged, and their table lists 7 for a full response. Fewer, if you call it synchronously -- and one concurrent job means you queue. Anyone running a daily visibility check across a hundred keywords burns through it in about two days. Read the credit table before the price table -- the same $100 buys 250,000 credits, which is 35,700 full ChatGPT calls or 62,500 Perplexity ones, so your engine mix decides your bill more than your plan does. And nothing carries: their FAQ, read 17 September 2026, states that unused credits expire at the end of every cycle, so a quiet month is money gone rather than headroom for a busy one.

Close

Is Close worth it?

Close is genuinely best for inside-sales teams that live on the phone and want calling, SMS and CRM in one place. Skip it if your sales are mostly email or self-serve — a cheaper CRM without built-in calling covers you.

How much does Close cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-12, read on their own pricing page) Per-seat: Solo $19, Essentials $49, Growth $109 and Scale $149 per user/mo, or $9, $35, $99 and $139 billed annually — the same twelve amounts we have now read on 23 July, 3, 11 and 14 August and 12 September 2026. No free plan; the trial runs 14 days and close.com states no credit card is required, with $5 of calling and enrichment credits included, and the page carries a 30-day money-back guarantee. AI credits are pooled per tier (500 a month on Solo, then 1,000, 1,500 and 2,000 per user up to 10,000, 15,000 and 20,000). Chloe, the AI sales agent Close now leads the page with, is free to access on every plan but spends those AI credits plus telephony as she works, so she is metered rather than included. Call minutes, SMS and dialer credits are billed separately and can meaningfully raise the real cost: outbound calls run about $0.02 a minute and phone lines start at about $1 a month. The Call Assistant add-on is $50 a month per organisation plus $0.02 a minute, and additional organisations are $50 a month each, with Growth and Scale including one free secondary org. Premium Phone Numbers are listed as a feature with no price attached. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Close?

The built-in calling is the draw, but call and SMS credits stack on top of the seat price — a '$99' plan can effectively cost ~$160/user once a rep dials 50+ times a day. Great for call-heavy teams, pricey if you barely dial.

Code Bulk Discounts

Is Code Bulk Discounts worth it?

Code Bulk Discounts is genuinely best for shopify stores that already run email or SMS campaigns and need thousands of unique, single-use codes generated out of one existing discount and handed over as a CSV. Skip it if you need one or two codes, which Shopify's own discount screen already gives you at no cost — or the campaign itself is what you want, because this app generates and exports the codes and stops there.

How much does Code Bulk Discounts cost?

(prices read 2026-09-06 on apps.shopify.com/code-bulk and re-verified there on 2026-09-16, unchanged) Two plans, billed in USD every 30 days. Free costs nothing and covers 500 lifetime codes with CSV export. Pro is $14.99 a month and lifts that to unlimited codes per month, with the same CSV export; both plans say they work with most discount applications. The plan table lists no annual rate, no free trial on Pro and no per-code charge, so the monthly figure is the whole cost. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Code Bulk Discounts?

Read the free plan's number twice, because the word doing the work is 'lifetime': it is 500 codes in total, not 500 a month. One influencer drop or one email segment can spend the whole allowance in an afternoon, and after that the only way on is $14.99 a month — so the free tier is a sample, not a plan. What the app does is also narrower than the word 'discounts' suggests. It takes a discount you have already created and multiplies it into unique codes you export as a CSV. It does not create the discount rule, does not send the codes to anyone, and does not report which ones were redeemed, so it sits between your discount settings and your email or SMS tool and needs both of those to be worth anything. The one critical review on the listing shows what that costs in practice: when a merchant's parent discount broke after an unrelated change to their stack, every code generated from it went inactive and they learned about it from customers rather than from the app. The developer's answer is the right one to remember — the rules and logic belong to the parent discount, not to Code Bulk — but it means nothing in this app will tell you that a batch has stopped working. The 5.0 rating also rests on 41 reviews, read 16 September 2026, which is a thin record next to the app's peers.

Cognism

Is Cognism worth it?

Cognism is genuinely best for outbound sales teams in Europe who need mobile numbers that are actually verified and care about GDPR provenance — that is the specific thing this is better at. Skip it if you are one or two people prospecting, because both named plans include five seats; also skip it if your market is US-only, where the data advantage is smaller and cheaper options exist.

How much does Cognism cost?

(2026-09-17, re-read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown. Two named plans, Standard and Pro, both stated to include 5 seats, with everything routed to 'Talk to sales' and 'Get a personalised quote'. The model is credit-based — their own wording is that 1 credit equals 1 revealed contact — with credits included in the subscription per seat, but no allowance is published. Their FAQ adds that a redeemed contact stays usable for the length of the contract and only costs a second credit if that person changes jobs, and that additional credits can be purchased at any point. CRM Enrichment is sold standalone or as an add-on; Data-as-a-Service is priced by volume, delivery method and the fields required, and its API route requires a prospecting seat. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Cognism?

No price, no credit allowance, and a five-seat minimum on both named plans. That combination means the smallest deal is five seats of something you cannot price, so budget conversations start with a sales call rather than a number. The credit model is the part to nail down: one credit reveals one contact, so your real cost per usable lead is the credit price divided by your connect rate, and neither figure is published. Before the call, work out how many contacts a month you actually reveal — that is the only number that lets you judge the quote you get. And it is worth asking whether unused credits roll over, because nothing on the page says.
