Consentmo

Is Consentmo worth it?

Consentmo is genuinely best for Shopify merchants selling into several jurisdictions who want one app to carry the cookie banner, the consent signals the ad platforms now demand, and a first layer of accessibility — and who go in knowing that the region-aware banner and the accessibility tools sit on the $37 tier.. Skip it if you sell outside Shopify; you need one plain cookie banner in one country, which the free tier or your theme already covers; or you need an actual accessibility audit and repair of your theme rather than a widget and a scanner..

How much does Consentmo cost?

(read 2026-09-08 on apps.shopify.com/gdpr-backpack and on the vendor's own consentmo.com/pricing, which list the same four tiers) Billed in USD every 30 days, with a 7-day free trial on each paid tier. Banner impressions are unlimited on every tier, the free one included, so the ladder gates features rather than traffic. Free costs nothing and covers the cookie banner and preferences, the data-request and Do-Not-Sell pages, one banner language and one cookie scan a month, with minimal Consentmo branding on the banner. Standard is $10 a month or $100 a year (17% off) and adds unlimited cookie scans, multi-region compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA and others), Google Consent Mode v2 and Meta, Microsoft and TikTok integrations, US opt-out signals, script blocking, multilingual banners with automatic detection, automatic Google Drive backups and removal of the branding. Plus is $37 or $370 a year and is where the accessibility side starts: web accessibility (ADA/WCAG), smart geotargeting, the EU withdrawal page for Directive 2023/2673, automated monitoring, scheduled scans, AI cookie categorisation, advanced analytics and full CSS customisation. Enterprise is $64 or $640 a year for IAB TCF 2.3, cross-domain consent sharing, a checkout banner for Shopify Plus, Hydrogen and headless support, A/B testing, an alt-text manager, bot and crawler protection and priority support. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Consentmo?

Read the ladder before you budget $10 for this. The two things the listing leads with — web accessibility and a smart region-specific banner — are not on Standard; they start at Plus, $37 a month, which is 3.7 times the entry price. A Shopify Plus store that wants a banner on the checkout needs Enterprise at $64, and so does anything headless or on Hydrogen. The accessibility side is a widget and a scanner: it overlays controls and flags issues, but it does not change the theme markup underneath, which is where an accessibility audit actually looks — treat it as a first layer, not as a remediation. And the free tier puts Consentmo's own branding on the banner your visitors see first.

Convert

Is Convert worth it?

Convert is genuinely best for CRO teams running serious A/B and multivariate testing who want a privacy-first, GDPR-friendly alternative to the big experimentation suites. Skip it if your traffic is modest — statistical significance needs volume, and 100K tested users a month is more than most small sites can use — or your landing-page tool's built-in testing covers it.

How much does Convert cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-20 on convert.com/pricing) 15-day standard free trial — through our link it's an exclusive 30-day full-access trial (verified 16 Jul 2026, no credit card). Growth $399/mo, or $299/mo paid annually ($3,588/yr, which the page calls a 25% saving); Pro $599/mo, or $420/mo paid annually ($5,040/yr, a 30% saving); Enterprise on request, annual only. Tested users are a slider rather than a plan feature: at the base position Growth AND Pro both include 100K tested users a month (1.2M a year), and Enterprise starts at 1M a month (12M a year). The tiers differ on limits — active projects 5 / 30 / unlimited, active experiences per project 5 / unlimited / unlimited, active domains 10 / unlimited / unlimited, goals per project 30 / 100 / 200, custom segments 5 / 10 / 20, deploys 10 / 100 / 300 — and Growth is marked absent on multipage, multivariate and full-stack testing, multi-arm bandit allocation, geotargeting, weather targeting, custom pop-ups and the beta request-approval system. Overuse is metered at $399 per extra 100K on Growth and $699 per 250K on Pro and Enterprise, and can be switched off; each additional custom domain (CNAME) costs $1,000/year. Prices exclude VAT and GST. Native heatmaps and frustration-sensing session recordings are included at every tier at no extra cost and do not consume tested users; 8% of the annual fee goes to tree planting with TIST. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Convert?

The meter is tested users, and it keeps running: blow past your monthly allowance and overuse blocks land at $399-699 unless you hard-cap them — and every extra custom domain is $1,000 a year. The friendly $299 headline assumes annual prepay; month-to-month is $399. One thing people misprice, and it is not the test itself: everyone expects an experiment to end when the subscription does. The trap is the winner. Convert describes itself as a client-side tool where “adding just one snippet of code on your site will then do all of the magic”. So a winning variant you leave running in the visual editor is not a change to your site — it is a rendering by their script. Ship the winner into your own code, or you are paying rent on a result you already bought.

Crazy Egg

Is Crazy Egg worth it?

Crazy Egg is genuinely best for lean marketing teams that want heatmaps, recordings and built-in A/B testing in one consolidated tool — noting that testing starts on the $99 plan, not the $29 one. Skip it if you want generous recordings, automatic heatmaps and qualitative feedback — Hotjar's free tier and product depth suit product teams better.

How much does Crazy Egg cost?

(2026-08-21, read on their own pricing page) Three plans, all billed annually, with a 30-day free trial and — in the vendor's words — no overages, ever. Analytics starts at $29/month and scales on tracked pageviews across 5,000, 50,000, 150,000, 500,000 and 1,000,000 a month, starting at 50 recordings. Growth starts at $99/month, but its slider starts at 50,000 pageviews rather than 5,000, and includes 500 recordings plus A/B testing, CTAs and targeting by device type. Enterprise is quoted. Note a conflict in the vendor's own material: their machine-readable pricing.md still lists an older Starter/Plus/Pro/Enterprise ladder at $29/$99/$249/$599 with different pageview allowances. The live pricing page is the one we read for the figures above. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Crazy Egg?

The entry plan is thin on recordings — 50 a month against Hotjar's far more generous free tier. And A/B testing is not in it at all: that starts on Growth at $99, whose pageview slider begins at 50,000 rather than 5,000. Heatmaps need manual per-page setup and annual-only billing locks you in. Like all these tools it's diagnostic — it shows what's broken, it doesn't fix it. Worth knowing before you treat a result as banked: Crazy Egg states it can run A/B tests “after implementing just a small code snippet directly on the website”, which means a winning variant is served by that snippet rather than written into your pages. Stop paying and the original page is what visitors get. Move the winner into your own templates once a test settles.

Diginius

Is Diginius worth it?

Diginius is genuinely best for lean teams and agencies that want PPC, SEO and lead intelligence consolidated in one affordable dashboard instead of five subscriptions. Skip it if your growth lives in one channel where a specialist tool's depth pays for itself, or you need enterprise analytics rigor.

How much does Diginius cost?

(re-verified 2026-08-21 on diginius.com/pricing/, business pricing) Essential $75 USD a month for 2 users, Pro $250 for 5 users, Core $500 for 10 users and marked Most Popular, Business by contact with sales. The FAQ on the same page confirms a 20% discount for annual payment. The plan limits scale with the price. SEO keywords run 25 / 500 / 1000 / custom, and SEO site pages 1000 / 5000 / 10000 / custom. Lead Intelligence leads run 10 / 25 / 50 per week, and Bombora intent leads 10 / 50 / 100 per week. Contact info credits run 25 / 50 / 100 per month, and support goes from email only to a dedicated customer success rep. The trial banner advertises 30 days including 100 intent leads a week and 100 contact credits, but the mobile plan card on the same page says 14 days. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Diginius?

All-in-one marketing dashboards live or die on data depth per module. Diginius bundles PPC, SEO, lead intelligence and reporting affordably, but specialists — a dedicated SEO suite, a dedicated PPC optimizer — go deeper in their lanes. So buy it as consolidation for a lean team, not as a replacement for expert-grade tooling in your primary channel. Verify the integrations you depend on (especially Microsoft Ads, its historical strength) in the trial.

Dondy

Is Dondy worth it?

Dondy is genuinely best for Shopify stores whose customers already live in WhatsApp — much of Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and Asia — that want cart recovery, order updates and campaigns on the official API without leaving the Shopify admin. Skip it if your customers are on email and SMS, or you need one predictable monthly figure: Meta's per-conversation charges sit on top of every paid tier here.

How much does Dondy cost?

(re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/dondy-marketing-ai, listed as “Dondy: WhatsApp Marketing+Chat”) Four tiers, each paid one with a 7-day free trial, and every amount unchanged since 22 August 2026. Free: a WhatsApp chat button with unlimited conversations, custom size and location, and prefilled messages. Pro $6.99 a month or $67.10 a year, a 20% saving: premium button designs, a WhatsApp widget, text customisation, product URLs in messages, custom hours, reports, and abandoned-cart and order-confirmation messages you send manually. Power Automation $79.99 a month or $719.88 a year, a 25% saving: automated abandoned-cart recovery, WhatsApp marketing campaigns, customisable automated messages, bulk messaging to Shopify segments, an inbox with Shopify integration and the official WhatsApp Business API. It includes 1,000 one-click messages every 30 days and quotes WhatsApp rates starting at $0.0158 in the US on top. Elite $159.99 a month or $1,439.88 a year, also a 25% saving, adds an AI chatbot for sales and support, AI corrections and training, AI product recommendations, a five-agent WhatsApp inbox, green-tick verification assistance, a VIP account manager and unlimited WhatsApp flows; same 1,000 included messages, rates starting at $0.0126. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and Meta's per-conversation charges are separate from all of it. The listing now also advertises work the dossier did not cover in August: collecting WhatsApp reviews through Judge.me, Loox, Yotpo, Trustoo or Google, cash-on-delivery messaging, and AI agents alongside the chatbot; the named integrations are Shopify Flow, Shopify Admin, Judge.me, Klaviyo, Loox, WhatsApp API and WhatsApp Business. Developer Dondy; the app launched 15 March 2023, is available in five languages and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. Reviews have grown to 823 averaging 4.9, up from 774 on 22 August, distributed 92% five-star (756), 4% four-star (36), 1% three-star (6), 0% two-star (4) and 3% one-star (21) — the one-star count is the same 21 as a month ago, so all 49 new reviews landed above the bottom. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Dondy?

The free plan is a chat button. It is a decent chat button, and conversations through it are unlimited. But none of the marketing this app is named for is in it. Automated cart recovery, campaigns and the official API begin at $79.99 a month, and the $6.99 tier in between only lets you send those same messages by hand. You will also get two bills. Dondy charges the subscription; Meta charges per conversation on the WhatsApp Business API. Dondy can only tell you the rate starts at $0.0158 or $0.0126, because the real figure depends on the country you are messaging and the type of conversation. A thousand one-click messages a month are included on the two top tiers; past that, your monthly total is not knowable from this listing, and a campaign to a large segment is exactly the kind of thing that produces a surprise. Model it against your own list size and destination countries before you send one. The rest is Meta's rulebook, not Dondy's. Opt-in, message templates and sender quality are governed on WhatsApp's side, so approval and reach are not things this app can promise you whatever you pay it. The review record is strong — 823 reviews, 92% at the top rating, and the 21 one-star reports have not grown while 49 reviews were added since August — and a misfired broadcast on this channel is still a block rather than an unsubscribe.

Drip

Is Drip worth it?

Drip is genuinely best for an online store on Shopify, WooCommerce or BigCommerce that already has order data worth segmenting and wants ecommerce playbooks — abandoned cart, welcome series, post-purchase — without assembling them by hand. The pricing model suits a list that grows steadily and mails at a normal cadence, because you pay for people rather than per seat or per feature, and every plan carries the whole feature set. Skip it if you are not selling online: Drip says an ecommerce store is not required but that the platform is built for one, and you would be paying for the half you cannot use. Skip it too if your list is large and you mail often, because the send allowance caps at twelve per contact per month once you are past the small tiers. The same goes past 175,000 people, where the published ladder ends and pricing becomes a conversation.

How much does Drip cost?

(ladder re-read on drip.com/pricing on 17 September 2026; every rung below was confirmed on the live slider and matches the page's own pricing object) One ladder, no tiers: you drag a slider to your list size and Drip prints a monthly price. The page now headlines it as paying for your list size and how many emails you send. 1-2,500 people is $39, then $49 at 3,000, $59 at 3,500, $69 at 4,000, $79 at 4,500, $89 at 5,000, $99 at 6,000, $109 at 7,000, $124 at 8,000, $139 at 9,000, $154 at 10,000, $169 at 12,500, $209 at 15,000, $249 at 17,500, $289 at 20,000, $329 at 22,500, $369 at 25,000, $409 at 27,500, $449 at 30,000 and $489 at 32,500; from there it climbs $40 a rung to $609 at 40,000, $649 at 45,000 and $699 at 50,000, after which every extra 5,000 people costs $50 — $1,299 at 110,000, $1,949 at 175,000, and a last published rung of $1,999 for 175,001-180,000 people. Above 180,000 the price is replaced by “Let’s chat”, though the card keeps printing a send allowance. The trial is 14 days and takes no card, and their FAQ states unlimited emails are not available during it. Three things the ladder does not advertise. Chat support is not included at the entry price: up to 5,000 people the line reads “Email support”, and “Chat and email support” only appears from $99 (6,000 people). “Unlimited email sends” stops being literally true at 30,001 people, where the bullet becomes “390,000 email sends” and every rung above it carries exactly twelve sends a month per person at the top of the bracket — 600,000 at 50,000 people, 2,160,000 at 180,000. And the card is not the same at every rung: free migration and personalized onboarding appear from 15,001 people ($249) and are absent on every rung below that. What is carried at every price is up to 50 workflows, unlimited sub-accounts, open API access, dynamic segments, onsite campaigns and the Drip MCP connection, which their FAQ describes as included at no extra cost. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Drip?

The word “unlimited” quietly expires. At the prices most small shops pay, the send allowance really is uncapped. But the switch has an exact address: unlimited holds to 30,000 people, and from 30,001 the bullet becomes a hard number — 390,000 sends there, 600,000 at 50,000 people, twelve per contact per month. Drip never flags the switch. If you run a daily-deal or high-frequency list, do the arithmetic before you migrate: twelve sends per contact is generous for a monthly newsletter and tight for anything that mails several times a week. The second thing to price in is service. The card looks the same at every level, but two lines on it are not: you cannot talk to anyone in chat until $99/month, and free migration and personalized onboarding only appear from 15,001 people ($249). Below those thresholds it is email support and your own move, which is a real difference on the day a broken automation is sending to the wrong segment.

Dripify

Is Dripify worth it?

Dripify is genuinely best for sales teams that already run LinkedIn outreach, understand that automation breaches LinkedIn's terms, and accept that risk with their eyes open — the cloud architecture means sequences run with your browser closed and no extension injected into your session. Skip it if your LinkedIn account is not expendable, since a restriction can be permanent and no tool can promise otherwise; or you are tempted by the 75-a-day ceiling, because the vendor's own advice is roughly a fifth of that.

How much does Dripify cost?

(re-verified 2026-08-26 on their own pricing page — note that dripify.io now redirects to dripify.com) Four tiers, priced per user: Basic $39, Pro $59 and Advanced $79 per user per month billed annually, plus an Enterprise tier that is quote-only. Month to month the same tiers read $59, $79 and $99 per user; both columns sit in the page and the FAQ repeats all six numbers in words. A 7-day free trial runs without a credit card. So the 'up to 35% off' the toggle advertises is real but front-loaded: you pay a year up front to get it, and the discount shrinks as you go up the range — about 34 percent on Basic, 25 on Pro, 20 on Advanced. What each tier buys is unusually consequential here, and the page now prints the daily quotas instead of calling them 'limited': Basic sends 20 connection requests, 30 messages, 10 Sales Navigator InMails and 100 profile views a day, against 75, 100+, 30 and 200+ on Pro and Advanced. Basic is also capped at one drip campaign; unlimited campaigns and full quotas start at Pro, which adds a dedicated inbox, CSV export and the webhook and HubSpot integrations, and Advanced adds multi-team management, advanced LinkedIn protection, lead tagging, step analytics and evergreen leads. Every tier includes 100 email-finder credits a month and the top-ups are priced openly: 1,000 credits $29, 2,000 $49, 5,000 $69, 10,000 $99. One seat connects one LinkedIn account, so five reps means five seats, and ten or more seats goes through sales. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Dripify?

Understand what you are buying before the price matters: LinkedIn prohibits this entire product category. Its User Agreement bans using 'bots or other unauthorized automated methods' to 'send or redirect messages', and its prohibited-software page says members using such tools 'risk having their accounts restricted or shut down'. There is no carve-out for cloud tools or low volumes, and Dripify is not an outlier here — every competitor sits on the same side of that line. Dripify's own documentation is candid about the consequence, warning that LinkedIn 'may issue warnings, temporary restrictions, or even permanent bans', and it publishes a recovery procedure for exactly that scenario. Two things follow. First, the advertised ceiling is not a working speed: the app allows up to 75 connection requests a day, while Dripify's own setup guide tells beginners to run 10 to 15, and brand-new accounts 2 to 5, building up 10 to 20 percent a week. Anyone buying on the headline number is buying capacity they are told not to use. Second, Activity Control sits on the $79 Advanced tier. It is the feature Dripify names as its best protection, and it adjusts your pace automatically. On Basic and Pro, safe pacing is your own manual responsibility. And when a vendor writes that a feature 'makes sure your LinkedIn account won't get flagged', read that as a claim about a third party's enforcement decisions that no vendor can actually guarantee.

Dripshipper

Is Dripshipper worth it?

Dripshipper is genuinely best for someone who wants a turnkey private-label coffee or tea brand on Shopify — their roasting and packaging, your label on the bag — and is content to stay inside one product category. Skip it if you want product breadth, fulfilment outside the US, or control over sourcing and packaging cost — this is a single-supplier pipeline and the higher tiers only add coaching.

How much does Dripshipper cost?

(re-read 2026-09-17 on apps.shopify.com/dripshipper, listed as “Dripshipper: Coffee & Tea”) Starter $30 a month, Professional $99 and Elite $197, each with a 14-day free trial — all three unchanged since 19 August 2026. Starter is also sold annually at $240 a year, which is $20 a month for the same tier, and it is the only tier with a published annual rate. The listing does spell out what the steps buy: Starter carries unlimited orders, unlimited products, automatic order fulfilment, a dedicated support team and 1-click product add; Professional adds live monthly training, priority support and a dedicated success manager; Elite adds monthly one-on-one coaching on top. Product and shipping cost is charged per order on top of the subscription. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. The listing now carries 159 reviews averaging 4.8, up from 142 averaging 4.7 on 19 August, distributed 130 / 14 / 7 / 4 / 4 from five down to one. Developer The Doughty Organization; the app launched 11 April 2018. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Dripshipper?

Read the ladder before you climb it. Starter already carries unlimited orders, unlimited products and automatic fulfilment — the whole product, in other words. Professional at $99 adds live monthly training, priority support and a success manager; Elite at $197 adds monthly one-on-one coaching on top. You are buying people, not capability: nothing above Starter makes the coffee ship faster or cost less per bag. The annual rate is the move worth noticing in the other direction, since $240 a year against $30 a month is a third off the same tier. Beyond that the model is narrow by design — one product category, roasted and shipped from their own US facilities in 3-5 business days, with no route to source elsewhere or negotiate the per-order cost.

Is DropGenius worth it?

How much does DropGenius cost?

Re-verified 19 September 2026 on their own pricing page, unchanged since August. Monthly: Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99, Unicorn $299, each with a 14-day free trial. What is the catch with DropGenius?

Dynasort

Is Dynasort worth it?

Dynasort is genuinely best for Shopify stores with large or fast-changing catalogues where product order is a merchandising decision — seasonal ranges, frequent stock-outs, wide margin spreads — and nobody who wants to re-order collections by hand every week.. Skip it if your catalogue is small enough for one person to curate in an afternoon, the order barely changes, or you are not on Shopify — at $99 a month for the first paid tier, the sorting has to be earning its fee.

How much does Dynasort cost?

(re-read 15 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/dynasort) Four tiers, all billed in USD and recurring every 30 days. Demo is free for as long as you like: 2 collections sorted round the clock, 10 recipes drawn from 40+ signals, 2 managed collections that build themselves, 10,000 serves a month, 7 days of serving analytics and a re-sort every 60 minutes. The three paid cards are described by four capacity lines and three yes/no lines rather than by feature lists. Basic is $99 a month for 25 sorted collections, 10 managed collections, 20 recipes and a 30-minute processing schedule, with custom attributes, partner integration and product boost all switched off. Pro is $249 for 100 sorted collections, 25 managed, 25 recipes and a 20-minute schedule, and switches all three of those on. Enterprise is $499 for 1,000 sorted collections, 100 managed, 250 recipes and a 10-minute schedule. Every paid tier carries a 30-day free trial, which is long enough to actually measure the effect. One number the paid cards do not publish is a serve allowance: only the free Demo card names one, so if serves are what your traffic will consume, ask before you buy. This reading corrects an earlier one made on 14 September 2026, which recorded the Pro and Enterprise capacity blocks the other way round; on 15 September the ladder rises from Basic to Enterprise on every line. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Dynasort?

Sorting driven by 40+ blended signals is powerful and opaque in the same breath: a recipe that ranks by margin, velocity and stock at once will sometimes bury a product you wanted seen, and there is real trial and error in getting the recipes to match how you actually merchandise. The jump from free to paid is steep at $99 a month, and it buys capacity without capability — custom attributes, partner integration and product boost all start at $249. The paid cards also publish no serve allowance, so the meter the free tier is capped on (10,000 serves a month) disappears from the page exactly where you start paying. And the evidence base is thin: 4.6 from 15 reviews, with fourteen fives and a single one-star and nothing in between. It is Shopify-only, so it is not an option if any part of your catalogue lives elsewhere.

Easy Bundles

Is Easy Bundles worth it?

Easy Bundles is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want build-your-own-box, gift-box, mix-and-match, fixed-price or volume bundles live in days rather than sprints, with bundle inventory syncing across Shopify and 3PLs and bundles that also sell through POS — and whose bundle revenue is still small enough to sit comfortably inside a published tier. Skip it if your bundle sales already run past $10,000 a month, because that is where the published ladder ends and the overage is not disclosed; or you need one straightforward fixed or mix-and-match bundle, which Shopify's own free first-party Bundles app already covers.

How much does Easy Bundles cost?

(read 2026-09-04 on apps.shopify.com/bundle-builder) Four tiers billed in USD every 30 days, and the meter is the part that matters: you are charged on bundle sales, not on orders, products or staff. The free plan is free to install and covers up to $500 of bundle sales a month. Essential is $29 a month or $299 a year and lifts that to $3,000; Growth is $49 or $499 a year up to $5,000; Scale is $99 or $999 a year up to $10,000. Annual billing saves 14% to 16% depending on the tier, and every paid tier has a 15-day free trial. Features climb the same ladder: free gives mix-and-match, fixed and volume bundles with templates and a custom or template design; Essential adds the single-step and multi-step bundle builders, landing-page templates, search and filtering, and multi-currency and multi-language support; Growth adds advanced discount logic, custom personalisation fields, add-ons, free gifts and subscription bundles; Scale adds AI-generated designs, advanced analytics, one-to-one onboarding and an account manager on Slack. Two things the block does not say are worth noting before you commit. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Easy Bundles?

The pricing is tied to the thing the app is supposed to grow. A revenue meter reads as generous at the bottom — $500 of bundle sales a month free is a real trial, not a crippled one — but it means every tier upgrade is triggered by the app working, and the published ladder stops at $10,000 a month with no stated overage. A store doing well on bundles has to ask what comes next rather than read it, and that is the wrong moment to be negotiating. Maturity is not the concern here: the app has been on the App Store since 15 September 2022 and carried 4.9 stars over 1,216 reviews on 4 September 2026 and 1,298 on 19 September, at the same average. The concern is where the money goes as you succeed. Two smaller things: the features most merchants picture when they think bundles are all paid: the guided single- and multi-step build-your-own-box builders sit on Essential at $29, and subscription bundles, add-ons and free gifts on Growth at $49 — none of them on the free plan, and the recent reviews that praise the app most warmly also praise the support team by name, which is a compliment to people rather than to a product that never needs them.

Is EcomXray worth it?

How much does EcomXray cost?

And its numbers are only as good as your cost prices. Is EmailListVerify worth it?

How much does EmailListVerify cost?

Is EngageBay worth it?

How much does EngageBay cost?

Essential Loyalty

Is Essential Loyalty worth it?

Essential Loyalty is genuinely best for Shopify stores with genuine repeat business that want a loyalty programme priced on the orders it influences rather than on total volume — and stores selling in person too, since POS support arrives at $10 and the free tier carries VIP tiers and referrals. Skip it if your customers buy once and rarely return, because a loyalty programme has nothing to work with and the free tier shows you that within a month; or you need API work from the start, since integrations are 'on request' and only on the $79 tier.

How much does Essential Loyalty cost?

(re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/essential-loyalty-rewards-program) Four tiers, every amount unchanged since 22 August 2026, and the meter is still the whole decision: it counts loyalty-influenced orders — repeat sales and referrals — rather than every order your store takes, which the plan text states outright. Free covers up to 250 of those and is unusually complete: the point program, VIP tiers, a referral program, twelve-plus ways to earn points, product, cart, popup and account placements, built-in email notifications with Klaviyo, and discount, gift, shipping and credit rewards. Starter is $10 a month for up to 500, adding a dedicated loyalty landing page, full customisation, Shopify Flow, POS support for in-store loyalty and 24/7 human support. Essential is $24 for up to 1,500, adding loyalty status on the customer orders and profile pages and points in product cards. Growth is $79 for unlimited loyalty orders, with API integrations on request, white-glove onboarding and priority support. Paid plans carry a 14-day free trial. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Essential Apps. The listing works with Checkout, Customer accounts, Shopify POS, Shopify Flow, Shopify Admin, Judge.me, Klaviyo, Omnisend, Point of Sale and Shopify's native store credit, and names twenty interface languages while a feature bullet on the same page claims 180+ — the vendor's own FAQ (essential-apps.com/loyalty, read 19 Sep 2026) reconciles those two: the twenty are the languages the app's own interface ships in, and the 180+ covers translating the storefront-facing text into any language you sell in. Nothing on the listing says what happens when a plan's order cap is passed; the same vendor FAQ does: you are upgraded in place to the next tier, there is no per-order overage fee, and $79 a month is the ceiling — unlimited loyalty orders, everything included. So the worst case for a store that outgrows Free is the $79 tier, not a surprise bill. The review record has moved: 482 reviews at 5.0, up from 438 in August, distributed 473 five-star, 8 four-star, none at three or two, and 1 one-star. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Essential Loyalty?

Two things to read closely before you pay. The meter is honest — loyalty-influenced orders, not all orders — and that is genuinely in your favour, but it also means you cannot work out your tier from your order count. A store doing 3,000 orders a month with little repeat business may sit on Free; one doing 800 with a loyal base may not. Measure your repeat and referral orders for a month before you choose. The second is an oddity on the listing itself. The free plan advertises an 'Advanced loyalty point program' while Starter at $10 advertises a 'Free loyalty point program', which read literally means the paid tier offers less on that line. It is almost certainly a labelling slip rather than a real downgrade, but it is the kind of line worth confirming with support before you upgrade for it.

Evey Events

Is Evey Events worth it?

Evey Events is genuinely best for Shopify stores that sell tickets alongside products and want attendees, orders and customer data in one place instead of reconciling a separate ticketing platform against the shop. Skip it if ticketing is your actual business rather than a sideline -- a dedicated platform gives you seating, promoter tools and box-office features that a Shopify app is not trying to match -- or you sell so few tickets that any per-ticket fee is friction you don't need.

How much does Evey Events cost?

(re-verified 8 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/event-tickets; every figure unchanged since 1 September 2026) Four tiers, and every one of them charges twice: a monthly fee and a fee per ticket processed. Lite is free to install and takes $1.00 per ticket. Growth is $19 a month and $0.75. Standard, the tier the store marks Popular, is $49 and $0.50. Professional is $189 and $0.25. The paid tiers carry a 7-day free trial. Read that structure the right way round: the monthly fee is not what you are buying, it is what you pay to lower the per-ticket rate, so the correct plan follows from your ticket volume and nothing else. The crossings are exact. Lite and Growth cost the same at 76 tickets a month; below that Lite wins. Growth and Standard cross at 120. Standard and Professional cross at 560. So a store selling 300 tickets a month pays $199 on Standard against $244 on Growth and $264 on Professional -- the middle tier, and the store's own Popular label happens to be right for that range. One feature line changes that arithmetic and sits above the crossover: Collect fees on every ticket sold appears on Standard and Professional only, so passing the per-ticket cost to attendees is itself a paid feature. Beyond that, feature differences barely enter into it until Professional, which is where reserved seating, Klaviyo and Mailchimp integrations, the multi-vendor dashboard and priority support live. The app is published by Staytuned and carries a 4.4 rating from 320 reviews. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Evey Events?

Nobody gets caught by the monthly fee here; they get caught by the per-ticket one. On Lite the app is free to install and then takes a dollar off every ticket you sell, which is invisible until you sell volume and then is the largest line on the invoice. Work out your monthly ticket count before you install anything, because that single number picks your plan: under 76 stay on Lite, 76 to 120 move to Growth, 120 to 560 move to Standard, above that Professional. Getting this wrong is not a small error -- at 300 tickets a month the gap between the best and worst choice is about $65 every month.

Fast Bundle

Is Fast Bundle worth it?

Fast Bundle is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want every bundle and upsell format from one app — mix-and-match, build-your-own, BOGO, volume breaks, AI frequently-bought-together — priced against what those offers actually earn rather than a flat fee, and who are comfortable with an app that Shopify delisted for two weeks in July 2026 and then restored. Skip it if you need one bundle type only, where a single-purpose app costs less than the metered ladder; you sell in person, since Shopify POS support sits behind the $299 Enterprise tier; or an app in your path to checkout having been pulled and deactivated once, however well handled, is a risk you cannot carry.

How much does Fast Bundle cost?

(read 2026-08-24 on apps.shopify.com/fast-bundle-product-bundles, listed as “FBP | Fast Bundle & Upsell App”, and on fastbundle.co/pricing) The meter here is not your catalogue, your traffic or your seats — it is the revenue your bundles themselves generate. The listing is free to install and shows four tiers. Development stores are free to install and free to run. Standard (1K) is $19 a month or $180 a year and covers up to $1,000 of monthly bundle sales. Standard (3K) is $49 a month or $468 a year for up to $3,000. Standard (10K) is $139 a month or $1,380 a year for up to $10,000. All three paid tiers carry a 7-day free trial and the same feature list: unlimited bundles, upsells and cross-sells, mix and match, volume-discount upsell, BOGO and Buy X Get Y, unlimited AI frequently-bought-together, product add-ons, 24/7 English support and the AI bundle image generator. The App Store states all charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. The vendor's own pricing page adds a fifth tier the listing never shows: Enterprise at $299 a month or $2,988 a year, described as limitless monthly bundle revenue, with automatic bundle detection in the cart, Shopify POS integration, minor specialised customisations, priority onboarding with an account manager and a five-minute support target against Standard's thirty. That page also prices the annual commitments as effective monthly rates — $15, $39, $115 and $249 — under a “2-MONTHS FREE” label, and it is the only place the free plan is described in full: all six bundle types, 24/7 support, available to development stores and “eligible merchants”, and capped at $500 in bundle sales a month. Its comparison table shows what the free tier gives up: volume discounts and product add-ons on selected products only rather than collections or the whole catalogue, no AI frequently-bought-together across all products, no multilingual translation, no subscription-app integration, and a “Powered by Fast Bundle” credit left on your storefront. Fast Bundle's own FAQ defines the metered revenue as sales through bundles, volume discounts, product add-ons, mix and match, Buy X Get Y, frequently bought together and other offers created with the app, and states that exceeding your plan's monthly bundle revenue limit means upgrading to keep campaigns running. Developer Fast Bundle, listed at 13353 Commerce Parkway, Unit 2353, Richmond, BC, Canada; the app launched on 26 November 2020, the vendor's site claims 22,400 merchants, and the listing carried 3,031 reviews at a 5.0 average at the time of writing. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Fast Bundle?

The most important thing about this app is not on its App Store listing. On 17 July 2026 Fast Bundle detected what its own status page calls a security attack; Shopify removed the app from the App Store as a precaution and deactivated it on existing stores, so merchants found it simply gone. It was restored to limited visibility on 30 July and fully searchable again on 3 August, after Shopify reviewed an incident report and a third-party vulnerability and penetration test. The vendor states its investigation and testing found no indication that any customer, store or shopper data was accessed, exposed or leaked, and that 2,405 stores had reinstalled by early August. Shopify's own words, quoted on that page, are that the app “has been restored to limited visibility”. Nobody outside the process can verify what was reached, and neither the vendor nor Shopify has published the technical detail. What is verifiable is the shape of the disruption: a storefront-facing app pulled without warning, deactivated on live stores, and roughly two weeks coming back. If your bundles carry your average order value, that is the risk you are underwriting — not because it is likely to recur, but because it has happened once and the app sits in the path to checkout. The review record needs reading with that date in mind. 5.0 from 3,031 reviews is exceptional, and the breakdown is 3,000 at five stars against 19 at one. But most of that history predates July 2026, and Shopify app ratings skew high because merchants are prompted for them. What an average cannot tell you is how a vendor handles an incident, and on that the status page is the better evidence: dated, specific, quoting Shopify directly, and correcting its own earlier estimates in public. That is a good sign about communication rather than about security. One practical hazard came out of the outage and has not gone away. While the app was delisted, other apps renamed themselves to include “Fast Bundle” — the vendor names Fast Bundle Offer, BOGO, BYOB; Sparrow Fast Bundle Upsell App; and Rabbit Fast Bundle & Upsell — and Shopify subsequently delisted three of them. Searching the App Store for the name is therefore not a reliable way to find this app. Install from the listing slug, fast-bundle-product-bundles, and check that the developer reads Fast Bundle. Finally, the listing's data grant is broad even for this category: it edits customers and customer tags, products, inventory and collections, orders including third-party fulfilment and order edits, discount codes and promotions, Shopify Functions cart transforms, the checkout page and Online Store pages. Cart transforms are how a bundle becomes a single line item, so the scope is explicable, but an app with write access to your discounts and your checkout page belongs in your processing register and in whatever review you run after an incident like July's.

Feedvisor

Is Feedvisor worth it?

Feedvisor is genuinely best for mid-market and enterprise Amazon sellers with large catalogs where algorithmic repricing and ad optimization move real revenue. Skip it if you're a small seller (rule-based repricers cost a tenth), or your margins are set by factors repricing can't touch.

How much does Feedvisor cost?

Feedvisor publishes no price, and we checked that again on 2026-09-03. feedvisor.com/pricing returns a 404. Their own llms.txt lists every public page and contains no pricing page and no amount. The plan comparison at feedvisor.com/plans does publish a tier structure — Professional, Premium and Enterprise for price optimisation, Feedvisor and Feedvisor Plus for advertising, and a single Enterprise tier for brand optimisation — but every column ends in Request Demo rather than a figure. One correction to what we wrote before: the sentence we attributed to Feedvisor, that pricing is hybrid and varies with catalogue size, ad spend and complexity, is no longer anywhere on their site. The platform has been rebranded to Agentis and that wording went with it, so we no longer put those words in their mouth. Every figure you will read elsewhere, including the roughly $100 a month entry tier and the roughly $1,500 a month for the full platform that we carried before, comes from third parties or from sales conversations rather than from Feedvisor. Treat those as indicative only, and expect a sales call. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Feedvisor?

The honest structure: the $100 tier is a limited on-ramp, and most of what Feedvisor is famous for (the algorithmic Buy-Box strategy that holds prices UP, ad management, analysts) lives behind the $1,500+ top tier — this is enterprise software for serious catalogs, priced accordingly. If your Amazon revenue can't absorb that as a small percentage, simpler repricers are the rational choice.

Feedyio

Is Feedyio worth it?

Feedyio is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who need several feeds at once, in formats they control — custom XML, CSV, TXT or JSON built from their own template — and especially those selling into Central and Eastern European marketplaces and price-comparison sites, with a catalogue that fits inside a published tier. Skip it if you need one Google Shopping feed and nothing else, where the older and far more widely reviewed feed apps cover the same ground; or your catalogue runs past 65,000 products, which is where the published ladder ends.

How much does Feedyio cost?

(read 2026-09-10 on apps.shopify.com/product-feed-10 and feedyio.com/pricing) Nine published tiers, billed in USD every 30 days through Shopify. The Shopify listing shows only the first four. Free is permanent and covers up to 30 products or 100 variants, one feed, the primary market only, a daily product update and email support. Basic at $9.99 a month raises that to 1,000 products or 2,000 variants, up to five feeds, hourly product updates and the named comparison-shopping integrations (Heureka, Favi and similar), still on the primary market and language only. Advanced at $19.99 covers 2,500 products or 5,000 variants, up to ten feeds, and all markets and languages. Pro at $29.99 covers 6,000 products or 12,000 variants and up to 30 feeds. The listing stops there and says additional plans are available; the vendor's own pricing page prices them: Enterprise $39.99 (10,000 products / 20,000 variants / 40 feeds), Enterprise Plus $59.99 (20,000 / 40,000 / 40), Enterprise Plus 2 $89.99 (30,000 / 60,000 / 40), Enterprise Plus 3 $99.99 (50,000 / 100,000 / 40) and Enterprise Plus 4 $119.99 (65,000 / 130,000 / 40). Every paid tier has a 7-day free trial. One inconsistency on that page: the line under the table says every paid plan unlocks Shopify markets, translations and inventory levels, while the Basic card above it lists the primary market and primary language only — the Shopify listing agrees with the card, so confirm before buying Basic for a second market. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Feedyio?

Two gates decide your bill and neither is about how much value the feeds create. The first is catalogue size: the ladder counts products and variants, and it runs further than the Shopify listing suggests — the listing stops at Pro ($29.99, 6,000 products) and says additional plans are available, while the vendor's own pricing page publishes five more tiers up to $119.99 for 65,000 products. The second is freshness: the free tier updates products once a day and hourly updates start at $9.99, which matters when stock moves faster than a day. Multi-market and multi-language feeds only appear at $19.99. The app is also younger and smaller than the shelf leaders: launched 16 May 2022 by happyapps.cz in Prague, with 115 reviews against thousands for the established Google Shopping feed apps. And the standout integrations — Heureka, Zboží.cz, Árukereső, Glami, Favi, Kaufland — are Central and Eastern European channels; that is the app's real edge, but it is not an edge if you only sell through Google and Meta.

Flocksy

Is Flocksy worth it?

Flocksy is genuinely best for marketing teams and agencies with steady, recurring creative volume (ads, social, video edits) that want predictable flat-fee capacity instead of freelancer wrangling. Skip it if your design needs are occasional or spiky (pay per project instead), or you need one senior specialist deeply embedded in your brand.

How much does Flocksy cost?

Flat monthly plans priced by dedicated creative hours per business day: $1,199/mo for 2h/day, $1,699 (3h/day), $2,199 (4h/day), $2,599 (5h/day), $2,999 (6h/day), $3,399 (7h/day) and $3,799/mo for 8h/day, each billed annually and shown per month (re-verified 2026-09-03; every annual rate unchanged since 6 August, and the monthly and quarterly ladders are now published beside them at $1,699 to $5,899 a month). Plans start at 2 daily hours and scale to 8, with custom teams beyond that; month-to-month costs more — on the 4h/day plan Flocksy prices annual billing as saving $10,800/yr versus monthly. The pricing page carries a money-back guarantee. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Flocksy?

'Unlimited' means unlimited queue, not unlimited throughput: work happens at your plan's daily capacity, so a big launch week still needs planning, and turnaround expectations are where subscription-design relationships sour. The economics are simple and honest — against even one freelance designer's day rate, the math works IF you feed it steady volume; if your design needs are sporadic, a flat monthly fee is paying for silence — unused hours do bank, but only for 30 days.

folk

Is folk worth it?

folk is genuinely best for small sales teams, agencies and VC/partnership teams who want a clean, fast-to-set-up CRM with a great LinkedIn enrichment extension. Skip it if you need real multi-step workflow automation and reporting, or you are on Standard and want Zapier, Make or the REST API — folk keeps those for Premium and up, and is lightweight by design.

How much does folk cost?

$30/member/month on Standard, $60 on Premium and from $100 on Enterprise when billed monthly; billed yearly those drop to $24, $48 and from $80 per member per month — 20% off — for $288, $576 and $960 per member per year (re-verified 2026-09-03; every figure held). The same page publishes euro rates: 27€, 54€ and from 83€ monthly, 22€, 43€ and from 67€ yearly, for 259€, 518€ and 804€ a year. The free trial is two weeks and needs no credit card; folk's own FAQ says an account that does not upgrade is blocked rather than deleted at the end, and that the trial can be extended by a week on request. The published caps: email enrichment 500 a month on Standard, 1,000 on Premium and custom on Enterprise; AI magic fields 2,000 and 5,000; account sync one per member and five per member. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with folk?

One gap has closed and one has narrowed. folk now has a mobile app — the pricing table carries a Mobile app row ticked on all three plans — so the browser-only complaint is out of date. Automation is still uneven, but the picture moved in September: Zapier and Make stay Premium and Enterprise only, and so does the REST API, yet the table now carries an MCP row ticked on all three plans. Standard therefore does have a programmatic route — through an AI client rather than a workflow builder — and no plan shows a native multi-step workflow. Enrichment is capped at 500 a month on Standard and 1,000 on Premium, and email sequences need at least Premium.

Frase

Is Frase worth it?

Frase is genuinely best for content teams and SEOs who want to speed up research, briefs and SERP-driven optimization in one workflow. Skip it if you publish only occasionally — the monthly quota and subscription outweigh the time saved for a handful of articles.

How much does Frase cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-14 against Frase's own machine-readable pricing file frase.io/pricing.md; every figure below was unchanged from our 17 August reading) The headline figure is the yearly rate; paying month to month costs about 25% more, and both are shown on the page. Starter $39/mo billed yearly against $49/mo monthly: 1 seat, 1 site, 10 articles and 50 audit pages a month, Content Guard watching 10 pages. Professional $103/mo yearly against $129/mo monthly: 3 seats, 5 sites, 40 articles and 250 audit pages, extra seats $29/mo. Scale $239/mo yearly against $299/mo monthly: 5 seats, up to 10 domains, 100 articles and 1,000 audit pages, Content Guard watching 300 pages, extra seats $29/mo. The trial is 7 days with no credit card. FraseCMS hosting is included free up to 100,000 page views a month; moving the blog to your own domain is $19/mo on top of a paid plan, or $99/mo at a million page views. On Starter, Frase stops at the limit rather than billing you extra; on Professional and Scale you can switch on pay-as-you-go capacity, so there the sticker price is a floor rather than a ceiling. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Frase?

The article quotas pinch if you publish at volume (overage docs bill each), and it's a research-and-optimization tool, not a magic ranking button — it speeds up briefs, it doesn't replace the writing or the backlinks.

FullEnrich

Is FullEnrich worth it?

FullEnrich is genuinely best for outbound teams that need maximum find-rates on emails and especially mobile numbers, and prefer paying only for verified hits. Skip it if you only need emails at volume (single-source tools are cheaper per hit), or your ICP data lives fine in one database already.

How much does FullEnrich cost?

(slider re-read 1 Sep 2026 on fullenrich.com/pricing from a Dutch exit; the USD amounts are the 26 Aug 2026 US reading, unchanged in structure) Pro is priced off a credit slider rather than a fixed tier: $55/mo at 1,000 credits a month, printed as $0.055 per credit, and $720/mo at 15,000 -- $0.048 each, so the rate drops as you commit to more. The slider runs from 500 credits to over 100,000. Enterprise is quoted. The free trial is 50 credits with no credit card, and inviting team members earns more. What a credit buys is the part worth reading and it did not change: one work email costs 1 credit, a personal email 3, a reverse email lookup 1, and a mobile number 10, so a list that needs phone numbers burns through ten times faster than the headline suggests. Credits roll over three months on monthly billing and twelve on annual. One caution for anyone checking these numbers from outside the US: the page localises. From the Netherlands the slider prints 0.055 euro per credit while the recommended-plan card on the same page still prints $720/mo, and the page structured data declares USD with a 0 to 500 range. Read the currency next to the number before comparing. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with FullEnrich?

The pay-on-success model is refreshingly honest, but note the 10x: phone numbers eat credits ten times faster than emails, so a calling-heavy motion consumes budget quickly — model your email/phone mix. As an orchestration layer over 15+ providers, its hit rate genuinely beats single databases; the flip side is you're paying a premium per contact versus querying one source that might have sufficed.

Gelato

Is Gelato worth it?

Gelato is genuinely best for creators and stores selling custom products internationally who want local production in many countries to cut shipping time and cost, with no inventory. Skip it if you sell only a handful of orders a month (stay on the free plan) or your customers are concentrated in one country where a single-hub competitor is simpler.

How much does Gelato cost?

(re-read 2026-09-03 on gelato.com/subscription-plans in a browser session, every figure unchanged since 26 August; the site serves a bot challenge that our capture cannot pass, so there is no dated screenshot beside this) Free is $0 forever with two connected stores and two account users. Gelato+ is $29.99 a month, or $19.99 a month billed annually, and lifts both of those to unlimited while adding Personalization Studio, the AI tools and up to 33% off products year-round. Platinum is quoted, with custom discounts, a rewards programme and a dedicated implementation service. Note where those figures live: gelato.com/pricing publishes no subscription rates at all — it explains how payment works, with no upfront fees and no commission — and the plan table sits on /subscription-plans. The rates are in dollars even read from Europe. Gelato+ pays for itself on product discounts rather than features, so the question is order volume, not which tools you want. What is the catch with Gelato?

GeoStock

Is GeoStock worth it?

GeoStock is genuinely best for retailers with physical locations who want shoppers to see per-store stock and find the nearest branch on the product page itself. Skip it if you are online-only — there are no locations to show — or you need actual inventory management, which this is not.

How much does GeoStock cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-20 on apps.shopify.com/product-inventory-information) Two plans, no free tier. Base Plan $9.99 a month and Plus Plan $29.99 a month, both with a 14-day free trial, billed in USD every 30 days. Unchanged since the readings of 18 August and 13 September 2026. Rating 4.9 from 99 ratings (92 five-star, two four-star, no three-star, two two-star, three one-star). Developer sohkal llc, 6381 Almaden Rd, San Jose, CA, US; on the App Store since 28 March 2019. What is the catch with GeoStock?

Know what this is before you buy it: despite the name it is a storefront widget, not an inventory system. It displays the stock you already track in Shopify per location, and adds a store-locator map — it does not manage, forecast or reconcile anything. If you came looking for multi-location inventory management, that is a different category and a different budget. What it does do well is close a specific gap: a shopper who can see that a nearby store has the item is a shopper who does not abandon.

Geotargetly

Is Geotargetly worth it?

Geotargetly is genuinely best for marketers personalizing redirects, content blocks and popups by visitor location — country to city level — without engineering work. Skip it if your traffic is small enough for a hand-built redirect, or your CDN/edge stack already covers the basic geo-cases you need.

How much does Geotargetly cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-20 on their own pricing page, from a European exit) 14-day free trial, no card. Six tiers: Dev $12/mo, Startup $24, Growth $49, Business $99, High Traffic $199, Enterprise from $349 — billed yearly $9, $19, $39, $79, $159 and from $279. The digits are unchanged since 31 August. CURRENCY: Geotargetly prices the same digits in more than one currency, so the symbol you see depends on where you are. Reading the page from Europe on 19 September returned these figures with a dollar sign; reading it from the same exit on 20 September returned the identical figures with a euro sign — €12, €24, €49, €99, €199 and from €349 monthly, €9 to €279 billed yearly. The numbers did not move, only the symbol did. We quote the dollar list here because that is the currency the rest of this page's figures were read in, but a European buyer should expect to be billed the same number in euros, which is not the same amount of money — do not convert one into the other. IMPORTANT: on 19 September the page was running a live 50/50 price split test on visitors from 32 countries (US, UK, CA, AU, NZ and 27 EU states), assigned by a 30-day cookie; the alternative set is about 20% higher — $14, $29, $59, $119, $239 and from $419. The amounts above are the lower, control set, which is also what visitors outside those 32 countries see; a fresh session on 20 September landed in that same control set. The page's own price table additionally enumerates an eight-step Enterprise ladder the plan card does not show: $349, $429, $519, $599, $699, $869, $1,299 and $1,739 monthly, $279 to $1,391 as yearly monthly-equivalents, with annual totals $3,350 to $16,694. Standard annual totals are $108, $230, $470, $950 and $1,910 — two dollars above twelve times the advertised monthly-equivalent on all but Dev. That table did not render on the 20 September reading, which served only the six plan cards, so those ladder and annual-total figures still carry their 19 September date. All plans include country, state and city-level targeting on unlimited domains. The meter is PAGEVIEWS, not visitors: a pageview is consumed for every page visit, and separately for each product in use; Geo Links consumes one on link click only. No refunds, and quota does not roll over to the next billing cycle. On quota exhaustion you get 2 days to upgrade or re-subscribe before services stop, with email alerts at 30%, 10%, 5% and 0%. Per-tier pageview quotas are still NOT reliably readable: the page shows one quota figure (500,000 monthly, 6,000,000 yearly) for the whole ladder at once, which cannot be right for six tiers. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Geotargetly?

The meter is pageviews, not visitors, and each product consumes its own pageview on the same page visit — so a redirect plus a popup bills twice. Run out and you get two days to upgrade or re-subscribe before services stop. The friendlier advertised numbers are the yearly rates; month-to-month runs about 25% higher. And the dependency worth pricing in: the rules run from a script you drop into your site, so they exist only while that script is served. Stop the subscription and every visitor sees the same page again, wherever they are.

GetResponse

Is GetResponse worth it?

GetResponse is genuinely best for small businesses that want email plus landing pages, automation and webinars in one affordable suite. Skip it if you only need basic broadcasts — a leaner tool costs less without the extra modules you won't use.

How much does GetResponse cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-14 on their own pricing page, in euros, quoted at 1,000 contacts) Starter €16/mo or €13.12/mo billed annually: 1 automation workflow, up to 3 users. Marketer €54/mo or €44.28 annual: unlimited workflows, ecommerce tools, advanced segmentation, abandoned-cart recovery. Creator €62/mo or €50.84 annual: website builder, course creator up to 500 students, webinars. Enterprise is quote-only and adds SMS, a dedicated IP and sending domain, SSO and unlimited users. Annual billing saves a stated 18%, and prices step up at 1k, 2.5k, 5k, 10k, 25k, 50k and 100k contacts. What changed since our August 2026 reading is the free tier: the pricing page no longer sells one. It opens with a 14-day trial that needs no card, and nine fresh loads on 14 September 2026 each showed the same four plan cards with no free option among them. Free accounts have not been withdrawn altogether — the FAQ on that same page still describes a Free account that keeps working once the trial lapses, with limits on webinars, messages, landing pages, marketing automation and chats — but it is no longer a tier you can pick from the grid, so treat it as what the trial decays into rather than as a plan. One currency warning survives unchanged: that same FAQ quotes the entry plan at $19 a month for 1,000 subscribers while the plan grid served us euros, so check which currency your own checkout uses before you budget. Charities and NGOs are offered 50% off every monthly plan. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with GetResponse?

Priced by contact count, so the entry number climbs as your list grows, and the best value only shows on long (annual/24-month) commitments. A solid all-rounder, but you lock in to get the good rate.

GrapeLeads

Is GrapeLeads worth it?

GrapeLeads is genuinely best for web developers, designers and agencies prospecting local businesses that do not have a website yet — surfaced from Google Maps with contact details. Skip it if you sell to companies that already have an online presence, or you want transparent pricing before creating an account.

How much does GrapeLeads cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-12, read on their own buy-credits page; every amount unchanged since 12 August) Pay-as-you-go credit packs, bought once rather than subscribed to: Freelancer $28 for 50 credits ($0.56 each), Startup $55 for 100 credits ($0.54) and Agency $127 for 250 credits ($0.51). Bulk pricing is on request and signing up gives 20 free credits. Credits measure work, not leads: one credit starts a search and one more is charged for every filtered result, so a search that returns 20 matching businesses costs 21 credits. The vendor also states that unused credits carry a 50% bonus when its 2.0 app ships. Mind the URL — the price list lives at /buy-credits/ while the /pricing link 404s, which is how we had this down as unpriced until now. One rounding note: the page prints $0.54 per credit for the Startup pack, but $55 for 100 credits is $0.55 — their own figure is a cent optimistic. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with GrapeLeads?

You are billed per result, not per usable lead: one credit opens the search and one more is charged for every business it returns, so a broad filter burns credits whether or not the results are worth calling. The packs are small enough that this is cheap to test ($28 for 50 credits) but it is the wrong shape if you want volume prospecting at a predictable monthly cost — there is no subscription at all. The site also still 404s its own /pricing link while the real list sits at /buy-credits/, which is an odd look for a tool sold to web professionals. And the niche (Google-Maps businesses without websites) is the real product: judge the data on one pack before you go further.

Grapevine

Is Grapevine worth it?

Grapevine is genuinely best for Shopify stores running more than one marketing channel that want attribution from customers rather than from cookies — post-purchase 'how did you hear about us', NPS and CSAT — with unlimited responses at a predictable flat price, and that already send data into Klaviyo, GA4 or Shopify Flow. Skip it if your order volume is small enough that $25 a month buys a handful of answers; you want a single one-off survey rather than a running programme; or you need a permanently free tier, because the only free access here is the 14-day trial.

How much does Grapevine cost?

(read 2026-09-10 on apps.shopify.com/grapevine) One plan, called Complete, at $25 a month, billed in USD every 30 days, with a 14-day free trial and no free tier. The single price also covers revenue and AOV reporting per marketing channel, targeting by order value, product, country, payment method and customer, delivery on-site, by email and on Shopify POS, exports to Shopify Flow, Klaviyo and GA4, and querying your survey data with your own AI assistant through the vendor's MCP server. What is the catch with Grapevine?

The flat price is the whole pricing page, which cuts both ways. There is no free tier and no small plan, so from day fifteen the app costs $25 a month whether it collects four responses or forty thousand — a low-volume store pays the same as a high-volume one, and several of the nearest alternatives do publish a free plan. The second thing to weigh is access rather than price: the listing's data section asks for customer data including sensitive, device and activity data, plus orders, staff accounts and the online store, which is a lot of reach for a survey tool and worth reading the privacy policy over. The evidence base is otherwise good for a Shopify app — launched 17 August 2017 by Union Works Apps in London, and 222 reviews on 10 September 2026 of which 215 are five-star and none below four.

Hello Bar

Is Hello Bar worth it?

Hello Bar is genuinely best for content sites, blogs and stores that already have traffic and a genuinely worthwhile offer, and want sticky bars, popups and slide-ins with A/B testing to convert more of that traffic into subscribers. Skip it if your traffic is still small (fix distribution first — a popup on 200 visitors captures almost nothing), or your list-building runs through gated content and landing pages rather than on-page interrupts.

How much does Hello Bar cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-03 against hellobar.com/pricing) Hello Bar publishes exact prices, so the ranges we carried before were wrong: they were the monthly and the annual rate side by side. Paid tiers meter monthly popup VIEWS. Growth is $39 a month billed monthly or $29 billed annually, up to 50,000 views a month; Premium $69 or $49, up to 150,000; Elite $129 or $99, up to 500,000, with unlimited seats. The annual feature table states the same quotas as 600,000, 1.8 million and 6 million views a year. Starter is $0 forever with 5,000 views in total rather than per month. The view limit applies per website, and only a custom agency or enterprise plan can move it to a per-account basis. No credit card is needed to start, and first-time customers on an annual plan get a 30-day money-back guarantee. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Hello Bar?

The meter is views, not results: every visitor who sees a popup counts against your quota, so a traffic spike raises the bill regardless of how many emails you actually captured — a busy site outgrows the entry tier fast. And the honest fundamental of every popup tool: it amplifies an offer, it doesn't create one. A weak lead magnet with a beautiful popup is still a weak lead magnet, and aggressive full-screen takeovers can cost more goodwill (and Core Web Vitals) than they capture.

HubSpot

Is HubSpot worth it?

HubSpot is genuinely best for teams that want marketing, sales, service and content on one contact database and will actually use more than one hub — that shared database is the real product, and it is what makes the price defensible when you use the breadth. Skip it if you need one job done well and cheaply, because a dedicated tool will almost always beat the equivalent HubSpot hub on price; or your contact list is growing fast and your budget is not, since contacts are the meter that moves without you touching anything.

How much does HubSpot cost?

(2026-08-18, read in a live browser on their own marketing pricing page, USD view) Free is $0 for up to 2 users and 1,000 marketing contacts, with no time limit. Starter is advertised at $7 per seat a month against a list price of $20 per seat a month, under a banner reading “Save up to 65% on Starter — new customers only, select offers available for a limited time”. It includes 500 HubSpot Credits and 1,000 marketing contacts. Professional starts at $800 a month paid annually, or $890 a month billed monthly, and includes 3 Core Seats with additional Core Seats from $45 a month, 3,000 credits and 2,000 marketing contacts. On top of that comes a required one-time Professional Onboarding fee of $3,000 that the headline price does not include. Enterprise starts at $3,600 a month with 5 Core Seats, extra seats from $75, 5,000 credits and 10,000 marketing contacts, and a required one-time onboarding fee of $7,000. HubSpot AEO, their answer-engine visibility tracker, is sold separately at $50 a month or $45 annually for 25 prompts across 3 engines, with a 28-day trial. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with HubSpot?

Three numbers on this pricing page are not what they look like, and they compound. The first is the $7. It is the number in large black type on the Starter card, and the $20 beside it in small grey type is the list price. The banner above the table explains why: up to 65% off Starter, new customers only, for a limited time. So $7 is an introductory rate and $20 is what the seat costs afterwards — a 186% step for a system that by then holds your contact database, which is the single most painful kind of software to leave. The second is the $800. Professional carries a required one-time onboarding fee of $3,000, disclosed in a footnote under the card rather than in the price. Year one on Professional is therefore $800 × 12 + $3,000 = $12,600 if you pay annually, or $890 × 12 + $3,000 = $13,680 month to month. The onboarding adds roughly a third to the first year, and no amount of shopping around removes it — it is mandatory. Enterprise does the same thing at $7,000 on top of $43,200 a year. The third is the seat count, because it is not the meter that usually bites. Professional includes 3 Core Seats and 2,000 marketing contacts. For a marketing platform, contacts are the axis that grows on its own: your list gets bigger whether or not you hire anyone, and the contact tier moves the bill without anyone deciding to upgrade. Price your next two years on the list you expect to have, not the team you have now. One more thing worth knowing before you start on Free. The free tier is genuinely usable — two users, 1,000 contacts, no expiry — and that is exactly how the ladder is designed to work. The step from Starter to Professional is not incremental: at list prices a three-seat team goes from $60 a month to $890 plus $3,000 once, which is roughly fifteen times the monthly cost. Whatever you build on Free, build it knowing where the next rung is.

Iconosquare

Is Iconosquare worth it?

Iconosquare is genuinely best for agencies and brands that want deep social analytics, reporting and competitor benchmarking alongside scheduling, especially Instagram-first teams. Skip it if you need a heavy-duty publishing workhorse across many niche platforms, or a single free native analytics view already answers your questions.

How much does Iconosquare cost?

(price re-verified 2026-09-15) Read on iconosquare.com/pricing from a Netherlands connection, at the profile count each plan includes. Free covers 2 social profiles, 1 user and 10 posts a month per profile, with one month of analytics history. Starter is €9 a month billed yearly, or €11 month to month, for 3 profiles, 1 user and 30 posts a month. Launch is €33 billed yearly (€39 monthly) for 5 profiles, 1 user and 100 posts. Scale is €69 billed yearly (€83 monthly) and is the first tier with 3 users, unlimited posts, one group and two years of history. Custom starts at €116 billed yearly and covers 5 to unlimited profiles and 1 to unlimited users, with white-label reporting, API access and a dedicated CSM. The page states the yearly saving as €24, €72, €168 and €276 a year. The ladder has changed since our 26 August reading over a US connection, which listed Launch $39, Scale $79 and an Excel tier at $139: Excel no longer appears as a named plan, its price and its white-label, API and CSM features now sit under Custom, and Starter is new below Launch. The profile count is the dial that moves the price, so a quote taken at five says little about what a team managing thirty will pay — and the tiers differ in users, posts and history, not just in profile allowance. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Iconosquare?

Its depth is strongest on Instagram and the core networks; if your priority platform sits outside its best-supported set, coverage thins. Analytics is where it shines — scheduling and community features exist but aren't always as deep as dedicated publishers. And the per-seat, per-profile tiering means agencies managing many brands climb toward the Custom plan quicker than the headline Starter price suggests: Starter and Launch carry one seat, Scale three, and only Custom lifts the five-profile ceiling.

Is iContact worth it?

How much does iContact cost?

InboxAlly

Is InboxAlly worth it?

InboxAlly is genuinely best for serious senders — email marketers and cold-outreach teams — whose deliverability problems are costing measurable revenue and who need active reputation repair. Skip it if you're a small sender who just needs basic list hygiene (cheaper warm-up tools suffice), or your inbox issues stem from content and list quality you haven't fixed.

How much does InboxAlly cost?

(price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page, read from a European exit) Every amount unchanged and confirmed on the plan comparison table, which states 'Pricing in USD, billed monthly': Starter $149/mo (100 seed emails/day, 1 sender profile), Plus $645/mo (500/day, 5 profiles), Premium $1,190/mo (1,000/day, 10 profiles), Enterprise custom (custom volume, unlimited profiles, dedicated deliverability experts). 10-day free trial, no card. No annual billing option is offered. Premium's sessions, more precisely than the previous dossier: a 1-hour setup/strategy session plus weekly 30-minute progress reviews. VENDOR SELF-CONTRADICTION, confirm before relying: the tier cards give Starter 'Email support' and reserve live chat for Plus and above, while the comparison table lower on the same page ticks 'Live chat support' and 'Dedicated CSM' for all four tiers including Starter. Phone & Zoom support, the setup session and the weekly reviews are consistently Premium-and-above in both places. What is the catch with InboxAlly?
