Influencer Hero

Is Influencer Hero worth it?

Influencer Hero is genuinely best for brands running influencer marketing as a continuous programme rather than a campaign, with enough volume to use 1,000 reach-outs a month from the first month, who want discovery, outreach, a creator CRM, UGC tracking and affiliate management in one place instead of a spreadsheet plus four tools. Skip it if you want to test the channel before committing, because the three-month minimum makes the real entry price $1,557 rather than $519; you are a two-person team on Standard's single seat; or you pay creators at any scale, since 20 payouts a month is the cap until you reach $839.

How much does Influencer Hero cost?

(pricing matrix read 18 September 2026 in documentation the vendor sent us; the public ladder at influencer-hero.com/pricing was read the same week and shows the quarterly column) Four plans, and the figure you see depends entirely on the billing term you pick. Billed monthly: Standard $649, Pro $1,049, Business $2,490. Billed quarterly: $519, $839 and $1,992 — and this is the column the public pricing page leads with, which is why $519 is the number most people quote. Billed annually: $454, $734 and $1,743. The advertised 20% and 30% savings check out exactly against the monthly rate ($649 × 0.8 = $519.20, × 0.7 = $454.30), so the discounts are real and the headline is simply the discounted one. What each plan carries: Standard is one seat, 1,000 reach-outs a month and 20 influencer payouts. Pro is three seats, 5,000 reach-outs and 200 payouts. Business is eight seats, 10,000 reach-outs and 500 payouts — the pricing page contradicts itself here. The Business plan card lists unlimited influencer payouts, but the Compare all features grid further down the same page reads 20, 200, 500 and Unlimited across Standard, Pro, Business and Enterprise on the row Number of influencer payouts, which puts Business at 500 and matches the figure in the documentation the vendor sent us. Read in a browser on 19 September 2026. Two of the three readings say 500, so that is the number to plan for, and it is worth having in writing. Enterprise is custom on every axis. Every plan carries a three-month minimum term and there is no free trial, so the smallest real commitment is three months of Standard: $1,947 billed monthly, or $1,557 if you take the quarterly rate. The influencer CRM, the outreach automation and the UGC tracking are in every plan; the ladder is gated on quota and seats. Influencer payouts run through bank debit at 0.1% to 0.4%, against the 2-3% that card processors typically charge. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Influencer Hero?

The three-month minimum is the real commitment, and there is no free trial to soften it. Every plan carries it, so the smallest honest entry price is not $519 but three months — $1,557 on the quarterly rate, $1,947 if you pay monthly. An influencer programme takes longer than four weeks to show you anything, so the vendor is not being unreasonable; it just means the decision is a quarter of spending rather than a month of trying. Read which column you are quoted. The public pricing page leads with the quarterly rate, so $519 is what gets repeated — but billed monthly the same plan is $649, a quarter more. Pro is $839 or $1,049, Business $1,992 or $2,490. The 20% and 30% savings are genuine and check out exactly against the monthly rate; the trap is only that the advertised number already has the discount in it. What the ladder actually meters is worth understanding, because it is better than it looks. A reach-out counts once, at the moment you first contact a new influencer. Every follow-up, reply and ongoing conversation with that same creator after that is unlimited and never draws the quota down again — so the meter counts new relationships opened, not messages sent. Standard's 1,000 a month is therefore 1,000 new creators, which is a great many, and nurturing the ones who answer costs nothing. Hitting the cap gives you two routes and the vendor recommends one of them against its own short-term interest: buy a top-up, or move up a tier. Their own documentation says brands who top up once tend to keep doing it, so repeated top-ups erode the saving from staying low. No top-up rate is published anywhere, which is the one number still missing from an otherwise unusually open account. One inconsistency to check before you sign, and it sits on the vendor's own page. The Business plan card lists unlimited influencer payouts; the comparison grid lower down that same page reads 20, 200, 500 and Unlimited across the four plans, putting Business at 500 — which is also what the documentation the vendor sent us says. Read in a browser on 19 September 2026. Two of the three readings give 500, so plan for 500 rather than unlimited, and on a plan at $1,992 a month get it in writing before you sign. Seats follow the quota — one, three, eight — so a two-person team is pushed to Pro by headcount alone, whatever its volume.

Instapage

Is Instapage worth it?

Instapage is genuinely best for marketing teams running significant paid ad campaigns who need post-click optimisation — AdMap ad-to-page personalisation, A/B testing and heatmaps. Skip it if you run limited ad campaigns or want budget pricing — at $99+/mo it's overkill below real paid-traffic volume.

How much does Instapage cost?

(re-verified 4 Sep 2026) Instapage does publish plan prices; they are not on the URL we had recorded. instapage.com/en/pricing redirects to the homepage at instapage.com/lp, and the plan table sits at instapage.com/plans. Our 26 August reading landed on the redirect, found no figures and concluded that prices had been withdrawn; the figures below match the last published rates this dossier already held, so the more likely explanation is a moved page rather than a withdrawal. Three tiers sit there. Create is $99 a month month-to-month or $79 billed annually, for 15,000 unique monthly visitors. Optimize is $199 or $159 annually for 30,000 unique monthly visitors, with selectors for 50,000 and for a custom volume — the custom option defaults to 50,000 and hands you to sales. Convert is quote-only. Annual billing is advertised as 'save up to 20%', and every tier carries unlimited contacts. The 14-day free trial asks for a credit card and is capped at 2,500 unique monthly visitors; Instapage's own FAQ states that exceeding that cap ends the trial automatically and moves you onto the paid plan you selected. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Instapage?

It's premium-priced and only justified by serious ad spend — Create is $79 a month billed annually for 15,000 unique monthly visitors, and the price per thousand barely improves as you climb, so the higher tiers buy features rather than cheaper traffic. The 14-day trial needs a card and carries its own cap of 2,500 visitors; crossing it ends the trial and starts the paid plan by itself. And there's the ownership question the feature list does not raise: publishing to your own domain means pointing a CNAME at Instapage — their help centre carries a per-registrar guide for exactly that — so the page is served by them and lives as long as the subscription does. Their own docs add a second catch worth knowing before you standardise on it: “we lock domains under the first Instapage account that uses them”. Treat these pages as rented campaign infrastructure, not as part of your site, and keep the copy somewhere you control.

Intelis

Is Intelis worth it?

Intelis is genuinely best for Shopify stores with hundreds to a few thousand variants that genuinely compete on price on Google Shopping and want competitor monitoring and repricing handled automatically. Skip it if your catalogue is small, you do not compete primarily on price, or your variant count sits just above a tier boundary and would push you to the next rung for a handful of SKUs.

How much does Intelis cost?

(re-verified 8 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/ecoprice-analytics, intelis.ai/pricing and the Intelis homepage) Four tiers on the Shopify listing, priced by how many products or variants you track, each with a 14-day free trial. Basic $49 a month or $490 a year, a 17% saving: up to 100 products or variants, Google Shopping competitor monitoring, AI automatch for unlimited competitors, dynamic pricing, unlimited competitor URL tracking, reports, pricing history and chat support. Professional $179 a month or $1,790 a year: up to 1,000, adding variant tracking, sales analysis, live feed export, pricing strategy monitoring, an AI assistant and premium chat support. Premium $249 a month or $2,490 a year: up to 2,000, adding Shopify Markets support per market, Google Analytics integration and API access. Business $399 a month or $3,990 a year: up to 5,000, adding a custom labels feed for Google Merchant Center, MAP monitoring, a customised AI matching algorithm, pricing consultation, advanced analytics and A+ support. The vendor's own pages used to disagree with the listing above Premium -- on 21 August 2026 intelis.ai/pricing showed Business at $499 with a $4,990 annual rate and Enterprise at $849, while the homepage said $749. That is now resolved: on 8 September 2026 the pricing page and the homepage both show Business at $399 ($3,990 a year) and Enterprise at $749 ($7,490 a year) for up to 10,000 SKUs, matching the listing. The vendor's own pages count SKUs where the listing counts products or variants. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Intelis; the app launched 6 July 2021 and carries a 4.9 rating from 101 reviews. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Intelis?

The ladder counts variants, not products, and that is where stores get caught. A catalogue of forty garments in five sizes and three colours is six hundred variants, so a shop most people would call small lands on the $179 tier rather than the $49 one. Count your variants, not your line items, before you read the price. The vendor's own numbers above Premium used to contradict each other, and that is worth knowing mainly because it has been fixed. On 21 August 2026 the Shopify listing said Business was $399 while intelis.ai/pricing said $499 with a $4,990 annual rate, and the homepage and the pricing page gave Enterprise as $749 and $849. Re-read on 8 September 2026, all three pages agree: Business $399 ($3,990 a year), Enterprise $749 ($7,490) for up to 10,000 SKUs. If you are working from a comparison written earlier this year, check its figures against the listing. And automatic repricing is not a switch you leave alone. The matching is AI-driven across Google Shopping and competitor sites, and a mismatched listing quietly reprices the wrong product, while an unbounded rule set on a busy category is how a store races itself to the bottom. Set floor prices before you turn dynamic pricing on, and audit what the automatch decided in the first fortnight.

involve.me

Is involve.me worth it?

involve.me is genuinely best for marketers building interactive lead-gen — quizzes, calculators, assessments and payment funnels with built-in email sequences — who want a free tier to validate the concept first. Skip it if you just need a simple form (lighter tools do that free), or you don’t yet have the traffic to feed an interactive funnel.

How much does involve.me cost?

(re-verified 19 September 2026 on the public pricing page; the free plan's feature set was measured inside the product, because the plan cards still do not state it) There is a free plan, and this is what it actually gives: 2 live funnels, publishing on a daanV.involve.me subdomain (or one of ten alternatives such as quizzes.cx, forms.ac and calculators.cx), the AI funnel builder, and involve.me branding on every page. No team seats at all. The pricing FAQ does publish the number that decides when it runs out: a free account runs to 50 submissions or 500 visits a month, and if you reach that without upgrading your funnels lock until the next calendar month starts. Paid, per person per month, annual against monthly: Start $29 / $49 with 3 live funnels and 1 user, Grow $69 / $99 with 5 funnels and 2 users, Scale $139 / $199 with 25 funnels, 5 users, A/B testing and lead verification. Enterprise is from $499/mo on annual contracts only. In the app the same tiers are priced in euros — €29, €69, €139 — and the annual toggle says “save up to 41%” where the public page says 40%. Two meters that decide more than the funnel count does are still missing from the tier pages: funnel visits a month (10,000 / 25,000 / 100,000) and contacts collected a month (300 / 1,000 / 3,000); the AI-credit allowance (50 / 100 / 300) is on the public comparison table. Each is toppable: +5,000 visits €8.33, +200 contacts €8.33, +250 AI credits €7.50, +1 seat €7.50, +5 live funnels €7.50. Prices exclude EU VAT. Every tier is higher than at the 17 Jul 2026 reading, when Start was $19/mo annual and $29 month-to-month. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with involve.me?

The tier pages sell live funnels, but the meter that empties first is contacts. Start collects 300 contacts a month against 10,000 funnel visits — so a funnel converting at 3% hits the contact ceiling and the visit ceiling in the same week, and the next 200 contacts cost €8.33 on top. Those two meters appear only in the in-app comparison table; the public table publishes the AI-credit allowance but not visits or contacts. The free plan is documented in exactly one place, and not where you would look for it: the pricing FAQ caps it at 50 submissions or 500 visits a month and warns that your funnels lock until the next calendar month if you hit that without upgrading, while the plan cards say nothing at all about what it includes. We measured that part — 2 live funnels, involve.me branding, no team seats — and you only learn it by hitting the wall, because a free account has no usage panel: “Plans & Billing” goes straight to the upgrade page. And the honest fundamental for any interactive-funnel tool: quizzes and calculators convert traffic you already have — they don't create it, so validate on the free plan before the subscription outruns the pipeline.

Is Kartra worth it?

Is Kit worth it?

How much does Kit cost?

Is Kite worth it?

What is the catch with Koongo?

The headline price is a base, not a bill. Each paid plan includes 1,000 items, 5 feeds, two marketplace wizards and 100 orders a month, and the listing says plainly that surcharges apply for extras used across all four of those dimensions. For a store with a real catalogue selling on several European marketplaces, every one of those limits is one you pass in week one. Price your own numbers on koongo.com's surcharge table before you take $39 seriously. The two pricing pages also do not quote the same bill. The App Store lists $39, $79 and $119 and bills in USD. koongo.com lists €35, €69 and €99 and states that all prices exclude VAT. Depending on where you trade and how you are registered, those are meaningfully different amounts for the same plan, and nothing on either page reconciles them. Then the record, which is the most useful thing on this listing. 4.4 from 98 reviews is the lowest average in this category among the apps Shopify shows beside it, and the breakdown explains why: 84 five-star ratings sit alongside six one-star ones. The critical reviews are specific rather than vague, which makes them worth reading in full. In July 2026 a Belgian merchant described a repricer set to Monitoring Mode that still blocked updates to live Bol offers because of MinimumPrice errors, so a delivery-promise change never reached the marketplace. In January 2026 a UK merchant described unresolved integration errors on OnBuy and a refused refund, with Koongo replying publicly that they had reached out several times without response. Neither is disqualifying on its own. Together they describe an app whose complexity is real and whose marketplace integrations sometimes need support to untangle — which is consistent with the vendor's own listing offering personal onboarding for complex setups. One more line to read before you install: the listing states the app views sensitive customer data as well as device and activity data, and can view and edit products, orders and custom data. Marketplace order sync needs customer details to work, so that is expected, but it makes this a processor of personal data on your behalf rather than a feed formatter.

Kumo

Is Kumo worth it?

Kumo is genuinely best for Shopify merchants on a standard plan who need wholesale prices for named customer groups, with CSV price lists and a registration form that someone approves, and who would rather not pay three times as much for a heavier wholesale app. Skip it if you are already on Shopify Plus, where company accounts and price lists come with the platform; or you want prices that react to competitors or to the market, because this sets fixed rules per customer group and nothing reads the outside world.

How much does Kumo cost?

(read 2026-09-16 on apps.shopify.com/b2b-wholesale-tools) Two plans and no free tier: B2B at $15 a month and PLUS at $30, both with a 7-day free trial, billed in USD every 30 days. B2B carries the whole working app — wholesale pricing, volume pricing, customer registration forms and the approval workflow — and pricing rules are unlimited rather than metered, so the ladder is not a volume ladder. PLUS adds exactly three things, and all three are Shopify Plus features: company registration, product catalog assignment and checkout integration. If you are not on Shopify Plus, the $30 tier has nothing to sell you. The app is Built for Shopify, launched on 21 November 2024, and shows 5.0 stars over 9 reviews. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Kumo?

Five stars over nine reviews is not a track record, and the age makes that worse rather than better. The app launched on 21 November 2024, so it has had close to two years on the App Store to collect them. Nine reviews in that window is a small installed base, and a small installed base is what decides whether an app is still maintained in 2028 — the rating tells you the nine are happy, not that the app is safe to build a wholesale channel on. The second plan is a trap for anyone who reads the ladder as a feature ladder. PLUS costs twice B2B and the three things it adds — company registration, catalog assignment, checkout integration — are all labelled Shopify Plus on the listing itself. On a standard Shopify plan the extra $15 a month buys nothing you can switch on.

Is Landingi worth it?

Is LangShop worth it?

Skip it if you sell in one language; or your translations must land in metafields without checking, which is precisely what the recent one-star reviews say is unreliable; or your catalogue is large enough that the tier you need is one of the unlisted ones — check langshop.app/pricing rather than the Shopify listing before you budget.

How much does LangShop cost?

(read 2026-09-10 on apps.shopify.com/langshop and langshop.app/pricing) Seven published tiers, billed in USD. The Shopify listing shows only the first four and links to 'more pricing plans'; the vendor's own pricing page prices the rest. Free costs nothing and covers one language and 50 products, with limited manual and AI translation, the standard language and currency switcher and multilingual SEO. Basic is $10 a month or $100 a year, and raises that to 250 products with five glossary rules, unlimited editing of translations, bulk editing and removal of LangShop branding. Standard is $40 a month or $400 a year: three languages, 2,000 products, 100 glossary rules, automatic sync of 50 new items, and the point at which the named engines (OpenAI, DeepL Pro, Google Cloud Translation), the advanced switcher and translation of dynamic content and third-party apps become available. Advanced is $75 a month or $750 a year: five languages, 5,000 products, 250 glossary rules, sync of 125 new items, ten content-exclusion rules and Shopify Flow support. Beyond the listing: Pro at $120 a month or $1,200 a year adds API access with ten languages, 10,000 products, 500 glossary rules, sync of 250 and 50 exclusion rules; Enterprise at $250 or $2,500 gives 20 languages, 50,000 products, 1,000 glossary rules, sync of 1,250, 200 exclusion rules and a customer success manager; Unlimited at $500 or $5,000 lifts products, glossary, sync and exclusion rules to unlimited at 20 languages. Annual billing is described as two months free, which is the same 17% the listing quotes. Trial length is inconsistent across the vendor's own pages: every plan card on langshop.app/pricing says 7-day, while langshop.app/faq and the Shopify listing both say 14-day. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with LangShop?

Two things sit awkwardly next to each other in the plan table. The headline promise is 'unlimited words', but every tier caps how many products you may translate and how many languages you may run, so the meter you actually pay is catalogue size. And the named engines that the listing leads with — OpenAI, DeepL Pro, Google Cloud Translation — are a Standard-tier feature at $40 a month; below that you get limited manual and AI translation. The Shopify listing also understates the ladder: it stops at Advanced and links to 'more pricing plans', while the vendor's pricing page publishes Pro at $120, Enterprise at $250 and Unlimited at $500 — and API access, which no listing tier mentions, starts at Pro. The app is old enough to judge (launched 15 September 2016, developer Aheadworks) and most of its 480 reviews are positive, but 23 of them are one-star, and the recent negative ones are specific rather than vague: a Slovak store reporting that metafield translations ignore both the AI store context and the glossary rules, and a Swedish store of almost three years reporting that products duplicated from another product carry the wrong translation across. If metafields or duplicated products are central to your catalogue, test exactly that during the trial.

Livestorm

Is Livestorm worth it?

Livestorm is genuinely best for teams running a predictable programme of webinars to a known audience size, where buying a year of attendance up front is cheaper than a per-seat platform. Skip it if your webinar schedule is irregular or experimental, because paying a year ahead for attendance you cannot forecast is the wrong shape; a per-month platform is safer while you find out what works.

How much does Livestorm cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-05 on their own pricing page) There is still no plan price. Pro is sold as attendee credits, bought as a yearly pack up front, with sessions up to 4 hours and unlimited team members; Enterprise is quote-only with sessions up to 12 hours. The rate depends on the currency you pick on the page, and the two are not conversions of each other: €2.50 per attendee in euros, $3.00 in dollars. Their own definition, worth reading twice because it decides your bill: one credit is spent for each unique participant, per session, over a 12-month period. Someone attending two different sessions costs 2 credits; the same person joining live and later watching the replay of that session counts once. Registrants who never show up cost nothing, and your own team members never consume credits. New since August: the FAQ now says what happens when the pack runs out — you get alerts as you approach the limit, and once you reach it new attendees cannot join a session until you move to a higher yearly tier. What still is not answered anywhere on the page is what becomes of credits you have not used at the twelve-month mark. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Livestorm?

This is a bet on attendance that you place a year in advance. You buy credits up front — €2.50 each in euros, $3.00 in dollars, set separately rather than converted — and a credit is spent per unique participant per session, so a four-part series to the same 200 people is 800 credits, not 200, which is €2,000. A webinar that does better than expected runs you out, and the page is now clear about what that means: new attendees cannot join until you buy a higher tier. The page publishes the per-attendee rate but never a total. Before you commit, count sessions times expected attendees for the whole year, and ask what happens to unused credits at the twelve-month mark, because the page does not say.

Meeri

Is Meeri worth it?

Meeri is genuinely best for small Shopify stores that want a cart-recovery channel which costs almost nothing and takes no commission on what it recovers — and that are willing to treat the free 300 notifications a month as a measurement of their own push opt-in rate before paying anything. Skip it if you need the recovered contacts anywhere other than the browser that opted in, you run recovery through Klaviyo, Postscript or another stack you want this to feed, or you cannot get the usage-based charge on Pro quoted as a rate before you enable it.

How much does Meeri cost?

(read 2026-08-23 on apps.shopify.com/meeripush-push-notifications, listed as “Meeri Abandoned Cart Recovery”, and on meeritech.com; both re-read 2026-09-19 with no amount changed) Two plans, and the free one is a real plan rather than a demo. Basic is free to install and covers up to 300 push notifications a month, which the listing itself translates as roughly 100 recovered carts. It carries unlimited subscribers and segmentation, the abandoned-cart recovery campaign, scheduled promotional campaigns, AI-generated campaign content, intelligent delivery timing and basic email support, and it takes no commission on recovered revenue. Pro is $4.99 a month with a 7-day free trial and adds up to 3,000 push notification impressions, unlimited campaigns and automations and premium support. All charges are billed in USD, and recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days. The plan text says Pro “upgrades as you grow” and that additional usage-based charges are billed every 30 days, without printing a rate anywhere on the listing. The vendor’s own site sells the same two tiers at the same prices, calling Basic free forever and Pro’s allowance 3,000 notification impressions a month, and it does not print a usage rate either. The app is English-only, works with Shopify Admin and sits in Shopify’s abandoned-cart category. Developer MEERI TECH L.L.C-FZ, Dubai; the app launched on 23 February 2024 and carried 9 App Store reviews in August 2026 and 11 on 19 September 2026. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Meeri?

Start with the numbers on the vendor’s own homepage, because they do not match the App Store. Read on 19 September 2026, meeritech.com still says “5.0 on Shopify App Store”, “100% five-star reviews” and “5.0 average — 8 verified reviews on Shopify” — word for word what it said on 23 August. The listing that same morning shows 4.7 from 11 reviews: ten at five stars and one at one star. So the vendor’s figure is what you get by leaving the single bad review out, and its review count has stood still while the real one moved. Nothing about the app is settled by that, but a marketing page that rounds its own rating up by dropping the worst review, and then does not refresh it for a month, is a useful thing to know before you weigh the rest of the page. The review base is thin whichever number you use. Eleven reviews on an app that launched in February 2024, and the three the listing shows first come from one store in the United Kingdom and two in Pakistan, one of which had been using the app for seven days when it wrote. That is not evidence of anything wrong; it is very little evidence of anything at all, and it cannot tell you how this behaves on a store like yours. Then there is the channel itself, which is the real decision. Web push needs a browser-level subscription, and the app’s own pitch is that no email or phone number is required to get one. That cuts both ways: the list is easier to build and worthless off the browser that built it. You cannot export those subscribers into an email tool, you cannot reach them anywhere else, and your recovery ceiling is set by opt-in rate rather than by the app. Measure the opt-in rate first — 300 free notifications a month is enough to find out — because it decides everything the paid plan can do for you. One more limit worth reading before you install: the listing names English as the only language, and Shopify Admin as the only integration. There is no Klaviyo, no email platform, no SMS tool on that line, so this sits beside your existing stack rather than inside it.

No public pricing (re-verified 6 September 2026): mktg.ai/pricing still returns 404 and the navigation carries no pricing item, so every route ends at 'Book a Demo'. The tiers themselves are no longer secret, though — the FAQ names Growth and Enterprise above the entry level and describes what they add (dedicated onboarding on both; a dedicated customer success manager, SLA-backed response times and quarterly business reviews on top of that). Email support is on every plan; custom integrations and EU data residency are Enterprise-only, with US data centres the default. The machine-readable llms.txt is Wix boilerplate advertising an MCP endpoint and carries no price either. Rates require a sales conversation. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Mktg.ai?

Two honest cautions. First, the price is still hidden — a 404 where the pricing page should be, and no pricing item in the navigation — which for a tool that promises spend transparency is an irony worth noticing, and the FAQ makes it sharper: its own introduction says it covers what the platform costs, and then no answer in it names a figure. What the FAQ does publish is the tier names, Growth and Enterprise, and the fact that EU data residency is Enterprise-only. Second, the ROI story is the vendor's own: the homepage tile assumes a $5M budget and puts a 3% efficiency gain at $150K alongside $100K of reallocated spend, which is 2% of the same budget. Ask for verified case numbers at your spend level on the demo call.

Moosend

Is Moosend worth it?

Moosend is genuinely best for small businesses and marketers who want affordable email marketing and automation with a low entry price, a real free trial and a clean drag-and-drop builder. Skip it if you run a very large list where per-subscriber pricing adds up, or you only need transactional/API email — a developer-focused sender is cheaper for that.

How much does Moosend cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-06) A 30-day free trial with no credit card. Pro is priced by list size across 21 steps from 500 to 1,000,000 contacts, quoted monthly, biannually (sold as 15% off) or annually (sold as 20% off). At 500 contacts it is $9 monthly, $8 biannual and $7 annual. The ladder is not monotonic per contact: paid annually, 8,000 contacts is $51 a month against $70 at 10,000, 75,000 is $333 against $499 at 100,000, and 500,000 is $2,317 against $2,829 at 600,000 — three steps up the slider that cost more per head than the step below them. The discounts round to whole dollars and so land short at small sizes: at 1,000 contacts $16 monthly becomes $14 biannual (12.5% off) and $13 annual (18.75% off). Instead of a subscription you can buy email credits outright with no expiry: 350,000 for $350, 500,000 for $500, 750,000 for $750 and 1,000,000 for $1,000 — a flat $0.001 per email with no volume discount. Above Pro the page shows Moosend+ (a custom plan assembled from add-ons: dedicated IPs, transactional emails, audience discovery, custom dashboards, hosted files, extra team members, SSO and SAML) and Enterprise, both quote-only. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Moosend?

The friendly $7-9 headline is the entry rate at the smallest list size (500 contacts), and the ladder above it does not fall smoothly: paid annually, 8,000 contacts costs $51 a month while 10,000 costs $70, so a list of 9,000 sits on the wrong side of the sharpest jump on the slider. The same reversal repeats at 100,000 and at 600,000. Read the comparison table before you assume Pro covers you, too: transactional emails, SSO and SAML, a dedicated IP, hosted files and an account manager are Moosend+ add-ons or Enterprise rather than included.

Is Nexis CRO worth it?

How much does Nexis CRO cost?

That matters more than usual here, because AEO tracking is a young field: nobody has yet shown that being cited by ChatGPT or Perplexity moves revenue, and the numbers a tracker reports are hard for a merchant to check independently. Nextify.ai

Is Nextify.ai worth it?

Nextify.ai is genuinely best for advertisers who need a steady stream of short product clips and will deliberately choose the cheap model for drafts, and teams who would rather have video, avatars, lip-sync and product imagery drawing on one credit pool than pay for four separate subscriptions. Skip it if you are budgeting from the “up to N videos” figures on the pricing page, you need talking-head or avatar video at any volume — that route is 6.7 credits a second, so Pro buys seven sixty-second ads a month — or you expected the free tier to work as a trial: it is 50 watermarked credits and it cannot reach the Seedance models at all.

How much does Nextify.ai cost?

(read 7 September 2026 on nextify.ai/pricing, signed in and signed out, in both billing modes) Five ways to pay, and the free plan is only visible when you are logged out — the signed-in pricing page starts at Starter. Free is $0 for 50 credits a month, watermarked, on the basic models only, and the page sells that as up to 2 videos and 25 images. Billed monthly the paid tiers are Starter $29, Pro $79 and Business $189. Billed annually the same tiers are $21, $52 and $114 a month, charged $244, $617 and $1,361 a year — the 30%, 35% and 40% badges check out at 28%, 34% and 40% against the monthly rate. Credit allowances are 1,000, 3,000 and 8,000 a month; Business is the only tier with a second seat. A one-off pack of 1,250 credits is $50, never expires and does not auto-renew, which works out at $0.04 a credit against $0.017 on annual Pro — so topping up costs more than twice what the subscription does. Subscription credits do not roll over between cycles. Refunds are limited to three days from a first subscription, and add-on packs are non-refundable. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Nextify.ai?

The plans are sold in videos and images; the meter runs in credits per second, and the two do not reconcile. Every tier's headline count works out at 20 credits a video and 2 credits an image — 1,000 credits become “up to 50 videos” and “up to 500 images”, 3,000 become 150 and 1,500, 8,000 become 400 and 4,000. The app's own credit table prices video per second of output: Seedance 2.0, the model the editor pre-selects, is 12 credits a second at 720p, so the default four-second clip costs 48. We generated one and watched the balance fall from 3,000 to 2,952. That makes Pro 62 clips a month rather than 150, and 16 if you use the 15-second maximum. The 20-credit figure is reachable, but only on the 5-credit-a-second model at four seconds. The image claim has no such escape hatch: the cheapest image model in the table is 7 credits and the pre-selected one is 10, so nothing in the product costs the 2 credits those counts assume, and Starter's 500 images is nearer 100.

NiceJob

Is NiceJob worth it?

NiceJob is genuinely best for local and service businesses that want reputation marketing on offense — automatically asking happy customers for reviews and showcasing them — rather than only managing damage when a bad review lands. Skip it if you need deep reporting or highly customized review workflows, or your service quality isn't ready for more visibility yet — fix that first, then amplify it.

How much does NiceJob cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-11 on their own pricing page) Software plans are Reviews at $75/mo and Pro at $125/mo, both USD, with a 14-day free trial, no credit card up front and no contracts. The website plans are Sites at $99/mo and Grow + Sites at $174/mo, each with a one-off $199 setup fee; the software-only plans carry no setup fee. The page also runs a contact-count ladder that the headline figures hide: Grow is $75 for 1-2,500 customers, $95 above 2,500, $145 above 5,000 and $290 above 10,000, and Grow + Sites is $174, $194, $244 and $389 across the same steps — an even $99 apart at every rung. Sites add-ons are billed on top: an extra landing page is $145 one-time plus $15/mo, and a CMS for blogs, services or locations is $245 one-time plus $15/mo. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with NiceJob?

Reporting and customization are fairly basic and there's a setup fee on top of the monthly. noCRM

Is noCRM worth it?

noCRM is genuinely best for solo sellers, small outbound teams and telesales operations that want a list of leads each carrying a next step, rather than a CRM to configure — and European buyers who care that it is built and hosted in the EU, ISO 27001 certified and billed in euros. Skip it if you want email to live inside the tool without paying for the top tier, because Starter and Expert are BCC-only; you need WhatsApp, VoIP dialling or call recording, all of which are Dream-only; you are running a team and expected roles, permissions and performance reports below €33 a user a month; or you wanted a free plan rather than a 15-day trial.

How much does noCRM cost?

(read 9 September 2026 on www.nocrm.io/pricing, in both billing modes) Three per-seat tiers and no free plan. The page opens on annual billing, where Starter is €11, Expert €22 and Dream €33 per user a month; switch the toggle to monthly and the same tiers are €19, €29 and €39. That makes the annual saving 42% on Starter, 24% on Expert and 15% on Dream, so the "save up to 40%" badge is carried entirely by the cheapest tier. Starter is capped at 500 leads in a single pipeline with at most four custom fields, and it is sold to new customers only. Every tier includes 5,000 emails a month and all users on one account must sit on the same plan. There is no free tier: a 15-day trial runs without a credit card, or 30 days if you add one, and the account is paused rather than downgraded when it ends. Checkout is through Stripe, and 20% VAT is added for French companies and for EU businesses without a valid VAT number. One thing to read twice — in the annual view the Starter card reads €11/user/year while the comparison table directly beneath it reads €11/user/month for the same plan. The month is the correct one: it is what the page's own plan data carries for every other tier and what the monthly figure of €19 is measured against. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with noCRM?

The pitch is that salespeople hate CRMs, and the answer is a tool built around the next action rather than the form. What the plan table shows is that almost everything a sales team needs to work that way sits on the top tier. Two-way email sync is Dream at €33 a user; on Starter and on Expert, email is BCC only, which means you copy noCRM on outgoing mail and read replies elsewhere. WhatsApp lead creation and conversation sync are Dream. The VoIP integrations the homepage leads with — CloudTalk, JustCall, Aircall, power dialling, call recording, transcripts — are Dream. Roles and permissions, lead assignment, team goal tracking and team performance reports are Dream. Internal automations are Dream. noCRM's own FAQ calls Expert "the best fit for most teams", and Expert has no team management in it at all. So the honest way to read the ladder is that Starter and Expert are versions for one person — a lead list with follow-ups, and then the same thing without the caps — while the product the marketing describes starts at €33 a user a month on annual billing, or €39 monthly. That is three times the entry price, and it is the number to budget from if more than one person is selling. Two smaller things. Starter is restricted to new customers, so it is not a tier you can fall back to when a year on Expert turns out to be more than you needed. And there is no free plan behind the trial: 15 days, or 30 if you hand over a card first.

Is Notify Me worth it?

How much does Notify Me cost?

Is Outgrow worth it?

How much does Outgrow cost?

Parallel AI

Is Parallel AI worth it?

Parallel AI is genuinely best for teams that want the sales, content and support agents in one place and will genuinely use the lead engine -- that half is priced per result, gets cheaper in bulk, and a lookup that finds nothing costs nothing. Skip it if you need a bill you can forecast, because the platform credits that power every AI action carry no published per-action rate -- or you only need one of the four things it does, where a dedicated tool costs less than $99 a month.

How much does Parallel AI cost?

(read on 11 September 2026 on parallellabs.app/pricing, which stamps itself 'Last updated: 2026-08-18') The meter is credits, and there are two separate pools. Plan credits come with the subscription: Pay As You Go is $0 with 50 credits and no card, Entrepreneur $99 a month for 2,000 credits and 2 companies, Business $297 for 9,000 credits and 10 companies, and Enterprise is quote-only with SSO, on-premise deployment and dedicated support. Data credits are a different pool, bought once and never expiring, and they are the only part of the product priced per action: 1 data credit per lead or contact returned, 2 per matched enrichment lookup through the API or an agent, and a lookup that finds nothing is free. They run $25 for 500 down to $175 for 5,000, so between 5.0 and 3.5 cents a lead. The two pools expire differently, and the page says so in two places that sit far apart: plan credits 'reset on the 1st of each month', while purchased credit packs and data credits never expire. What the page never says is how many PLATFORM credits an action costs. Content generation, an agent conversation and an outreach step are all simply 'credits' with no published rate, so the 2,000 on Entrepreneur is a quantity without a unit until you have run your own work through it. Per credit the tiers differ by a third: 5.0 cents on Entrepreneur against 3.3 on Business, which is three times the price for four and a half times the credits. Running out has a tier-shaped answer -- the FAQ offers extra credit packages on the Business plan and the Pay-As-You-Go card offers top-ups, but Entrepreneur sits between them with no stated top-up route, so the $99 tier's answer to an empty meter appears to be the $297 one. Seats do not add capacity: every seat in a company shares one monthly pool, and extra seats are $15 a month ($12 annual). The add-ons are where the bill can outgrow the plan -- an extra company is $20 a month ($16 annual), an extra white-label instance $50, and anonymous website pixel identification runs $75, $250 or $500 a month for 500, 2,000 or 5,000 resolutions. On the free tier the limits are real: a 200k context window against 1M on every paid plan, 30 days of chat history instead of unlimited, no App Builder, and model access listed as 'Limited' with response times 'limited on bandwidth and availability'. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Parallel AI?

The free tier is genuinely free -- 50 credits, no card -- and it is the only way to answer the question the pricing page leaves open. Data credits are priced per unit, but platform credits are not: nowhere does the page say what a content run, an agent conversation or an outreach step costs, and those are the actions the plan is sold on. So spend those 50 credits on the workflow you would actually buy this for and read Usage & Billing, which tracks consumption by feature, model and timestamp. Until you have that number, 2,000 credits a month is a quantity without a unit.

PartnerStack

Is PartnerStack worth it?

PartnerStack is genuinely best for B2B SaaS teams that want partner payments, lead and deal registration and a marketplace of active B2B partners in one place, and are prepared to go through a demo to find out what it costs. Skip it if you want to know the price before you talk to anyone, you need click-level attribution back to the page that earned it, or you only need a simple affiliate link tracker.

How much does PartnerStack cost?

(read 2026-08-26 on partnerstack.com/pricing) There is no public price at any tier. PartnerStack publishes three plans — Launch, Growth and Enterprise — and every one of them carries a Book your demo button where the number would be; /plans is a 404. What the page does publish is what moves between tiers, and it is unusually specific. Launch gives you affiliate link tracking OR lead and deal registration — you pick one — plus marketplace access, partner payments built for B2B sales cycles, onboarding and enablement tooling, CRM integrations and their AI and MCP connector. Growth adds deeper integration support, a learning-management solution, partner challenges and incentives, MDF management and payments, and segmentation by performance or strategy. Enterprise is the only tier with full access to link tracking AND both registration motions at once, and adds custom workflows, a designated CSM with semi-annual business reviews, partner introductions and priority support. So the meter is not seats or volume as far as the page will say — it is which partner motions you are allowed to run, and the choice between tracking and registration on the entry tier is the line worth reading twice. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with PartnerStack?

The reporting counts clicks and calls them customers. A record in the Partner API's customers endpoint is a tracked click, not a signup: on 29 July 2026 a single bare curl against one tracking link at 07:09:01 UTC produced a customer record at 07:09:02, with no browser, no account and has_paid false. Read that endpoint's length as signups and you will report volume that never existed. The second half of the problem is that there is no referring-URL field anywhere in the partnership data, so you can see that a link was clicked and never learn which of your pages earned it — which is exactly the thing you need to decide what to write next.

Is Pecan AI worth it?

Pecan AI is genuinely best for data and marketing teams that want churn, LTV or demand predictions running against their own warehouse without hiring data scientists, and can work with an annual commitment quoted on a call. Skip it if you need to compare prices before you talk to anyone, you only want to see what already happened rather than what is likely to, or a fortnightly prediction cadence is not enough and the entry tier is therefore out.

How much does Pecan AI cost?

(read 2026-08-27 on pecan.ai/pricing) No public price at any tier. Pecan publishes three plans — Starter, Team and Business — and each one carries a Talk to sales button where the number would be, with a fourth enterprise route for special deployment and granular explainability. Billing is annual only and Pecan states there is no setup fee. What the page does publish is the meter, and it is not the one most buyers expect: the tier is set by monthly prediction batches and stored rows, not by seats. Starter gives 2 batches a month and 500M rows, Team 10 batches and 2Bn rows, Business custom batches and 5Bn rows; support runs from in-app only, to in-app plus Essential enablement, to Pro enablement. A batch is one run against a dataset, so two a month is a fortnightly cadence — the number that decides your tier before any conversation about team size. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Pecan AI?

The pricing page argues instead of quoting. Where the amount would be, it sets out what a data-science team would cost you — $600,000 and up for three or four specialists, and a claim that salaries are 60 to 80% of the lifecycle cost of building this yourself. That may well be true, but it is a comparison to hiring rather than a price, and it means you cannot put Pecan next to anything else until you have been through a sales call. The second thing to catch is the meter. Starter's two prediction batches a month is a fortnightly cadence; any team that wants a weekly refresh is on Team from the first day, whatever its size, and that is a tier decision made by scheduling rather than by headcount.

Pingtree

Is Pingtree worth it?

Pingtree is genuinely best for performance marketers, lead brokers and affiliate operations that already move real lead volume and want ping-tree routing, partner management, funnels and reporting in one system — the unlimited-users-with-roles policy on the self-service path means team size is not what pushes you up a plan. Skip it if you are a solo marketer or small team still testing whether a lead-gen idea works. $199/month plus unpublished overage is a lot of fixed cost to carry while you find out, and the included allowances are sized for volume you likely do not have yet. Also skip it if your actual problem is finding or enriching leads rather than distributing them, since this is routing plumbing, not a data provider.

How much does Pingtree cost?

(2026-08-27, read on their own pricing page) Self Service is “From $199” per month with a free trial included, and Managed Services carries a starting cost of $2,500, “scoped with your account team”. That is a rebuilt price list: the six named tiers that were on this page in July are gone, and there are now two paths rather than six. Self Service is the whole platform driven by Pingtree Copilot, with core usage — leads, pings, clicks and storage — included each month, overage billed after month close, unlimited users on role-based access, and validations and throughput added as volume climbs. Managed Services is a scoped engagement priced on volume, markets and complexity: implementation, integrations and workflow design are included, along with a dedicated Solutions Engineer, ongoing account optimisation, priority support with SLAs where required, and optional retainers for media, creative and ad ops. There is also an “Explore Pingtree Free” entry straight into the app. No overage rate is published on the page, and the trial no longer carries a stated length — in July it said 14 days. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Pingtree?

Two things about this price list will cost you money if you skim it. First, the $199 is a floor rather than a bill. Pingtree describes its model as usage-based and prints “overage billed after month close — no surprise mid-cycle fees” directly under the Self Service price. Leads, ping requests, clicks and database API calls past the included allowances are charged afterwards. You find out what the month cost when the month is over. No overage rate is published on the pricing page, which means the one number you most need in order to budget is the one you have to ask for. Second, the page was rebuilt between our July and August readings, and the tier structure went with it. On 27 July 2026 there were six tiers: Self Managed at Startup $499, Starter $1,250 and Growth $2,500, plus two quote-only managed tiers. On 27 August 2026 that is gone — one Self Service path from $199 a month, one Managed Services path from $2,500. Any quote, screenshot or comparison table you were handed before that date describes a price list that no longer exists, so ask for the current one in writing. There is a third gap worth naming. Copilot, the prompt-driven AI agent, is what the entire homepage is built around. Yet the pricing page is written purely in infrastructure units: leads, requests, clicks, storage, API calls. It says nothing about AI usage limits, or which path gates which Copilot capability. Read the marketing and the pricing side by side and you cannot tell what $199 buys you of the feature you are being sold on. Pingtree's own partner manager answered that question for us in writing on 28 July 2026, and agreed the pricing page says it nowhere. The answer is in the section below on what the paid path actually buys. Three things he confirmed belong here rather than in a footnote. The overage rate is still not published. The vendor says the figures are being pulled internally, and that he will not send a number he cannot source. So the budgeting gap above stands until a rate card exists. The trial length used to be printed twice, differently: the July pricing page said 14 days while the app's own countdown said 15 days left. The vendor calls that his own two surfaces disagreeing. The August page prints no length at all — it says only that a free trial is included — so ask before you start the clock. And the paid upgrade screen asks for your card without restating the plan, the price or the billing terms. The vendor confirmed that, and says it is going to product. Until it changes, note down which path you picked before you type the number in. One disclosure belongs on this page specifically. Pingtree pays us at two points in its funnel: when someone starts building, and when someone starts the free trial. Neither of those requires a purchase. We get paid whether or not you ever spend a cent with them, which is precisely why this section is about what their pricing page does not tell you.

Pipedrive

Is Pipedrive worth it?

Pipedrive is genuinely best for sales teams that want a simple, visual pipeline they can use on day one, with a separate marketing tool already in place. Skip it if you want marketing automation in the same tool (HubSpot) or need built-in outbound prospecting.

How much does Pipedrive cost?

(read 2026-08-26 on pipedrive.com/pricing over a US connection; the monthly column below is our 2026-08-16 reading from the EU) Four seat-based plans. Billed annually they are US$14, US$39, US$59 and US$79 per seat per month — which is one payment of $168, $468, $708 or $948 per seat per year, since Pipedrive charges the year up front. The page advertises that annual billing saves up to 42%. Read from the Netherlands the same column reads €14, €39, €59 and €79: the numbers do not convert, they are simply reprinted with a different symbol, so a European pays materially more for the same seat. We could not get the monthly column to render from the US on three attempts, so this is the annual view only — by Pipedrive's own 42% figure, paying month to month costs meaningfully more. The trial is 14 days with no credit card, though the affiliate landing page our own link leads to advertised 30 days, with LeadBooster, Smart Docs and Projects included, when we followed it on 3 September 2026. LeadBooster, Projects, Campaigns, Web Visitors and Smart Docs are optional paid add-ons on top, from €13.33 for Campaigns up to €41 for Web Visitors — and those add-ons are where a Pipedrive bill usually stops matching the number you picked off this page. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Pipedrive?

Pipedrive manages what happens after a lead enters your pipeline — it doesn't do outbound prospecting or marketing, so you'll pair it with a separate tool for that. As you scale and need sales, marketing and support data joined up, its sales-only focus starts to lean on add-ons.

Is Pippit worth it?

How much does Pippit cost?

(read 2026-09-19 on pippit.ai/pricing from a Netherlands exit; the page prices in the visitor's currency, so these are euro amounts) Every tier was repriced and every credit allowance cut since our 6 September reading, so treat any older figure, ours included, as withdrawn. The page opens on the Yearly tab. Yearly: Free €0 with recurring daily credits and no card; Starter €87 a year against a struck-through €145; Plus €213 against €355; Pro is a five-step ladder at €467, €948, €1,260, €1,901 and €3,117 against list prices of €779, €1,580, €2,100, €3,169 and €5,195, with the €1,901 step shown by default. What is the catch with Pippit?

Pixel Union

Is Pixel Union worth it?

Pixel Union is genuinely best for online retailers and larger-catalog stores that want a professionally designed, conversion-focused Shopify storefront without paying for custom development. Skip it if a free or low-cost Shopify theme already covers your needs, or you have a developer building a bespoke storefront anyway.

How much does Pixel Union cost?

Read on 7 September 2026, re-read on 12 September 2026. The theme pages on pixelunion.net print the price in plain text beside the 'Try theme for free' button, and the store's own product feed and the JSON-LD offer on those same pages carry the same figures, so all three agree: every theme is a one-time purchase in USD, Startup $100, Editions $120, Grid $280, Atlantic $300, Empire $360 and Tailor $360. That is a change between our two readings -- on 7 September the theme pages showed the button and no amount, and the price was readable only in the store's product data. Sister brand Out of the Sandbox, sold from outofthesandbox.com, runs from $220 (Responsive, Retina) and $240 (Launch, Pacific) through $260 (Parallax), $320 (Superstore) and $425 (Turbo) to $495 (Flex) and $499 (Amphora, Merlot, Vino); those amounts are from the 7 September reading and were not re-checked. Poptin

Is Poptin worth it?

Poptin is genuinely best for sites that want popups, forms and coupons with a genuinely usable free tier and a cheap first paid rung — $20 a month for 10,000 visitors, unlimited popups and no Poptin branding — and that are happy to run the email side elsewhere. Skip it if you want the combined email-and-popup product, because the recommended tier publishes no price at any list size; you need a second administrator or an API key, which is a $95 tier rather than a $20 one; or your traffic is measured in views rather than unique visitors, where a view-metered competitor may cost less.

How much does Poptin cost?

(read 18 September 2026 in a live browser on poptin.com/pricing, in both product modes and both billing cycles, with the in-app billing page at app.popt.in checked alongside it) The page opens with a question — “What are you looking for?” — and the answer changes the whole ladder. Pick Poptins, the popup product, and every tier carries a figure. Free is $0 forever with 1,000 unique visitors a month, one domain and unlimited poptins. Basic is $20 a month billed annually ($240 a year) or $25 billed monthly, for 10,000 visitors and one domain. Pro, marked Most Popular, is $47 annually ($564) or $59 monthly, for 50,000 visitors and four domains. Agency is $95 annually ($1,140) or $119 monthly, starting at 150,000 visitors with a dropdown that climbs through 300,000, 500,000, 750,000, one million and two million, plus unlimited domains and premium support. The stated 20% annual saving checks out at all three rungs: $60 off $300, $144 off $708 and $288 off $1,428. Pick Emails & Poptins, the combined product, and the ladder loses its prices. Free is $0 for 250 active contacts, 500 emails and 1,000 visitors. Growth — the tier the page marks RECOMMENDED — shows the word “/month” and no amount at all, at any of the eighteen contact bands in the selector. Enterprise is quote-only in both modes. The meter is unique monthly visitors, and their FAQ defines it: anyone who loads a page carrying the snippet in the last 30 days, counted once however many sessions or pages they open — unless they clear cookies or switch device or browser, in which case they count again. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Poptin?

The plan Poptin recommends does not have a price on it. Choose Emails & Poptins, and the Growth card renders the word “/month” with nothing in front of it. That is not a slow-loading figure: the contact selector works perfectly beside it — move it and the allowance updates from 500 to 1,500 to 7,500 active contacts — while the amount stays absent at every one of the eighteen bands, and the Free card in the same row renders its $0 without trouble. We checked three bands and inspected the card itself; there is no amount element in it. So the page invites you to size your list and then declines to tell you what sizing it costs. Switch to the popup-only product and everything is priced, which makes the omission stranger rather than more forgivable. It also means the honest advice depends on which door you came through: if you want the popups, this is a transparent, cheap tool; if you want the email marketing alongside them, the price is a conversation. The free plan is thinner than the feature list suggests. It carries 1,000 visitors a month, which is real, but the in-app billing page marks three things with a cross rather than a tick: Unbranded, Manage accounts, and Manage users & API keys. So the free tier shows Poptin's own branding on your popups. That is normal for the category, but the pricing page lists those rows under Free without making the distinction obvious. Branding is settled at the first paid rung, but team access is not. Basic at $20 and Pro at $47 both still carry a cross on Manage accounts and on Manage users & API keys. If you need more than one person administering this, or an API key, the tier is Agency at $95 — four and a half times the entry price for a permission rather than for volume. And read the meter definition before you size yourself. A unique visitor is counted per browser, not per person: the same buyer on a phone and a laptop is two, and anyone who clears cookies becomes new again. Your real headroom is therefore lower than your analytics suggests.

Post Purchase Upsell Hero

Is Post Purchase Upsell Hero worth it?

Post Purchase Upsell Hero is genuinely best for shopify stores that want post-purchase upsells with no fixed monthly cost, where the bill only exists once the app has already added revenue, and that are comfortable being early on an app a few months old. Skip it if you already do more than $20,000 of upsell revenue a month and would rather pay a flat fee than 2.5% of the first slice, you sell thin-margin add-ons where a revenue percentage eats the profit on the extra sale, or you want an app with more than a few months of track record.

How much does Post Purchase Upsell Hero cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/post-purchase-upsell-hero and the vendor's own site; amounts unchanged since 31 August, USD) One plan, Performance, free to install, at $0 a month plus usage charges. The usage table, read from the listing's own pricing-estimator data, has two tiers: 2.5% on the first $20,000 of upsell revenue in a month, and $0 from $20,001 up. In practice that is a commission with a ceiling — the app cannot charge more than $500 in a month, and a month in which it sells nothing costs nothing. There is no paid tier above it: unlimited funnels and offers, one-click upsell and downsell, AI product recommendations, analytics and A/B testing and market translations all sit on that single plan. Charges are billed in USD every 30 days. The vendor's own site publishes no prices at all — its pricing link leads to the same single-plan listing — so the listing is the only place the meter is stated. Neither page defines how 'upsell revenue' is measured, whether it is net of discounts, or how refunds and returns are treated. Published by HeroSoftware GmbH, which states it is independent of and not affiliated with Shopify. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Post Purchase Upsell Hero?

The 2.5% comes off revenue, not margin. On a $40 upsell carrying a 20% margin the app takes a dollar of the eight you actually made — fine. On discounted or thin-margin add-ons the same percentage is a far bigger share of the profit, and the meter reads revenue either way. There is also no flat option to escape to: a store doing $20,000 of upsell revenue a month pays the full $500 and cannot buy out of the percentage, while the free-above-$20,001 tier only rewards stores already past that line. And the app is young — it launched on 19 June 2026, so at the end of August there were barely ten weeks of merchant experience behind it. Post-purchase offers also depend on your store's checkout supporting the post-purchase extension; check that before you plan around them.

Postscript

Is Postscript worth it?

Postscript is genuinely best for Shopify stores with a list large enough that SMS beats email on response — the per-message economics only work once volume justifies the platform fee. Skip it if you are testing whether SMS works for you at all — the $49 minimum spend on the free tier means the experiment has a floor before you have sent a single message, and the listed rates cover the US and Canada only.

How much does Postscript cost?

(Re-verified 19 September 2026 on their own pricing page; every figure below is unchanged from the 30 August reading.) Starter is shown as $0 a month with a $49 monthly minimum spend, at $0.015 then $0.009 per SMS and $0.045 per MMS, plus carrier fees. Growth is $100 a month at $0.01 then $0.008 per SMS and $0.03 per MMS. Professional is $500 a month at $0.007 per SMS and $0.024 per MMS. Enterprise is contact-sales. Carrier fees are asterisked on every tier and are quantified in the footnote below the feature list: average US carrier fees of $0.00418 per SMS and $0.00841 per MMS, with the listed rates covering the US 50 states and Canada only. The free trial is a credit equal to $100 against message and carrier fees during your first 30 days; exhaust it and you are billed at the Free package rate unless you select another package. Phone numbers are priced outside the tiers: a dedicated toll-free number is assigned and verified free of charge at install, while a dedicated short code costs $750 a month levied by the carriers and passed on without markup. No contract is required. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Postscript?

The $0 a month is not free — it carries a $49 monthly minimum spend, which means $49 is your floor whether you send anything or not. Read the tiers as what they are: a platform fee plus a per-message rate plus carrier fees. That third line is easy to miss because it sits in a footnote rather than on the tier cards, and it is not small: the page puts the average US carrier fee at $0.00418 an SMS and $0.00841 an MMS, so against the $0.009 volume rate on Starter it adds close to half again. Before you compare this with anything, work out your monthly message volume and multiply it out on all three published tiers: Growth costs $100 more than Starter but saves a fifth of a cent per message, so it pays back somewhere around 50,000 messages a month.

PreOrder Now

Is PreOrder Now worth it?

PreOrder Now is genuinely best for stores that sell drops, restocks or made-to-order products and want pre-order badges, partial payments and back-in-stock emails without touching the theme — and that are on Shopify Basic or Standard, where the price is proportionate. Skip it if you are on Shopify Plus and pre-orders are a small part of what you do, because you will pay $99.95 for the same feature set a Basic store gets for $19.95 — or you only ever need one pre-order product at a time, which the free tier already covers.

How much does PreOrder Now cost?

(re-verified 13 September 2026 on zenpire.tech/app-listing/pre-order-now/, every amount unchanged since 10 September; the amounts come from Zenpire's own page because the app is not installable from the Shopify App Store: apps.shopify.com/preorder-now, checked 14 September 2026, carries it as "PreOrder Now WOD" by Website on Demand Studio, LLC and states the app is currently not available there, and a store search for Zenpire returns no apps) Five tiers, and they are named after your Shopify plan rather than after what the app does. Free is $0 and covers your first pre-order product, with mixed-cart warnings and email tech support. Then Shopify Basic is $19.95 a month, Shopify Standard $39.95, Shopify Advanced $59.95 and Shopify Plus $99.95 -- all with unlimited pre-order products. Read the feature lists side by side and the point becomes obvious: Basic and Standard list exactly the same five features (unlimited pre-order products, collection page badges, preorder discount, pre-order by product tag, Quickview support), and Advanced and Plus list exactly the same three (unlimited pre-order products, "ALL FEATURES of Basic Shopify & Shopify plans", dedicated success manager support). So the ladder is not buying you capability; it is charging you according to the size of store Shopify says you run. A Plus merchant pays five times what a Basic merchant pays for the same badges, the same discounts and the same tagging. The one real step is Advanced, which adds a dedicated success manager. Note that partial payments, which the FAQ advertises as a feature, are named on none of the five plan cards, so the tier that carries them is unstated. All charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with PreOrder Now?

The free tier is more useful than it first looks: one pre-order product, unlimited time, with the mixed-cart warning included. For a store that runs one drop at a time that is not a trial, it is a plan. Before you upgrade, check which Shopify plan you are on, because that — not your feature needs — is what sets the price here. And if you are on Plus, price this against alternatives properly: at $99.95 a month you are paying a Plus surcharge for a feature set the app itself lists as identical to the $59.95 tier.

Printify

Is Printify worth it?

Printify is genuinely best for creators and stores testing print-on-demand with no upfront cost, upgrading to Premium once volume justifies it. Skip it if you sell only a handful of items a month — the free plan is right, and Premium's fee outweighs the discount.

How much does Printify cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-07) A free plan at $0 a month -- you pay only the product base cost plus shipping per order -- and Premium from $39 a month, or from $24.99 a month billed yearly, which the page states as 36% off. Premium's discount is printed as two separate lines: up to 33% off new products and up to 20% off all products. Enterprise is custom. How much does ProtectMyOrder cost?

(re-read 2026-09-18) The App Store route has closed. apps.shopify.com/protectmyorder, the page this review was built on, now returns “This app is not currently available on the Shopify App Store. If you have support questions, contact ProtectMyOrder directly.” — no plan block, no review record, no install button. ProtectMyOrder's own pricing page, re-read the same day, is unchanged and still sells three tiers, all priced as a share of upsell revenue rather than a monthly fee. Standard at 19.99% adds a profitability guarantee, a gradual roll-out to 50% of visitors, fully customisable design and wording, and an assigned support agent. What is the catch with ProtectMyOrder?

Start with what is no longer there. Read on 18 September 2026, the Shopify App Store listing for this app is gone: the page says it is not currently available and sends support questions to the vendor. The vendor's site is still live and still selling, and its own footer still links to that dead page. The way in is now a form and a collaborator-access request rather than an install button, and the $20 monthly minimum — which only ever appeared on the App Store plan — no longer appears anywhere a buyer can read it. That removes the discrepancy this review was first built around and leaves a harder one. Everything you can now learn about what this costs sits on a page the vendor controls, and all three tiers take a share of your upsell revenue rather than a fee. On Standard the pitch is that you keep 80%, and whether that is profit is settled by your own loss rate: a missing parcel is your replacement, your postage and your conversation. The public record has thinned with the listing. Twelve reviews sat on it in August, most of them from 2024, and while it is down that record is not readable at all — the revenue figures merchants quote on the vendor's own site are theirs and unaudited. Selling package protection also brushes against insurance rules in some jurisdictions. The vendor says its arrangement has been verified with US and UK insurance lawyers, which is their statement rather than a regulator's; if you trade where that matters, ask your own adviser what you are allowed to sell before you turn it on.

Pumper Bundles

Is Pumper Bundles worth it?

Pumper Bundles is genuinely best for shopify stores that want bundles, quantity breaks, BOGO and free-gift offers without touching code, and that value a free tier which is the complete app rather than a feature-stripped demo. Skip it if you expect more capability as you pay more — every tier here carries the same features and you are only buying a higher revenue ceiling — or you need conditional bundling logic beyond tiered discounts.

How much does Pumper Bundles cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/pumper-quantity-breaks-product-bundles-discounts AND on the vendor's own site, USD; listed amounts unchanged since 2 September) Four tiers on the listing, with a 7-day free trial on the paid ones. The ladder is priced by how much extra revenue the app is allowed to generate for you, not by what it can do: the feature list — unlimited bundles and quantity breaks, chat support seven days a week, bundles on page builders, cart drawer integrations — is identical on all four. Free covers up to $300 of extra revenue generated by the app. Starter is $9.99 a month, or $94.68 a year (saves 21%), and covers up to $1,000. Growth is $29.99 a month or $269.88 a year (save 25%) and covers up to $5,000. Unlimited is $49.99 a month or $449.88 a year (save 25%) and removes the ceiling. Charges are billed in USD every 30 days. Two things on the vendor's own site contradict the listing and were unresolved on 19 September 2026: its FAQ says the trial is 14 days with full access and no card, against the listing's 7 days; and it answers 'Are there any hidden charges?' by saying Pumper charges a maximum of $39.99 a month, against the listing's $49.99 top tier. Where the two differ, the listing is the page Shopify bills from. Neither page defines how the attributed extra revenue that decides your tier is measured. The vendor trades as Profit Pumper (Henq eCommerce LLC, Delaware). Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Pumper Bundles?

Every tier ships the same four features, so what you are buying is a ceiling on the revenue the app is allowed to earn you. The bill therefore rises exactly when the app is working, and it rises in steps: pass $300 and you owe $9.99, pass $1,000 and you owe $29.99, pass $5,000 and you owe $49.99. Read that in both directions. It makes the free plan unusually generous — the whole app, not a stripped demo — and it makes every upgrade buy you nothing new, only permission to keep going. The one number the pricing table never defines is how that attributed extra revenue is measured, and it is the number the entire ladder rests on.

Is PushOwl worth it?

PushOwl is genuinely best for Shopify stores that want to win back abandoned carts and browsing sessions with one-click web push — reaching shoppers who never handed over an email — and then layer in email and SMS, starting on a free tier that genuinely does something. How much does PushOwl cost?

Power is $79/month for 25,000 up to unlimited web push, with flash-sale and browse-abandonment triggers, segmentation and custom attribution windows. Yearly billing is advertised at 10% off, and 20% on the web push side of Plus. It is Shopify-only. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with PushOwl?

Quartile

Is Quartile worth it?

Quartile is genuinely best for brands and sellers already running paid media across several retail networks at once — Amazon Sponsored Ads and Amazon DSP, Walmart, Instacart, Criteo, Google, Meta, Microsoft and, newly listed on the site in September 2026, ChatGPT Ads — who would rather hand the whole set to one team than wire together a tool per channel. The fixed account team is the actual product here, not a support tier, and if you were going to hire an agency anyway then a platform with people attached is a fair shape for the money. Skip it if you want to know what something costs before you take a sales call — nothing on this site will tell you, and two of its direct competitors will. Skip it as well if your spend sits on one marketplace and you are comfortable running the bids yourself. The multi-network reach and the account team are what you would be paying for, and neither does much for a single-channel seller with a working routine.

How much does Quartile cost?

(2026-09-11, re-read on their own site) There is no public pricing. quartile.com/pricing serves the same page as the homepage — no tier, no rate card and no entry figure anywhere on it, and the only call to action is Request Demo. The dollar amounts the site does show are volume claims about their customer base rather than prices: over $2B in annual retail advertising spend managed and over $25B in annual managed revenue, across 5,300+ customers in more than 32 countries. Two audiences are named, Small Business and Mid-Market/Enterprise, with no rate attached to either. The 40% introductory discount that the referral route carried in August 2026 is no longer published: quartile.com/partners now rewards the referrer by an unnamed amount instead. Budget for this one from a written quote, because nothing else exists. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Quartile?

Everything about the sales motion here is a conversation. The product is sold as a platform plus a dedicated account team, and there is no self-serve entry: the only route in is Request Demo. That carries a cost which never appears on the page — you cannot size this against your ad budget before you talk to someone, and you cannot put it next to a competitor on paper. It matters more than usual in this category, because the direct peers do publish. Our own dossiers have Teikametrics at $149 a month billed annually for up to $10K in monthly ad spend, plus 3% of spend above that (read 2026-08-01), and BidX at €495 a month for its self-service Amazon tier (read 2026-08-06). Against those two, Quartile is an unknown until you have a quote in hand. The introductory offer that used to soften this has been withdrawn. In August 2026 a referral link carried 40% off a new customer's first three months; re-read on 11 September 2026, quartile.com/partners publishes no customer discount at all — it now rewards the person making the introduction, by an amount it declines to name. So there is no published discount left to negotiate against, and the quote is the only figure in the entire transaction. One more figure to handle carefully: the 41% average increase in ROAS on their homepage is Quartile's own number, measured by Quartile on Quartile's customers. Nobody independent has checked it and neither have we, so ask what the sample was and over what period before you let it weigh on the decision.
