ReachStream

Is ReachStream worth it?

ReachStream is genuinely best for small sales and marketing teams that want a B2B contact database with a published price rather than a quote, and whose volume is predictable enough to size in exports a month — the tier below the ones where ZoomInfo and Cognism start.. Skip it if you need more than three seats without an enterprise conversation; your volume is spiky, because nothing on the page tells you what an extra credit costs; or your market is outside the sectors where their data is strongest, in which case ask for a sample against your own ICP before you pay..

How much does ReachStream cost?

(read 2026-09-10 in a browser on reachstream.com/prospect/pricing/ with both billing toggles, and re-verified against that same page on 19 September 2026 -- every amount, credit allowance and seat count below is unchanged; only the credit-rollover answer in the FAQ has flipped) Five tiers in USD. Free is $0 with 100 export credits and 200 email views a month (1,200 and 2,400 a year). Starter is $39 a month, or $29 on annual billing, for 5,000 export credits a month (60,000 a year). Pro is $59 or $49 for 10,000 a month. Business is $99 or $79 for 20,000 a month (240,000 a year) and, for the first time, up to three seats instead of one. Enterprise is quote-only. The annual discount is a flat 20% on the price and nothing else: the credit allowance is identical either way. Two meters run separately — export credits are spent downloading to CSV or syncing to a CRM, email credits are spent revealing an address in the platform or the Chrome extension — while contact and company insight views are unlimited on every tier including Free. Email views are unlimited on all paid tiers. The FAQ, re-read on 19 September 2026, states that unused credits do not roll over and that they reset at the start of each new billing cycle -- on 10 September that same question answered the other way round, so size the plan for an ordinary month rather than a busy one and confirm the rule before you buy. It also states that direct-dial and mobile numbers are included on Starter, Pro and Business. Note that the main /pricing/ page carries no figures at all — it only routes you to Prospect or Email Verifier — and that the site answers a plain HTTP request with 403, so the figures above come from a browser reading of the Prospect pricing page one level down. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with ReachStream?

The meter is on exporting, not on looking, and that is the number to size before you pick a tier. Contact and company views are unlimited on every plan including the free one, so the demo will feel generous; what you actually pay for is pulling those records out, and separately for revealing an email address, which is a second meter the plan cards do not put next to the first. Free gives 100 exports and 200 email views a month, which is a sample rather than a workflow. The second thing to check is seats: Starter and Pro both include exactly one, so a two-person sales team is on Business at $99 a month before it needs the extra credits. Credits do not roll over: the FAQ, re-read on 19 September 2026, says unused credits reset at the start of each new billing cycle, so a plan sized for a busy month is simply wasted in a quiet one. That same question answered the other way on 10 September, which is reason enough to check it yourself before you commit. Underbuying is no clearer either: two figures on the page are not explained anywhere — Starter and Pro promise to "unlock an extra $250 / $500 worth of data", which is priced in dollars rather than in credits or records — and the cost of a credit once you run out is not published at all.

rePete

Is rePete worth it?

rePete is genuinely best for Shopify stores selling consumables or anything with a natural replenishment rhythm — coffee, supplements, pet food, skincare — whose customers refuse subscriptions but do come back, and who would rather pay for results than carry another monthly app fee. Skip it if your repeat revenue is already large, because an uncapped 3% overtakes any subscription app well before six figures; your customers buy once and rarely return, where there is no reorder moment to predict; or you cannot get comfortable with an app that can edit orders, discounts and the storefront.

How much does rePete cost?

(read 19 September 2026 in a live browser on repete.me/pricing and on the App Store listing at apps.shopify.com/reorder-service) There is no subscription and no tier. rePete is free to install and takes a percentage of the sales it claims to have caused, billed in USD, on three rates that are defined by a clock rather than by judgement. Direct Sales is 3%, charged when rePete nudges a customer to reorder a product and they complete the purchase within 24 hours. Assisted Sales is 1%, charged on the same nudge when the purchase lands within 7 days. Upsells and cross-sells are 5%, charged on any extra items the customer adds beyond the reorder product itself. What the page rules out is as useful as what it charges: no SMS fees, no email fees, no per-contact fees, no push fees, no app fees and no minimums. So the messaging channels — email, SMS, WhatsApp and on-site — carry no cost of their own, which is unusual in a category where SMS is normally metered separately. There is no published ceiling, no volume discount and no negotiated rate: the percentages are the whole price list. The app is built by Bold of Winnipeg, Shopify's first front-end app developer and the team behind Bold Subscriptions; it launched on 4 July 2025 and holds 5.0 from nine reviews. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with rePete?

The pricing is honest and the arithmetic still deserves care, because this is a percentage with no ceiling on it. There is no cap, no volume discount and no tier: 3% of attributed reorders at $5,000 a month is $150, at $50,000 it is $1,500, and at $200,000 it is $6,000 — for the same software. Most Shopify apps stop charging more once you pass their top tier; this one never does. If rePete works, the bill grows exactly as fast as the result, which is the deal you are signing rather than a trap, but it is the opposite shape to every subscription app you are comparing it against. The seven-day window is where I would push back. Direct Sales at 3% requires the purchase within 24 hours of the nudge, which is a strong causal claim. Assisted Sales at 1% counts anything that lands within seven days — and a customer who buys coffee, supplements or pet food every month was going to reorder in that window anyway. You will pay 1% on a quantity of revenue that would have arrived without the message, and there is no way to tell from the outside how much. Ask for the split between direct and assisted in your first month before you judge the return. The highest rate sits on the smallest claim. Upsells and cross-sells are 5%, charged on any extra item added beyond the reorder product — so a customer who reorders and adds one more thing pays 3% on the first and 5% on the second. That is the most expensive rate on the page attached to the action rePete has the weakest claim to have caused. The evidence base is thin rather than bad. Nine reviews, all five-star, the visible ones from early September 2026 and describing two to three months of use. That is real usage by named stores, and it is still nine. One thing to read before installing: the data scope is wide. The listing asks to view sensitive customer data, and to view *and edit* customers, products, orders, discounts, shop analytics and the online store. That is consistent with an app that writes discounts and builds carts, but it is a lot of reach for a tool you are trying on a commission basis.

How much does Riverside cost?

(read 2026-09-07 on riverside.com/pricing; riverside.fm now redirects to riverside.com. Is RocketReach worth it?

RocketReach is genuinely best for sales, recruiting and BD teams whose bottleneck is finding verified direct dials and personal emails, and who can commit to an annual term - that is where the search allowance stops being metered. Skip it if you need the outreach engine more than the data, or you cannot commit to a year: monthly billing caps lookups and exports at 100 to 1,000 a month, and platforms like lemlist or Amplemarket build the sequencing around the contacts instead of selling you the contacts first.

How much does RocketReach cost?

(read 2026-09-01 on rocketreach.co/pricing, re-verified 2026-09-19 in a real browser with every amount unchanged) A free account exists: signing up takes no credit card and gives 5 lookups. Above that are three paid plans, all quoted per month on an annual term. Essentials is $19/month, billed $229 USD annually, and is email only: unlimited personal and professional email lookups, 1,200 exports a year, 5 active Autopilot jobs and a send limit of 500 emails a day. Pro is $52/month, billed $619 USD annually, and adds unlimited mobile and direct phone numbers, 3,600 exports a year, technographics, news and org charts, 10 active Autopilot jobs and the Salesforce, Outreach, HubSpot, Salesloft and Bullhorn integrations. Ultimate is $115/month, billed $1,379 USD annually, with 20,000 exports a year, 25 active Autopilot jobs, Salesforce custom mapping, intent data and healthcare data. Above those, enterprise plans are quote-only and the page says they start at $6K annually. Read the headline figures as the annual rate: the plan-features table lists searches as unlimited on the annual term but capped at 100, 250 and 1,000 a month on monthly billing, with exports capped at those same numbers instead of the yearly allowances. RocketReach says a lookup is refunded when it returns no verified email or phone number, and that cancelling takes effect from the next term, so you keep access for the term you have already paid for. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with RocketReach?

The published prices are annual rates, and the annual term is doing more work than the page lets on. RocketReach's own feature table lists searches as unlimited on the annual term but caps them at 100, 250 and 1,000 a month if you bill monthly, and caps exports at those same numbers instead of 1,200, 3,600 and 20,000 a year. So the $19 on the card is $229 up front, and the flexible-looking monthly option is the one that rations the product. Their FAQ adds that cancelling takes effect from the next term, so a year is a year. The plan boundary matters more than the price. Essentials is email only: mobile and direct phone numbers start at Pro, and so do the Salesforce, Outreach, Salesloft and Bullhorn integrations, technographics and org charts. Above Ultimate the ladder stops being a ladder, with enterprise starting at $6K annually against $1,379 for Ultimate. And the numbers that sell it are all RocketReach's own, printed on their pricing page: 700 million professionals, 60 million companies, 98% accuracy, 30 million users, 95% of the S&P 500. We have measured none of them. Contact-data accuracy is the thing that varies most by territory and by seniority, and a database claim is an average, not a promise about your list. The free account is the right answer to that: it costs nothing and needs no card, so run the free lookups against a slice of your own target accounts before you commit to a year. A lookup that finds nothing verified is refunded, per their FAQ, which makes that test cheaper still.

Is Scarcity.AI worth it?

Scarcity.AI is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who genuinely run low stock or timed promotions and want to surface that on the product page — the low stock counter is tied to real inventory, which makes it the honest one of the three when your stock actually is low. Skip it if your stock is not low and your sale does not end, because a claim a shopper would read as false is one the FTC treats as deceptive; or your brand sells on trust, where a blinking counter costs more in credibility than it returns.

How much does Scarcity.AI cost?

(read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com, across all three listings) These are three separate apps from one developer, each installed and billed on its own. The Low Stock Counter is $4.99 a month or $41.91 a year at a stated 30% saving, with a 7-day trial; its free tier is Development Stores, meaning development and partner stores only rather than a working free plan. The Visitors Counter is $1.99 a month or $16.71 a year, with a genuine free plan that carries the counter itself, customisation, product-level targeting and holiday presets — the $1.99 adds an upsell banner for your most-viewed product, on a 3-day trial. The Countdown Timer listing shows a free tier and no paid ladder. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Effective Apps, who also publish Blocky, TiXel and Way. Ratings at the time of writing: 4.7 from 84 reviews on the low stock counter, 4.8 from 36 on the visitors counter and 5.0 from 22 on the countdown timer. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Scarcity.AI?

All three read real data, which is worth saying before anything else — the low stock counter shows inventory levels and the visitors counter reads unique visitors, live traffic and product views. Nothing here invents a number. But the visitors counter carries two settings that shape which true number a shopper sees. It can show the counter only after a set number of views, so a quiet product simply displays nothing rather than a small figure. And the time frame is yours to set, so 'twelve people viewed this' can mean twelve in five minutes or twelve since yesterday, presented identically. Neither setting fabricates anything; together they let you present a true number that a reasonable shopper would read as something else. That distinction is where the legal line sits. The FTC treats false urgency and scarcity as deceptive practice under section 5 of the FTC Act, and the examples in its dark-patterns guidance are close to these mechanics: a low-stock claim when stock is plentiful, or a cart-activity figure well above the real one. The test is whether a reasonable consumer would be misled about a material fact. That test does not apply to the app; it applies to how you configure it, which means the compliance question lands on your desk rather than the developer's.

Scrolly

Is Scrolly worth it?

Scrolly is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want a free, one-click back-to-top button on long collection and product pages without touching theme code — and who can treat infinite scroll as a separate $2.99-a-month decision rather than part of the same install. Skip it if you run a large catalogue that depends on paginated collection URLs being crawled, your theme already ships its own load-more or filtering behaviour, or you need conversion work rather than navigation polish — this only changes how the page scrolls.

How much does Scrolly cost?

(read 2026-08-25 and re-read 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/custom-scroll-to-top) Two plans now, where there was one. On 25 August 2026 the listing carried no paid tier, no usage meter and no surcharge — the pricing block most App Store listings use to sell an upgrade was simply absent. On 19 September 2026 it carries a Free Plan and an Unlimited Plan at $2.99 a month, or $25.11 a year with a 30% saving and a 7-day free trial. The split does not fall where the app’s name suggests. Free keeps the scroll-to-top button and its styling: multiple presets, button colour and hover colour, and the option to hide it on the mobile storefront. Unlimited adds infinite scrolling and the load-more button, plus uploading your own SVG icon for the button. So the feature the app is named after, and the one the first three of the listing’s five selling points describe, is now the paid half. All charges are billed in USD every 30 days. The app has been on the App Store since March 2020, carries Shopify’s Built for Shopify badge — the store’s own bar for performance, design and integration — and the listing names eleven interface languages. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Scrolly?

The two features carry very different risk, the app presents them as one install, and since August the money has been split across them in a way the name does not warn you about. Infinite scroll replaces the paginated collection URLs a crawler uses to walk a large catalogue, pushes your footer permanently out of reach, and on some themes collides with the load-more or filtering logic already in the theme — that is a merchandising decision, not a styling toggle. The app also edits Online Store script tags and the theme, so it adds a third-party script to every page and an uninstall can leave remnants. What changed is which half you pay for. Read on 19 September 2026, the free plan keeps the scroll-to-top button and infinite scroll sits on the $2.99 Unlimited plan, where on 25 August the whole app was free. The amount is trivial; the shape is not. The half that can quietly alter how your collection pages are crawled is now the half with a billing relationship behind it, and the seven-day trial is the only window in which you will find out what it does to your store before the charge starts. Anything written about this app before September — including a free-forever recommendation — describes an install that no longer exists.

Seamless.ai

Is Seamless.ai worth it?

Seamless.ai is genuinely best for teams that want a huge real-time contact database and AI list-building for less than ZoomInfo, and can tolerate cleaning the data. Skip it if data accuracy is your top priority (ZoomInfo bounces far less), or you want simple no-contract pricing — the bounce rates and auto-renewal bite.

How much does Seamless.ai cost?

(read 2026-09-07 on seamless.ai/pricing and seamless.ai/llms.txt) Still no published amount above the free plan, in a fourth reading. Free: 1 user, 50 credits. Pro: 'Per User', unlimited exports, annual credit packages, '1 Credits = Phone + Email', Contact sales. Enterprise: unlimited users, unlimited exports, custom packages, customer success and enterprise support, Contact sales. The only quantity they publish above Free is in the FAQ: Pro plans start at 10,000 annual credits, and custom accounts get a daily allotment at five or more licence tiers. The FAQ also says there are no setup fees, and that 'the prices shown on this page reflect this annual discount' — on a page that shows none. Four capabilities are marked Add-on in every column, Enterprise included: AI Assistant, Data Enrichment, Autopilot and Buyer Intent Data. Third-party guides report an entry around $147 a month for roughly 250 credits and up to $150-500 per user a month; those are not Seamless's numbers, and 250 credits a month is 3,000 a year against a published Pro floor of 10,000. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Seamless.ai?

Data accuracy is the recurring complaint — independent tests put email deliverability around 74% (20–30% bounce) versus ZoomInfo's ~2–3%, so real cost per usable contact climbs. The buying experience is the other weak spot: sales-led, auto-renew with 30–60 day written cancellation, and reports of charges after a 'confirmed' cancellation.

Securify

Is Securify worth it?

Securify is genuinely best for stores seeing real fraud or bot traffic that want country, IP, VPN and email-risk rules plus automatic holds on suspicious orders, and who will review the block log rather than set and forget. Skip it if you are blocking on a hunch rather than on measured fraud — start by reading your order data, because a blocked legitimate customer never tells you they were blocked.

How much does Securify cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-20 on apps.shopify.com/easy-block-customer-ip-country) Free plan plus three paid tiers, unchanged since the readings of 18 August and 13 September 2026. Free: unlimited countries and IPs, last 1,000 visitor records, 500 blocked visitors a month. Pro $5.99 a month or $49.99 a year (30% less), Advanced $9.49 or $79.99 a year (30% less), Growth $49 or $490 a year (17% less). Trials are 3 days on Pro and Advanced and 7 days on Growth. Rating 4.6 from 95 ratings (78 five-star, four four-star, two three-star, one two-star, ten one-star). Listed as 'Country Blocker Fraud Securify' from siimple.ai, with Shopify's Built for Shopify badge and Shopify Flow actions and triggers. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Securify?

Blocking by country and IP is a blunt instrument and it cuts both ways: every rule that keeps out a fraudster also keeps out a customer travelling, using a corporate VPN, or living behind a carrier NAT. The app is honest enough to give you a live log of what it blocked, and that log is the part to actually read — a rule set nobody reviews quietly costs sales. Also worth separating in your head: blocking bots from your analytics is a reporting fix, while blocking fraud at checkout is a money fix, and the two need different rules.

Seel

Is Seel worth it?

Seel is genuinely best for stores selling final-sale, high-consideration or hard-to-size products, where return anxiety is the thing killing the order — merchants report conversion lifting around 5% and shoppers taking the option roughly 24% of the time. Skip it if your margin already absorbs returns comfortably, or you need control over what appears on your own checkout — the fee is set by Seel and shown to your customer either way.

How much does Seel cost?

Three plans on seel.com/pricing, re-read 7 September and again 19 September 2026 (on that second reading the plan cards no longer print a monthly figure at all — all three say “Contact us” — and the $99 survives only in the FAQ below them, which states it three times; the rate card and the usage caps are unchanged): Free at $0 per store per month (no monthly platform fee), Growth at $99 per store per month, Enterprise at custom pricing. Worry-Free Purchase (formerly Return Assurance), Worry-Free Delivery and Extended Warranty are listed as included on all three, so the returns-protection product stays shopper-paid: customers who add it pay roughly $2-$5, reported elsewhere as 3-5% of order value, set by Seel's algorithm. The plans differ on the AI agencies. Free is pay-as-you-go for one agency at $0.99 per resolved ticket, $0.40 per listing, 3% of attributed GMV, $5 per store review and $29 per storefront regulation scan. Growth covers all five with capped usage — up to 100 resolved tickets, 100 listings, $500 attributed GMV, one Voice of Customer report (sentiment across your brand and three competitors), up to four 5-star reviews and one storefront regulation scan — and order tracking for 2,000 orders instead of 250; overage bills at the Free rate card. Their FAQ states the subscription is fixed per store per month and that attributed GMV does not feed it. Enterprise usage scope and commercial terms sit in the merchant agreement. Insurance benefits are provided by Seel Insurance Inc. or Arch Specialty Insurance Company, with availability varying by jurisdiction and state (re-verified 2026-09-07; on 2026-08-02 the page showed no plans or rate card). Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Seel?

Two things to weigh, and neither is the price you pay — because you do not pay one. First, you cannot set the fee. Seel's algorithm prices it, so if it lands too high for your niche and shoppers stop opting in, your only lever is switching the feature off entirely. Second, the charge appears on your checkout, not Seel's: shopper-side complaints filed with the BBB describe the fee arriving in the cart with the opt-out easy to miss, and that lands on your brand. Test it as a customer before you enable it. Also check the platform list — Shopify, BigCommerce and Adobe Commerce only, with no WooCommerce, Wix or custom storefront support.

Is Selixer worth it?

Selixer is genuinely best for Shopify fashion and apparel brands with real ad spend that want profit per SKU and per campaign in one place, and can carry the $299 tier where those features actually live. Skip it if your store is small enough that a spreadsheet still works, you need more than three connected ad accounts without paying $399, or you want a longer public track record than an app launched in May 2026 with one review.

How much does Selixer cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/selixer; unchanged since 10 September 2026) Three tiers, no free plan, each with a 14-day free trial. Essence $149 a month: two user seats, one connected ad platform, a year of historical data, the ad dashboard with campaigns and trends, stockout, overstock and dead-stock views, an inventory health score, 500 AI credits with top-ups from $25, and a site speed analyzer. Catalyst $299 a month adds four seats, two ad platforms and no date cap on history, the full True Profit waterfall, POAS, CAC and product-level ad revenue, per-product P&L and an SKU action matrix, a WhatsApp inbox with AI agent and campaigns, 50,000 emails a month with branded invoices, and 2,000 AI credits. Aether $399 a month adds eight seats, three ad platforms, all nine profit-leak detectors, multi-touch attribution and ad cohorts, demand forecasting and return on inventory, RFM scoring and retention cohorts, automations with 200,000 emails a month, and 3,000 AI credits. The listing publishes no annual rate, so all three are monthly. Charges are billed in USD, and the listing files recurring and usage-based charges together on the same 30-day cycle — the AI credits are the usage part, with top-ups starting at $25. Developer Akaame Export Private Limited; the app launched 19 May 2026 and carries a single App Store review. Two details on the same page as the plans: the entry card is labelled Essance while the Catalyst card's feature list calls the same tier Essence, and the App Store record still shows a single five-star review, from a merchant who had used the app for 15 days. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Selixer?

Read the feature lists rather than the prices and the entry tier stops looking like the product. Essence at $149 a month gives you two seats, one connected ad platform, a year of history and an inventory health score. The full True Profit waterfall, the per-product P&L and the POAS and CAC tracking — the reason anyone installs a profit dashboard — all start on Catalyst at $299. So the real price of what this app is sold on is double the headline. The ad-platform caps decide the tier as much as the features do: one, then two, then three. If you run Meta, Google and TikTok you are on the $399 plan for connectivity alone, whatever your revenue looks like. The monthly figure is also not the whole bill. Each plan carries an AI credit allowance — 500, 2,000 and 3,000 — and the listing sells top-ups from $25, with usage-based charges billed on the same 30-day cycle. Find out what spends a credit before you budget around the headline. And this is a new app. It launched on 19 May 2026 and has one public review. There is nothing bad in the record, but there is barely any record, and this is a tool you hand your cost prices, your ad spend and your margins to. Use the 14-day trial to reconcile its numbers against a month you have already closed in your own books before you trust a dashboard you cannot yet audit.

Selleasy

Is Selleasy worth it?

Selleasy is genuinely best for shopify stores that want bundles, add-ons, cart funnels and post-purchase offers out of one app and would rather be billed on order volume than hand over a share of the upsell revenue — and small stores in particular, since under 50 orders a month the full strategy set costs nothing. Skip it if you are on Shopify Plus and came for checkout upsells, or you want AI recommendations at any real volume: both start at Pro, $49 a month, which the App Store listing never shows — and a high-order store that runs no upsells still pays the top Starter step.

How much does Selleasy cost?

(prices read 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/upsell-cross-sell-kit-1 and on logbase.io/products/shopify-upsell-app-selleasy) Billed in USD. The App Store listing shows one ladder, Starter, and it is priced by your store's total monthly order count rather than by anything the app does: free up to 50 orders a month, $9 from 51 to 500, $19 from 501 to 1,000, and $29 above 1,000. All four steps carry the same 18 upsell and cross-sell strategies, 50 free AI recommendations, free setup on a call and chat, email and Zoom support, with a 30-day free trial on the paid steps. Logbase's own pricing page adds two tiers the listing does not show. Pro is $49 a month or $499 a year — $42 a month, which the site says saves $89 — and lifts the order limit entirely while adding 1,000 AI recommendations a month, an AI campaign optimizer, checkout upsells for Shopify Plus, advanced campaign targeting and metafield bulk recommendations. Max is $99 a month or $1,009 a year — $84 a month, saving $179 — adding 2,500 AI recommendations a month, advanced customization, a rules engine, an AOV advisor and priority support. An Enterprise tier is quoted on request. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Selleasy?

The meter is your whole store, not the app. Every Starter tier counts total store orders, so the free plan's 50-order ceiling is reached by any shop doing two orders a day whether or not a single upsell ever fired — and, read the other way, a 5,000-order store running one quiet bundle pays the top step of the ladder all the same. That cuts both ways and it is cheap in either direction, but it is not the meter most people assume they are signing up to. Second, the App Store listing shows only the Starter ladder, so it reads as though $29 is the ceiling. It is not. Pro at $49 and Max at $99 exist only on logbase.io, and that is where AI recommendations at volume and checkout upsells for Shopify Plus sit — the two upgrades a growing store is most likely to want. Third, every Starter tier says '50 free AI recommendations' with no period attached, while Pro says '1,000 AI recommendations/month' and Max says '2,500 AI recommendations/month'. The contrast in wording suggests the 50 is a one-off allowance rather than a monthly one, but neither page says so outright. Ask before you plan around it. And treat the vendor's headline claims as claims: the 20% AOV increase and the 40,000+ brands are Logbase's own figures on its own site, with no methodology attached to either.

Seller Investigators

Is Seller Investigators worth it?

Seller Investigators is genuinely best for established FBA sellers with enough inventory movement that discrepancies add up and nobody in-house has time to file case-by-case claims — the contingency model means an audit costs you nothing but the access you grant. Skip it if you are a small seller whose monthly discrepancies are modest, where 25% of a small recovery buys less than the hour it takes to file yourself. Also skip it until you have asked what share of the claim Amazon would have paid automatically, because that is the part of the bill that buys you nothing.

How much does Seller Investigators cost?

(2026-08-15, read on their own site) One number, and it is the whole model: a 25% commission, charged only after Amazon has deposited recovered funds in your account. We found it stated twice. Once on the home page — “only pay a 25% commission fee when your money is back with you” — and again in the FAQ: “no risk or upfront commitment, with a 25% recovery fee only after Amazon deposits recovered funds into your account”. The audit is free, takes 48 hours and carries no obligation. There is no subscription and no /pricing page, because there is nothing else to price. Cases they say they cover fall into five groups: inbound shipments (cancelled shipments, receiving discrepancies, carrier damage), items lost in transit or in the warehouse, items damaged or disposed of by Amazon, customer returns (refunds not returned within 60 days, overpayments, the wrong item returned, chargebacks), and overages and discrepancies (removal orders, incorrect weights or dimensions, overcharged orders); unfair reimbursement appears as a sub-case under both the lost and the damaged group. Re-read 29 August 2026: the 25% figure, the free 48-hour audit and the absence of any subscription are unchanged. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Seller Investigators?

Contingency pricing is the honest kind — you pay only out of money that arrived — but 25% of a recovery is not the same as 25% of a profit, and there is one question that decides whether this is worth it for you. Amazon reimburses some categories automatically, and its policies on that have changed more than once. So ask, before you sign: which of these cases would Amazon have settled on its own within the claim window, and what exactly is the 25% charged on — the gross amount recovered, or what is left after Amazon's own fees? A free audit that finds $20,000 sounds decisive until you learn how much of it was already on its way. Ask for the split, in writing, before the audit turns into an engagement.

Seller Snap

Is Seller Snap worth it?

Seller Snap is genuinely best for Amazon and Walmart sellers past the hobby stage who compete for the Buy Box on a catalog of up to a few thousand SKUs, and want AI repricing and deep seller analytics in one place. The 15-day no-card trial makes it cheap to test against your own listings before any commitment. Skip it if you sell mainly outside Amazon and Walmart, since those are the only two marketplaces supported. Also skip it if your catalog and revenue are small enough that a rules-based repricer at a fraction of the price does the same job, or if what you actually need is multi-channel competitor price monitoring rather than marketplace Buy Box repricing.

How much does Seller Snap cost?

(re-verified 2026-08-26 on their own pricing page, both the monthly and the annual column; every figure below was read again on that date and none of them had moved since 24 Jul 2026) There are four tiers, and the axis that sets your price is capacity, not features. All four list the same six feature groups: Amazon & Walmart, AI repricing technology, min & max calculation, analytics, connectivity and integrations. The four tiers are set out above; what the page does not tell you is what each step actually buys. Accelerator doubles your revenue ceiling and leaves the SKU count alone, and Standard does the reverse — fifteen times the catalogue with the ceiling removed — while the seller ID and user counts never move at all. So the middle tier is for turnover and the top tier is for range, and a shop that needs neither is paying for the other one. The revenue ceilings themselves are printed without any period attached; Seller Snap told us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both are calculated per month, so read them as $15,000 and $30,000 a month. Annual billing saves a flat $900 a year on both Accelerator and Standard — the same money, but 30 percent off the smaller plan against 15 percent off the larger one. Every tier carries a 15-day trial with no credit card, and in the monthly view each price is labelled 'Starting at'. Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that readers coming through our link get 10% off for their first three months; it runs through the link, there is no code to enter. Update: asked directly, Seller Snap confirmed by email on 24 July 2026 that the Starter and Accelerator revenue caps are calculated per month. Their pricing page still does not say so — we are passing on the vendor's answer, not something you can verify on the page yourself. One thing on the page has changed and it is not a price: a banner above the plans offers 'your first month for only $1 when you subscribe before 2026', a deadline that had already passed when we read it on 26 Aug 2026, so treat it as decoration rather than an offer until support confirms it. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Seller Snap?

Read the caps before you read the prices, because the caps are what you are actually buying. Two of them deserve scrutiny. First, the revenue limits — $15,000 on Starter, $30,000 on Accelerator — are printed with no period attached on the pricing page. We asked, and Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both caps are calculated per month. That is the reading that costs you money. $15,000 a month is roughly $500 a day, so a seller who already clears that sits above Starter before signing up — and $30,000 a month puts the ceiling of Accelerator within reach of a shop doing $1,000 a day. Measure your own monthly revenue against the tier first, because the page will not do it for you. Second, the SKU limit sits at 1,000 on both of the lower tiers, so catalog growth alone — not revenue, not users — can push you up a step. And the steps are steep: leaving Accelerator for Standard means $425/month annually or $500 monthly, roughly 2.4 times what you were paying, for capacity rather than for any feature you did not already have. The cheapest door is also not quite $100: Starter is annual-billing only, so the lowest month-to-month entry into the product is $250/month. Finally, 'Starting at' appears above every monthly price on the vendor's own page — treat all of these as floors and confirm your own quote. Worth checking first, though: Amazon already includes a rule-based repricer. Automate Pricing comes with the Professional selling plan and supports rules such as Competitive Featured Offer and Competitive Lowest Price with a seller-set price floor, so if your problem is simply matching the competitive price without going below cost, test that before paying for anything. And note what sets your tier: their FAQ says pricing follows the total number of SKUs in your Seller Central account, not the active ones, so a dormant catalogue costs you money. One more thing to time correctly. In September 2026 Seller Snap began telling affiliates that its most advanced repricing engine yet had just launched, built on the premise that Amazon no longer awards one Buy Box but thousands of local ones, buyer by buyer and city by city. Their own repricing-engine page, read on 3 Sep 2026, is more careful than that: it says a redesigned app today, a new repricing engine coming soon, and it offers a waitlist and an early-access form rather than the engine itself. What has actually shipped is the redesigned app — a live Buy Box filter at SKU level, one preset across every store, repricing from a phone, and historical inventory value tracked over time. The local Buy Box logic sits behind that, still ahead of the product rather than in it. So judge the subscription on what the app does today; if the local pricing engine is the reason you are signing up, ask support for a ship date in writing before you pay for a year of it.

SEOKart

Is SEOKart worth it?

SEOKart is genuinely best for Shopify or BigCommerce merchants with a few hundred to a few thousand products who want on-page SEO cleaned up in bulk — meta tags, image alt text and file names, URLs, JSON-LD schema, 404s and redirects, image compression for page speed — and who would rather have a keyword rank tracker in the same app than pay for a second subscription. Skip it if you need keyword research, backlink data or content strategy, none of which this does; or you want daily rank checks, because the tracker runs monthly on Free and weekly above it. A small catalogue is not a reason to skip the app: if the free plan's 50 pages already cover you, the answer is to stay on Free, which the vendor says has no time limit.

How much does SEOKart cost?

(price read 2026-09-12, re-verified 2026-09-15) Two publishers, and they do not publish the same ladder. The Shopify listing, https://apps.shopify.com/seokart, bills in USD and recurs every 30 days through Shopify, with four fixed tiers. Free covers 50 pages of one-click AI optimisation, 10 tracked keywords checked monthly, 50 image optimisations and 50 pages of bulk editing, with limited rich snippets. Pro is $20 a month or $216 a year for 1,000 products with 100 tracked keywords checked weekly, unlimited image and bulk optimisation, full rich snippets, a 404 fixer and Cruise Control auto-SEO. Plus is $30 a month or $324 a year for 5,000 products, Max $40 or $432 for 10,000, and annual billing saves 10% on all three. On those four cards the tracked-keyword line never moves off 100 and the feature lists above Pro are word for word identical. The vendor's own page sells the same app as one configurable Pro plan and runs much further. Under the APP tab on https://seokart.com/pricing (read 15 September 2026) the card carries two dropdowns. Catalogue size, priced at the base 100 keywords: 1,000 products $20 a month, 5,000 $30, 10,000 $40, 25,000 $75, 50,000 $100, 100,000 $150, 500,000 $300, 1,000,000 $500 and 2,000,000 $800. Tracked keywords are the second dropdown and run 100, 200, 300, 400, 500. That step is charged, and it costs more the larger the catalogue: on 1,000 products the five choices are $20, $30, $40, $50 and $60 a month, and on 10,000 products they are $40, $60, $80, $100 and $120. So 500 keywords on a 10,000-product store is $120 a month, three times the $40 the Shopify card presents as the top of the range. The first three catalogue rungs match the Shopify tiers exactly; what the listing leaves out is everything above 10,000 products and the keyword dropdown altogether. The same vendor page also sells a managed SEO service at $799, $1,299 and $1,949 a month (read 14 September 2026). That is a separate, optional service alongside the app, and it is what the free SEO consultancy in the plan table opens the door to. The app is sold for BigCommerce too: that listing, https://www.bigcommerce.com/apps/seokart/ (read 14 September 2026, last updated there 2 September 2026), publishes a $20 a month recurring fee, no upfront charge and a 10-day free trial. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with SEOKart?

Every plan, free included, lists free SEO consultancy, and it is worth knowing what sits next to it. seokart.com sells a managed SEO service at $799, $1,299 and $1,949 a month (read 14 September 2026). That is a separate, optional service rather than a tier of the app, and a free consultation is the natural place for a conversation about it to start. The evidence base is decent rather than deep: 69 reviews on 12 September 2026, launched 4 June 2020, developer Activant Solutions Pvt Ltd in Jaipur. The 5.0 average hides the shape — 67 five-star reviews and two one-star, with nothing in between. Then the two limits that decide whether this is the right tool. The rank tracker checks monthly on Free and weekly on Pro and above, so it is a trend line, not a daily rank check, and 100 tracked keywords is what every Shopify plan card publishes, but that is not the ceiling: the vendor's own configurator at seokart.com/pricing sells 200 to 500 tracked keywords as a priced step, $10 a month per extra 100 on a 1,000-product store and $20 a step on a 10,000-product one (read 15 September 2026). And one-click AI optimisation writes meta titles and descriptions in bulk: that is the whole appeal. This review is researched rather than hands-on, so take the next line as general practice with any bulk AI writer and not as something we watched SEOKart produce -- budget a pass for reading what it wrote on your best-selling pages before you let Cruise Control run unattended. The app also needs access to products, store analytics and the Online Store, plus blog contributor data.

SEOmatic

Is SEOmatic worth it?

SEOmatic is genuinely best for Shopify stores under 5,000 products that want image compression, alt text, auto-generated meta tags, schema and sitemaps from one app on a flat monthly fee, and would rather not pay per AI credit. Skip it if your catalogue is larger than 5,000 products, or you want the safest bet in a category where three rivals on the same page carry 850 to 2,400 reviews at 4.9-5.0 against this app's 4.4 over 114.

How much does SEOmatic cost?

(read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/minifier and on seomatic.io) Four tiers, and the only thing that changes between the three paid ones is how many products they cover. Free: 10 products, 50 image optimisations, AI SEO audit, auto-pilot AI meta title and description, schema markup, HTML sitemap. Starter $15 a month or $144 a year (save 20%): 500 products, unlimited image optimiser, broken links, XML and HTML sitemaps, 14-day free trial. Basic $25 a month or $240 a year: 2,000 products. Advanced $40 a month or $384 a year: 5,000 products. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. The vendor's own pricing page at seomatic.io publishes the identical ladder, which is worth noting because the two often disagree — here they do not. There is no plan above 5,000 products on either page, so a larger catalogue has no listed price at all. Developer Aheadworks, 12495 S Parkland Bay Trail, Parkland, Florida; the app launched 18 August 2015 and carries a 4.4 average over 114 App Store reviews, and it holds Shopify's 'Built for Shopify' badge. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with SEOmatic?

This app is eleven years old and has 114 reviews. That is the number to sit with. On the same listing page Shopify shows three direct rivals. SEOLab is 5.0 over 2,368 reviews and free, Tiny SEO 5.0 over 2,261 and free to install, and Smart SEO 4.9 over 851 with a free plan. All three carry between seven and twenty times the review volume, all are rated higher, and none of them charges by product count. SEOmatic's 4.4 is a real rating from real merchants, but it is the weakest track record on its own page. The distribution behind that 4.4 matters too: 81% five stars against 8% one star, with almost nothing in the middle. The most substantial recent review, from March 2025, is a merchant of six months saying it appears to work on images and nothing else, and that support is difficult and slow. The vendor replied that the reports do exist, and asked them to get in touch. An older one-star from a merchant who lasted seventeen minutes reads 'Paid for it to tell me 0% savings'. Both are about the same thing — what the app actually did after installation was not visible to the person paying for it. And the product cap is a hard ceiling, not a soft one. There is no tier above 5,000 products on the listing or on seomatic.io, so if your catalogue is larger than that, the published ladder simply does not have a row for you.

Serpstat

Is Serpstat worth it?

Serpstat is genuinely best for solo SEOs and small in-house teams who want the whole workflow — keywords, rankings, audit, competitors — under one subscription at roughly a third of what the incumbents charge, and who will judge the data on their own market during the trial. Skip it if your work depends on deep backlink analysis, since the 10,000 results per report ceiling does not move no matter which tier you buy; or you need more than three seats, because seats are not sold separately and the next tier roughly doubles the bill.

How much does Serpstat cost?

(2026-07-24, read on their own pricing page) Four plans, and the page opens on the annual view — so the first number you see is not the month-to-month price. Individual $69/month, or $50 on annual billing. Team $129, or $100 annually. Team x2 $209, or $169. Agency $499, or $410. There is a hidden middle step: two dropdowns inside the Team column (position checks 50,000 or 99,999, API credits 200,000 or 400,000) move Team to $169/month monthly or $135 annually, so Team is really three price points. Seats are capped rather than sold: Individual is single-user, Team 3, Team x2 6, Agency 30, and no per-seat price is published anywhere — a fourth user means the next tier. The limits matter more than the prices: 100 searches a day on Individual (500 / 1,000 / 5,000 above it), export rows 50,000 a month, and no API at all on the entry plan. The 7-day trial takes a card, charges $1 to verify, turns on auto-renewal and bills the plan after seven days unless you cancel. Re-verified 2026-08-26: the four annual prices are unchanged, and the page now heads the table with 'save up to 27% with annual discount' and prints the saving per plan — $228, $348, $484 and $1,068 a year. That is the arithmetic that turns $50, $100, $169 and $410 back into $69, $129, $209 and $499, which matters because the monthly column itself is not in the page's HTML at all; only the annual one renders. The comparison table still carries the two-value Team column (position checks 50,000 or 99,999, API credits 200,000 or 400,000), so the hidden middle step is still there, but its price is printed nowhere on the page today. Three limits worth reading before anyone picks Individual: Site Audit does no JavaScript rendering on that plan, it scans at most 5,000 pages, and its data retention figure is 2 where Team gets 10 and Agency 100. Re-verified 2026-09-19 on the same page: the four annual figures, the four annual savings and the two-value Team column are all unchanged, as are the seat caps of 1, 3, 6 and 30 and the seven-day trial with its $1 card verification and automatic renewal. What is new on the page is what the plans now sell rather than what they cost — Team upward advertises a ChatGPT and Claude integration over MCP and an AI Overview brand-opportunities report, and a separate LLM Brand Monitor is promoted underneath the plans with its own free scan and no price attached to it. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Serpstat?

The thing you are actually buying is data coverage, and that is the one thing you cannot verify — Serpstat's own published figures do not agree with each other. Re-read on 24 July 2026, their homepage says 529 billion backlinks, their data hub says 1.1 trillion, and their backlinks page says 1.7 trillion in the prose while its own spec block on that same page says 1.1 trillion. The keyword count reads 8.62 billion on one page and 7.46 billion on another. That is not evidence the data is thin; it is evidence that these numbers cannot serve as a basis for your decision. Judge it on your own searches during the trial instead. Two other things to weigh. Backlink reports are capped at 10,000 results per report on Team, Team x2 and Agency alike, so paying from $129 to $499 buys more of everything except a deeper backlink report. And 'maximum pages to scan' in a single crawl (5,000 / 25,000 / 50,000) is a far smaller number than the monthly 'pages to audit' allowance it sits next to.

Shipdock

Is Shipdock worth it?

Shipdock is genuinely best for Shopify merchants shipping in Central and Eastern Europe who want pickup points, multi-carrier label printing and cash-on-delivery tracking in one app rather than one integration per carrier — and who are on Shopify Plus, where the pickup-point picker sits inside checkout instead of after it. Skip it if your carriers are not in its list, which is the first thing to check, since the app's centre of gravity is Packeta and the Central European networks; or you need a label only occasionally, when a CSV export and your carrier's portal cost nothing.

How much does Shipdock cost?

(re-read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/packeta) Three tiers, no free plan, every amount unchanged since 22 August 2026, and the entry tier still names its own limitation. Lite is $9.99 a month or $107.88 a year and is labelled 'only CSV': pickup point and home delivery, an email reminder, the pickup-point widget on the thank-you and order-status pages, unlimited carriers across more than twenty, and an order export to custom CSV. Basic is $14.99 or $161.89 a year and is the first tier that prints shipping labels, adding parcels created automatically after fulfilment and cash-on-delivery payment tracking. Shopify Plus is $24.99 or $269.89 and moves the pickup-point widget into the checkout itself rather than the pages after it. Annual billing saves a stated 10% on each. Trials are five days on Lite and Basic and ten on Plus. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. The listing now names its carriers rather than counting them: Packeta, Balíkovna, DPD, Magyar Posta, InPost, DHL24, Posti, GLS and myGLS, Omniva, Foxpost, PPL, One, Telli, Eserviss, Esiunt, Slovenská pošta, Česká pošta, Fan Courier, Easyship, Econt and PostNord. Developer happyapps.cz; the app sits in Shopify's delivery and pickup category, is offered in English and Czech, and carries 42 reviews at a 5.0 rating — the same total as in August, but now with every one of the 42 at five stars where our earlier reading recorded one at four. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Shipdock?

Read the carrier list against your own country before anything else. The listing slug is 'packeta', the developer is happyapps.cz, and cash-on-delivery tracking is a headline feature — all three point at Central and Eastern Europe, where Packeta and Zásilkovna are everyday carriers and COD is a normal way to pay. More than twenty carriers are supported, but a US or UK merchant should confirm theirs is among them before the five-day trial starts. The second thing is the trial length against the job. Five days on Lite and Basic is short for a shipping integration, because the test that matters is a real order going out with a real label to a real address. Install it on a day you are actually shipping, not on a quiet Sunday.

Shorby

Is Shorby worth it?

Shorby is genuinely best for creators and businesses that sell via messenger conversations or retarget link-in-bio traffic with ad pixels. Skip it if you just need a links page (free tools abound), or your audience doesn't click through to chat apps.

How much does Shorby cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-06 at dash.shorby.com/pricing) Three paid plans, no free plan on the table. Rocket $15/mo, or $12/mo billed annually ($36 off the year); Pro $29/mo, or $24/mo annually ($60 off); Agency $99/mo, or $82/mo annually ($204 off). Pages included: 5 on Rocket, 50 on Pro, 250 on Agency, with Agency adding Projects and Teams from three up. Direct messenger buttons, Click Insights and Shor Rewards are on all three; Google Analytics, custom domains (per project) and Dynamic Feeds (5 per page) start at Pro. The table states all prices are in USD and all sales are final. Note that the marketing site's own /pricing/ page renders nothing — this table is only reachable at dash.shorby.com. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Shorby?

In a category where the market leader has a generous free plan, Shorby charges from day one, so it has to earn the gap. Its case rests on two genuinely differentiated features: messenger deep-links, one tap into WhatsApp/Telegram chats, and retargeting pixels firing on every click. If you use neither, Linktree's free tier wins; if messenger-first selling or ad retargeting is your funnel, the $15 pays for itself.

Signitic

Is Signitic worth it?

Signitic is genuinely best for European organisations of roughly twenty people and up, on Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, that want every signature centrally controlled and the banner slot run as a measurable campaign channel — and that need EU hosting and ISO 27001 on the record. Skip it if you have fewer than twenty employees, where the free plan is the whole offer and the paid tier cannot be bought below its 20-licence minimum, or your people sit on Outlook 2013-2021 or Apple Mail and would land on the agent with its plain signatures rather than the add-in.

How much does Signitic cost?

(price read 2026-09-14) Signitic's own pricing page, read in euros from a European connection, carries three tiers. Free covers organisations up to 19 employees and gives one signature template, one banner campaign, and a Signitic badge at the bottom of every signature that the plan does not let you remove. The paid tier — the card the page marks Most popular — is €1 per user with a minimum of 20 licences, and it is where the caps come off: unlimited signature templates, unlimited banner campaigns, a custom subdomain for deliverability, multi-entity segmentation, A/B testing with click statistics, and no badge. That card prints the euro and the word user but never a period; the ROI calculator further down the same page settles it, pricing 100 employees at 1 200 € a year, which is twelve euros per user per year — so the euro is monthly, and the 20-licence minimum puts the real floor at twenty euros a month. The third tier is Custom and carries no public figure: advanced permission management, campaign targeting from CRM lists, HRIS/SFTP integration, vCard digital business cards and a dedicated support team all sit behind a quote. Registered non-profits are offered 50% off subject to an eligibility check. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Signitic?

The homepage sells deployment 'without going through IT', and Signitic's own help centre contradicts that on every path in. Connecting Google Workspace is possible only from the Super Admin profile, and if that admin ever changes you have to reconnect or call support. Microsoft 365 needs an Azure Active Directory administrator account. Rolling out the Outlook add-in — the fuller of the two Microsoft options — needs a Microsoft 365 Global Administrator plus the Exchange Administrator role carrying the ReadWriteMailbox permission, must not be installed by end users themselves, and can take up to 72 hours to appear in people's Outlook. Marketing does keep the keys afterwards, which is the real promise; it does not get them without IT first. The add-in also needs a Microsoft 365 Outlook licence at version 16.0.14026.20000 or later, so Outlook 2013 to 2021 and Apple Mail fall back to the Signitic agent, which pushes plain signatures instead.

Similarweb

Is Similarweb worth it?

Similarweb is genuinely best for a single analyst or marketer who needs competitor traffic and channel estimates often enough to justify $125 a month, and teams who are prepared to negotiate an annual contract for more than one seat. Skip it if you want a quick check on one competitor — the free tier and public estimates cover that, and the cheapest paid plan is $125 a month for a single user.

How much does Similarweb cost?

(read 2026-08-25 on their own pricing page) The entrepreneur plans are published: $125 per month on annual billing for Competitive Intelligence, $333 for Competitive Intel & SEO & AEO, and $542 for Competitive Intel, SEO & AEO & Ads — or $199, $399 and $649 respectively on monthly billing, each for a single user. Included history differs by plan and is easy to miss: 3 months on the entry plan, 6 months on the two above it. What is not published is the business and enterprise tab: it carries no figure at all and routes every tier to 'Talk to sales' for a custom package, and the FAQ repeats that premium features require one. A free trial is offered without a stated length. Up to 37 months of data history is sold as an add-on rather than an inclusion, and API access is either standalone or inside a custom package. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Similarweb?

Similarweb does publish a price — $125 a month for one seat on annual billing, or $199 if you pay monthly. What it does not publish is anything above one seat: the business and enterprise tab carries no figure at all and routes straight to a sales call, where the number depends on what they think you can pay. So the decision splits in two. One analyst can price this today and start a trial without speaking to anyone. A team walks into a negotiation, and should walk in with a ceiling already written down — plus the two line items priced apart from the seats: 37 months of data history is an add-on, and API access is quoted separately.

Skip To Checkout

Is Skip To Checkout worth it?

Skip To Checkout is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want a free sticky buy button, or who need to hide add-to-cart and express-payment buttons on products they list online but sell in person. Skip it if your cart page carries shipping thresholds, discount codes or upsells you depend on, you manage the store on add-to-cart rate and cannot afford to lose that signal, or you are unwilling to grant read and write access to customers, products and analytics for a display widget.

How much does Skip To Checkout cost?

(read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/cart-auto-update) Free, and free is the only plan. The listing carries no pricing table at all: no paid tier, no usage meter and no surcharge tied to your Shopify plan. The app has been on the App Store since 29 November 2019 and carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge, which is the store's own bar for performance, design and integration. One of the 34 reviews alleges being billed twice, which is worth knowing about an app the listing prices at nothing; we cannot verify that claim from the outside, and the listing shows no charge to make. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Skip To Checkout?

The cart skip blinds the measurement you would use to judge it. The vendor's own help article confirms that bypassing Add To Cart and Start Checkout makes your add-to-cart rate read lower, and recommends watching overall sales trends instead — so the feature is sold on conversion while switching off the funnel that would show it. Skipping the cart also bypasses the page where shipping thresholds, discount codes and cart upsells normally work. For a free widget the permissions are broad: view and edit customers, products, store analytics, Shopify Functions and the online store, plus customer device and activity data. And because there is no paid tier there is no support contract behind it; what you get is the vendor's goodwill, which a six-year run and a 4.6 average suggest is real, but is not something you can buy more of. The app also carries at least three different names across the listing, the help centre index and its own setup article, which makes it harder to know what you are running.

Smartli

Is Smartli worth it?

Smartli is genuinely best for e-commerce sellers who want an affordable all-in-one AI suite to draft product listings, ad copy, SEO text and basic brand assets in one place. Skip it if you need best-in-class depth in one area (a specialist copy or image tool), or you won't edit and fact-check AI output before it ships.

How much does Smartli cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-11 on smartli.ai/pricing; Monthly and Yearly tabs both unchanged since 5 Aug 2026) Monthly: Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99, Unicorn $299, each with a 7-day free trial. Switch to annual billing and Starter disappears from the table; the rest become Pro $24/mo (billed annually at $288), Empire $57/mo ($684) and Unicorn $79/mo ($948). Starter was $29/mo when we first checked, so the entry price has gone up. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Smartli?

Smartli bundles nine AI tools — copy, SEO, images, logos — into one suite, and that breadth is also the honest catch: each individual tool is competent rather than best-in-class, so a team that leans hard on one job may outgrow it toward a specialist. And like all AI copy, its product descriptions and ad copy need a human edit and a fact-check — never publish specs or claims it invents about your product. For a store that wants many content jobs handled cheaply in one place, it's efficient.

Smarty Discounts

Is Smarty Discounts worth it?

Smarty Discounts is genuinely best for Shopify merchants whose promotions have outgrown the native discount engine — capped amounts, a fixed amount that behaves correctly in several currencies, tiers by quantity, subtotal or weight, BXGY, gifts, mix-and-match — and who want to build them with rules rather than with a developer, targeting by product, customer, cart, market, country or company. Skip it if your promotions are ordinary percentage or fixed-amount codes, which Shopify's built-in discounts already do for free; or you want a long support and reliability record before a young app gets write access to the discounts in your checkout.

How much does Smarty Discounts cost?

(read 2026-09-04 on apps.shopify.com/smarty-discount) Three tiers, all billed in USD and recurring every 30 days. Forever Free costs nothing, Lite is $9.99 a month or $99.99 a year, and Pro is $25.99 a month or $259.99 a year; the annual price on both paid tiers saves 17%, and both carry a 7-day free trial. What you are buying is capability, not volume: there is no order cap, no revenue meter and no surcharge tied to your Shopify plan anywhere in the block. Free covers product and order discounts with basic targeting and what the listing itself calls low support. Lite adds shipping and mix-and-match discounts, enhanced targeting and priority support. Pro unlocks every discount type, every targeting rule, active time periods and free shipping on a single rule. One detail in the plan table is worth reading twice, because it is unusual and it is in your favour: each tier gives unlimited discounts at its own level plus up to two at the level above. On Free you can build two Lite-grade discounts, on Lite two Pro-grade ones. That is a working trial of the next tier rather than a locked door, and it means you can prove the rule you actually need before you pay for it. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Smarty Discounts?

The evidence base is thin. The app launched on 14 January 2025 and carries six reviews as of 4 September 2026 — all five stars, but six is not a track record, and the vendor, Neezon, is a small developer in Ho Chi Minh City rather than a company with a support contract behind it. The listing is unusually candid about what that means at the bottom of the ladder: the free plan's own feature list says low support. Add to that what the app needs to do its job. The data-access panel says it reads customer data flagged as sensitive and can view and edit customers, products, discounts and the Online Store, which is the access any discount engine needs but is still broad. And because the ladder gates discount types rather than volume, the plan you land on is decided by the one rule you cannot live without: if the campaign you have in mind needs time-period scheduling or free shipping on a single rule, you are on Pro at $25.99 regardless of how few discounts you run.

Social Bar

Is Social Bar worth it?

Social Bar is genuinely best for Shopify merchants who want branded social icons and a WhatsApp chat button on product pages without touching theme code, and who will use the built-in click counter to check whether anyone taps them. Skip it if your theme already places social links where you need them, you are unwilling to pay a recurring fee for a display element, or you are looking for real social proof such as reviews, user content or engagement analytics rather than a row of icons.

How much does Social Bar cost?

(read 2026-09-18 on apps.shopify.com/sticky-social-media-icons-bar) Two plans, and the free one is not the one you will be on. Development is free but the listing limits it explicitly to development and partner stores, with billing activated on upgrade — so a real storefront does not run on it. The Monthly Plan is $4.99 a month, or $41.88 a year which the listing presents as a 30 percent saving, after a 7-day free trial. All charges are billed in USD and recurring charges are invoiced every 30 days. The app has been on the App Store since 27 April 2020 and carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Social Bar?

This is a styling subscription, and the listing's own framing oversells it: social icons and share buttons build no trust on their own, and 'boost sales with social proof' is a claim the app has no way to support. The free plan is free in a way that will not help you, since it is restricted to development and partner stores, so any live store is on $4.99 a month or $41.88 a year for something most themes already do in the footer. The 5.0 average deserves reading rather than trusting: two of the three reviews on the listing were written after 11 and 13 minutes of use and praise setup rather than results, while the one longer-running reviewer reports that icon placement is limited and the app is tricky to figure out at first. And more than 80 platform options mainly tempts you to advertise accounts you no longer maintain.

SocialBee

Is SocialBee worth it?

SocialBee is genuinely best for solo marketers and small agencies who post to several networks on a schedule and want evergreen recycling rather than a queue that empties. Skip it if you post to one or two networks by hand and are happy doing it, because the value here is category-based recycling across many profiles and that only pays back at volume.

How much does SocialBee cost?

(2026-08-30, read on their own pricing page) Bootstrap $29/month ($290 a year, 16% off): 5 profiles, 1 workspace, 1 user. Accelerate $49/month ($490 a year): 10 profiles, 1 workspace, 1 user. Pro $99/month ($990 a year): 25 profiles, 5 workspaces, 3 users per workspace. Agency tiers billed monthly: Pro50 $179, Pro100 $329, Pro150 $449 for 50, 100 and 150 profiles, with 10, 20 and 30 workspaces and 5 users per workspace; billed yearly they are $149.20, $274.20 and $374.20 a month. Add-ons: 5 extra profiles $15/month or $150/year, an extra user $10/month or $100/year, an extra workspace $10/month or $100/year. AI generation is unlimited on every tier. What is the catch with SocialBee?

You are billed per social profile, not per person, and a profile is one brand account on one network. A single business posting to Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X and TikTok has used the whole Bootstrap allowance before a second brand or a client exists. The second thing is that people cost extra on top: Bootstrap and Accelerate are single-user plans, so a two-person team on eight profiles is $49 plus $10, not $29. Count your profiles across every network first — that number, not your team size, decides the tier.

Is Spiky.ai worth it?

Meeting allowances: 3 on Free, 30 on both Plus and Pro, unlimited on Premium. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Spiky.ai?

The number to check first is the meeting cap, not the price. Plus and Pro both stop at 30 meetings per user per month, so the step from $15 to $24 buys features, not capacity. A rep taking two calls a day passes 30 in three weeks, which pushes you to Premium at $40 — nearly triple the entry price — for volume rather than capability. Price this from your team's actual call count and you will land on the right tier; price it from the feature table and you will not.

Spocket

Is Spocket worth it?

Spocket is genuinely best for dropshippers who want vetted US and EU suppliers with faster shipping and one-click store integration, prioritizing delivery speed over raw catalog size. Skip it if you want the widest possible catalog at the lowest sourcing cost (AliExpress-based tools fit), or your margins can't absorb both subscription and wholesale cost.

How much does Spocket cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-07) Four monthly plans, metered on unique products: Starter $39.99 (25 products), Pro $59.99 (250 products, 25 premium), Empire $99.99 (10,000 / 10,000) and Unicorn $299.99 (25,000 / 25,000). Annual billing is advertised as eight months free and the annual rates are printed on the cards: Pro $24 a month, Empire $57 and Unicorn $79, with stated savings of $432, $516 and $2,563. Unicorn's two figures do not reconcile - $299.99 a month for a year less $79 a month for a year is $2,651.88, not $2,563. There is a 7-day trial and 0% transaction fee on every tier. Multiple-store support is listed on all plans, but the page states a separate subscription is required for each store. Unicorn carries the MOST POPULAR badge. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Spocket?

Spocket's pitch is faster-shipping US and EU suppliers, and that's real — but you still pay twice: the monthly subscription and the wholesale product cost, so margins depend on picking items with room to mark up. Catalog breadth is narrower than giant AliExpress-based tools (that's the trade for vetting and shipping speed), and the low Starter product cap pushes serious stores up to Pro quickly. It reduces, not removes, the usual dropshipping risks.

Stackable

Is Stackable worth it?

Stackable is genuinely best for shopify stores running several promotions at once — an order discount, free shipping and a collection deal — that want shoppers to redeem them with one code instead of choosing, or that want the progress type which raises the discount as the cart fills. Skip it if you run one promotion at a time, because Shopify's own combined discounts already cover that at no cost — or the checkout upsells are the part you actually want, since those only exist in the $99.99 tier here.

How much does Stackable cost?

(prices read 2026-09-06 on apps.shopify.com/stackable-discounts) Two paid tiers, billed in USD every 30 days, and no free plan. Growth is $19.99 a month, or $199.99 a year with the annual saving the listing puts at 17%, and covers unlimited combined discounts; that plan carries the label 'For Non-Plus'. Unlimited is $99.99 a month, or $999.99 a year on the same 17%, and adds unlimited checkout upsells and unlimited linked discounts on top of the same combined discounts. Both tiers come with a 7-day free trial. The plan table lists no order caps, credit allowances or per-use charges, so what the tier costs is what the app costs. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Stackable?

The two halves of the pitch are priced five times apart. Discount stacking — order, collection and shipping discounts redeemed with a single code — is the $19.99 Growth plan, the one the listing labels 'For Non-Plus'. The checkout upsells and linked discounts the app leads with sit in the $99.99 Unlimited tier only, so a merchant who came for the upsells is reading $1,199.88 a year rather than $239.88. There is no free plan to settle whether the stacking alone lifts an order, so the seven-day trial is the entire evaluation. One more thing to check before you commit: the Website link on the listing, www.stkbl.app, now redirects to the documentation for Discount Kit — a different, pricier Optizio app — and that documentation does not mention Stackable anywhere (checked 6 September 2026). For an app that launched on 13 October 2020 and has collected 54 App Store reviews since, ask support where the current documentation lives before the trial clock starts.

Stamped

Is Stamped worth it?

Stamped is genuinely best for mid-market Shopify brands that want reviews and loyalty in one platform instead of juggling separate apps. Skip it if you're an early-stage store — the removed free plan and $199+/product pricing are steep before you have the volume to justify them.

How much does Stamped cost?

(re-verified 12 September 2026, read in a browser on their own pricing page across every step of the order-volume selector and both the single-product and bundle tabs) There is no free plan, and what you can actually buy depends on your monthly order volume. Below 5,000 orders a month the page sells only one product: Reviews, at $23/month at the 200-order step and $99/month at 1,000 orders. Repeat and Loyalty do not appear at those volumes at all. At the 5,000-order step the full line-up shows up — Repeat $499/month, Loyalty $299/month, Reviews $199/month — and the Multi-Product Bundle, which advertises 20% off, is a flat $798/month. The bundle tab locks the 200- and 1,000-order steps, so $798 is the entry price for taking more than one product, not a figure from the top of a ladder. From 20,000 orders upward, Unlimited included, every card turns into "Custom plan — Talk to Sales". Their FAQ says the same thing in words: plans start at $199/month for a single product and $798/month for multi-product access, and smaller brands are pointed at the self-serve plans in Stamped's Shopify App listings instead. Plans include up to two domains, each additional store gets its first month free, and additional domains are $100/month each. Sales tax is added as a separate line item. The redesigned page no longer says anything about overage charges. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Stamped?

The $798/month figure that circulates for the full suite is real, but it is a floor rather than a ceiling: that is what multi-product access costs from the 5,000-order step, and below that step you cannot buy the bundle at all — the pricing page sells Reviews on its own, $23/month at 200 orders and $99 at 1,000, and does not show Repeat or Loyalty. So the ladder has a cliff in it rather than a slope. Crossing 5,000 orders doubles Reviews from $99 to $199, and wanting a second product moves you to $798. A second storefront is another $100 a month on top, and past 20,000 orders every card turns into "Talk to Sales". Start with one product and price the step above the volume you actually expect.

Stampezee

Is Stampezee worth it?

Stampezee is genuinely best for local businesses (cafés, salons, retail) that want a simple digital stamp-card loyalty program starting free. Skip it if you need POS-integrated loyalty with CRM depth (bigger platforms exist), or your offer isn't repeat-visit shaped.

How much does Stampezee cost?

(read 2026-08-30 on stampezee.com/en/pricing from a US exit) Four tiers, all now named and priced on the public page. Stamp Start free: 1 branch, 1 stamp card, up to 100 customers or 100 stamps, whichever comes first. Stamp Lite $29.99/month: 2 branches, 3 stamp cards, unlimited customers and stamps, signup rewards, EzeeCodes, birthday/anniversary/referral automations. Stamp Pro $49.99: 3 branches, 6 cards, spend-based stamping, tiered and exclusive rewards, 4 push notifications. Note the entry tier's own contradiction: the plan card frames Stamp Start as a 14-day free trial, the comparison table on the same page lists it as Free with no time limit. What is the catch with Stampezee?

The category is honest and proven (digital stamp cards beat lost paper cards), and the platform is young with limited public pricing and review coverage — so start on the free plan, run one real campaign, and measure repeat-visit lift before paying.
