StoreSEO

Is StoreSEO worth it?

StoreSEO is genuinely best for Shopify stores with a few hundred products and no in-house SEO help, who want metadata, schema, alt text and indexing handled in bulk and reported against Search Console. Skip it if you have fewer than 25 products, in which case the free tier is the whole product, or you expect an app to fix a demand problem rather than a metadata one.

How much does StoreSEO cost?

(read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/storeseo) Free Forever covers 25 products with SEO scoring, 200 AI credits, 25 image optimisations, up to 5 tracked keywords, an LLMs.txt generator and Agents.md editor, an SEO migrator, alt-text optimisation and 24/7 chat support. Paid tiers are Lite $14.99, Essential $39.99 and Advanced $249.99 a month, each with a 7-day free trial. Lite covers 100 products, 500 image optimisations and 1,000 AI credits and adds one-click schema markup, instant indexing requests, Google Analytics and Search Console and automatic sitemap submission. Essential covers 250 products, 2,000 images and 5,000 credits. Advanced covers 10,000 products, 50,000 images, 50,000 credits and adds multilingual SEO. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Worth knowing: storeseo.com sells a Growth plan at $99.99 a month (1,000 products, 5,000 images, 12,500 AI credits, 200 keywords) that does not appear on the App Store listing at all, and also sells credit top-ups from $10 for 5,000 credits and $50 for 25,000. Rating 5.0 from 751 App Store reviews, re-read 19 September 2026 (it was 674 on 19 August). Developer Storeware, Milton, Delaware; the app launched 19 October 2021 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with StoreSEO?

Know what an SEO app can and cannot do before you buy any tier. This one fixes the mechanical layer well — meta titles and descriptions in bulk, alt text, compressed images, JSON-LD, sitemaps, indexing requests — and none of that creates demand for products nobody is searching for. It is maintenance, not marketing, and on a catalogue of 25 products the free tier already does most of it. Two specifics worth a raised eyebrow. The pricing gap between Essential at $39.99 for 250 products and Advanced at $249.99 for 10,000 is filled by a $99.99 Growth plan. That plan lives on the vendor's own site but not on the App Store listing our link points to, which is a strange place to hide a tier. And the AEO/GEO features — the LLMs.txt generator, the Agents.md editor, the separate “agentic” ranking — are a bet, not a channel. No major search or AI vendor has committed to reading llms.txt, so treat those numbers as a hypothesis you are testing rather than traffic you are buying.

Is Storista worth it?

Storista is genuinely best for Shopify stores that already produce TikTok or Reels content and want it on the storefront as shoppable video, with the free tier's unlimited views making it cheap to test whether social video converts on your product pages at all. Skip it if you have no UGC or short-form pipeline to feed it — the widget displays content, it does not create any — or you want automatic product-to-video tagging without paying $49 a month for it.

How much does Storista cost?

(read 2026-08-23 on apps.shopify.com/storista-stories, listed as “Storista Shoppable Video UGC”) Four tiers. Free covers 10 videos with unlimited views, TikTok Shop and Shop app integration, GEO/SEO optimisation and the Carousel and Spotlight widgets, and it keeps Storista branding on the widget. Basic is $15 a month for 50 videos, unlimited views, basic analytics and videos on any page. Business is $49 a month for unlimited videos, AI Smart Tagging, advanced analytics and all widget types. Scale is $199 a month for Shopify Plus stores and adds VIP support and multiple stores. Every paid tier carries a 14-day free trial, all charges are billed in USD, and recurring and usage-based charges are billed every 30 days. The app is English-only, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge and works with Checkout, Shopify Admin, TikTok Shop, the Shop app, Instagram Reels, TikTok Videos, GemPages, Rebuy, Skio, Shogun and Subscriptions. Developer Storista LLC, Sheridan, Wyoming; the app launched on 19 February 2021 and had 49 reviews at a 5.0 average at the time of writing. Note that storista.io, the vendor's own domain, sells a different product on a different meter — AI-generated UGC video at roughly $1 to $4 a render, free to start with a $19 a month Pro plan — and not the widget ladder above. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Storista?

The first thing to know is that the brand sells two different products, and the one you find by searching the name is not the one this link installs. storista.io is an AI UGC video generator priced per render, roughly $1 to $4 a video, free to start with a $19 a month Pro plan. The Shopify app is a shoppable-video widget priced at $0, $15, $49 and $199 a month. Same company, same name, unrelated ladders, and nothing on either page maps one to the other. If you arrive at a price expecting the other product, you will be wrong by a factor of ten in either direction. Second, read the headline against the pricing table. AI Smart Tagging is one of four bullets in the app's own pitch and one of the four features named in the listing summary. It appears on Business at $49 and above. On Free and Basic you tag products to videos yourself. Third, the rating deserves its detail. 5.0 from 49 reviews is excellent, and the breakdown is 47 five-star, one four-star and one one-star — so the round number is a rounding, not a perfect record. That is a small point, but it is the kind of thing worth checking on any app whose average sits exactly on the ceiling. Finally, the data access. The listing states the app views customer device and activity data and can view and edit customers, products, store analytics, custom data and Shopify admin. That is a wide grant for a widget that displays video, and it belongs in your processing register whatever you decide about the product.

Is Storylane worth it?

How much does Storylane cost?

What is the catch with Storylane?

The jump from Starter to Growth is $50 to $625 a month — twelve and a half times — and the free tier is capped at one live demo, so the moment you want a second demo published you are on the ladder. Price that against what you already pay a separate tool to do, because it is the meter that decides your tier, not the number of demos. Is Streak worth it?

Everyone on a team must be on the same plan. Success.co

Is Success.co worth it?

Success.co is genuinely best for leadership teams that already run on goals and want one place to set objectives, track KPIs and scorecards, and keep strategy execution on cadence. How much does Success.co cost?

(read 2026-08-21 in Success.co's own structured data on success.co/pricing and re-read there unchanged on 2026-09-08) There is a Free Forever plan at $0, and the paid product is tiered per user with the rate falling as the team grows. Monthly billing: $12 per user a month for 1-25 users, $11 for 26-75, $9 for 76-125, $7 for 126-250 and $6 for 251-1,000. What is the catch with Success.co?

Is SupaEasy worth it?

How much does SupaEasy cost?

How much does Super cost?

(price read 2026-09-12) Four paid tiers, billed in USD every 30 days through Shopify, and the Shopify listing prints only three of them. On apps.shopify.com/super-gift-wraps: Basic is $9.99 a month or $83.92 a year for a paid or free gift message and a gift receipt that hides prices; Advanced $12.99 or $109.12 adds one paid or free gift wrap and an animated gift label; Pro $19.99 or $167.92 adds unlimited wraps, pop-up and checkbox display types, cart and product-page placement, custom images and gift revenue reporting. If you are on Shopify Plus, the price block on the listing is not the one you pay from — the three published tiers exclude Plus stores in their own text, and the tier that covers you is $24.99 in a help-centre article. On 24 August 2026 another Effective Apps title, TnC, carried a ladder we had verified the day before; twenty-four hours later every tier had gone up with no change to the feature lists. Treat any price for this developer that is older than the day you read it as a guess, this one included. The review base is broad and middling: 4.7 over 254 reviews on 12 September 2026, 227 of them five-star but seven at one star, on an app listed since 17 August 2020. The app reads customer device and activity data and can view and edit products, orders and the Online Store. And be honest about what it sells. Is SurveySparrow worth it?

Used the other way round, as a drafting and structuring tool for posts you actually edit, it is sensible. The price is the second thing to watch, and on 19 September 2026 there is none to read. Is Tapstitch worth it?

Teikametrics

Is Teikametrics worth it?

Teikametrics is genuinely best for Amazon and Walmart sellers spending enough on ads that a few points of efficiency covers the fee — under $10K a month the flat $149 is straightforward. How much does Teikametrics cost?

(2026-08-30, re-read on their own pricing page from a US exit) Essentials, for up to $10K a month in ad spend: $149 a month billed annually, or $179 billed monthly. Advanced, for over $10K a month in ad spend: custom pricing plus 3% of ad spend above $10K. Enterprise, for over $100K a month in ad spend: also custom pricing plus 3% of ad spend above $10K. What is the catch with Teikametrics?

Read the Advanced tier carefully, because it is not a subscription — it is a subscription plus a percentage. Three per cent of ad spend above $10,000 means a seller spending $40,000 a month pays an extra $900 on top of whatever the custom base is, and that line scales with the thing the product is supposed to make more efficient. That is not automatically wrong — it aligns them with your growth — but it does mean your bill rises when your advertising does, and you should model it at your expected spend rather than your current one. The $10K threshold is the number to watch: crossing it changes the pricing model, not just the price.

TicketTailor

Is TicketTailor worth it?

TicketTailor is genuinely best for event organizers with their own audience (venues, communities, creators) who want flat low per-ticket fees, full branding and no subscription. Skip it if you depend on marketplace discovery to sell tickets (Eventbrite's traffic is the fee you're paying for), or you run two events a year at tiny volume.

How much does TicketTailor cost?

(re-verified 2026-09-09 on tickettailor.com/pricing with the currency switched to USD) No subscription and no contract: pay-as-you-sell $0.85 a ticket, or prepaid credits from $0.70 down to $0.34 depending on volume — 100 credits (the minimum) cost $70, 500 cost $300, 1,000 cost $520 and 20,000 cost $6,800. Credits carry no time limit. Free events are free up to 5,000 tickets a year, the first five paid tickets cost nothing, and charities, B Corps, PTAs and not-for-profits get 50% off, as do very low-priced tickets. Seated tickets cost two credits rather than one. Prices switch across GBP, EUR, USD, AUD and CAD. Stripe, PayPal or Square fees apply separately and Ticket Tailor never touches the payment. Note one contradiction in their own FAQ: one answer puts the free-ticket allowance at 5,000 a year, another at 2,000. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with TicketTailor?

The fee honesty is the product — flat cents per ticket instead of percentage skims makes it dramatically cheaper than the big platforms on higher-priced tickets (a $0.30-0.85 fee on a $50 ticket vs a percentage is no contest). Is TiXel worth it?

TiXel is genuinely best for Shopify merchants running Meta and TikTok ads who need more than the free channel apps give them — several pixels on one store, pixels scoped to individual products, or server-side Events API tracking alongside the browser pixel to recover events that ad-blockers and Safari strip. Skip it if you run one pixel for one brand, since Shopify's Meta and TikTok channels do that for nothing; or you cannot put real traffic through the store inside the seven-day trial, because the reported failure is a pixel that installs cleanly and then tracks nothing.

How much does TiXel cost?

Unlimited Plan is $19.99 a month, or $119.94 a year at a stated 50% saving, and carries unlimited pixels, server-side Events API pixels, regular pixels via pixel code, pixels scoped to specific products, automatic event triggers with no manual event configuration, accurate tracking and online support. One term has changed and it matters: the free trial is now seven days, where the listing advertised three in August. The review record has moved a long way: 93 reviews at 4.6, up from 78 at 4.1 in August, distributed 84 five-star, 3 four-star, none at three or two, and 6 one-star — one fewer bottom-rated review than a month ago, against fifteen more reviews overall. What is the catch with TiXel?

The rating is the most useful number on this listing, but not for the reason an average usually is. Read on 18 September 2026 it is 4.6 across 93 reviews, and the shape behind it is 84 five-star, 3 four-star, nothing at three or two, and 6 one-star. A month earlier it was 4.1 across 78, with 7 at the bottom. Nothing sits in the middle on either reading. That is not a mediocre product; it is a binary one — it works immediately, or it installs cleanly and then tracks nothing at all. The one-star reviews describe the same failure in the same words: the pixel is set up by the instructions, no page views or add-to-carts ever arrive, and support does not reply. We cannot verify what happened in any individual account, but the consistency of the complaint is itself information. What is new since August is that the developer now answers them in public. A reply dated 2 September 2026 attributes the empty data to manual pixel configuration, where one mismatched ID or event setting is enough to stop events being recorded at all, and says that step is no longer needed: TiXel now integrates officially with Meta and TikTok and links the pixel to your ad account automatically. That is the vendor's account of its own worst reviews, so treat it as a claim to test rather than a fix to trust. It is at least a specific and checkable one, and the trial has gone from three days to seven, which is enough room to check it.

TnC

Is TnC worth it?

TnC is genuinely best for Shopify merchants on a standard plan who need a recorded “I agree” gate before payment — for GDPR, an age gate, digital-goods withdrawal rules or chargeback defence — and who go to Advanced at $12.99 for the consent timestamp rather than stopping at the $7.99 headline. Skip it if you are on Shopify Plus and want the checkbox inside the real checkout page, where the plan you need is the $19.99 Plus tier the App Store listing does not show; you expected a free tier from the listing's badge, which covers development and partner stores only; or a checkbox on the cart and the express buttons is not the enforcement your legal requirement actually asks for.

How much does TnC cost?

(read 2026-08-25 and re-verified 2026-09-09 on apps.shopify.com/terms-and-conditions-checkbox, listed as “TnC: Terms and Conditions Box”, and in the vendor's own pricing article at www.effectify.help) The monthly ladder is $7.99, $12.99 and $14.99, and it has held there since the August rise: read on 24 August 2026 the same three plans, carrying the same feature lists, cost $6.99, $9.99 and $12.99. What moved between 25 August and 9 September is the annual price. It used to be $67.12, $109.12 and $125.92, roughly a 30% saving; the listing now shows $47.94, $77.94 and $89.94 and says “save 50%”. That is exactly six months' money for a year at every tier, where in August it was seven-tenths of the year, so the annual route got cheaper while the monthly one did not move at all. Four plans on the listing, and the free one is not for you. Development Stores is free and carries every Pro feature, but the listing states it is for development and partner stores only and that payment will be activated on upgrade — so the “Free plan available” line at the top of the listing describes a partner sandbox rather than a free tier for a store that takes orders. Basic is $7.99 a month or $47.94 a year and covers the AI terms-and-conditions checkbox with support for Buy It Now and express checkout buttons. Advanced is $12.99 a month or $77.94 a year and adds the consent date logged into the order's details plus the ability to show the checkbox for specific countries and products. Pro is $14.99 a month or $89.94 a year and adds newsletter and contact forms, translation of the checkbox into multiple languages, the checkbox in Shopify POS and an AI-powered policies generator. Every paid tier carries a 7-day free trial, and the listing states charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. The vendor's own pricing article, re-read on 9 September 2026, has not followed. It still prints the old annual rates of $67.12, $109.12 and $125.92, still puts the annual saving at approximately 30%, and still answers its own question “are there any hidden fees?” with “No. All pricing is transparent and listed above” — while the App Store listing, which is where the charge is actually raised, prints a different number for the same plan. It is also the only page where a fifth plan appears at all: a Plus Plan at $19.99 a month or $167.92 a year, for Shopify Plus merchants only, adding “the ability to show the checkbox in the actual Checkout page of your store”. The Plus Plan is the one monthly rate that has never moved, so the gap between the top listed plan and the hidden one is $5. The article also notes that uninstalling during an ongoing billing period still incurs that period's charge. Developer Effective Apps, trading as Effectify, at 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched on 2 December 2019, carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge, and stood at 550 listing reviews with a 4.9 average on 9 September 2026, up from 514 two weeks earlier. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with TnC?

Start with the badge at the top of the listing, because it is the one thing on this page that misleads. “Free plan available” is displayed twice, and the free plan is Development Stores — for development and partner stores only, with payment activated on upgrade. A store that takes real orders has no free tier here. It is the same shape as this developer's Blocky and TiXel listings, where the advertised free plan is also development stores rather than a working free tier, so read it as a house pattern rather than an oversight. Second, the App Store's pricing table is incomplete. The vendor's own help-centre article lists a Plus Plan at $19.99 a month, Shopify Plus only, and describes it as the plan that shows the checkbox in the actual checkout page. The App Store listing shows four plans and not that one. The same article answers its own hidden-fees question with “No. All pricing is transparent and listed above”, which is true of that article and not of the listing most buyers will read first. If you are on Plus and you want consent captured in checkout rather than in the cart, the price is two and a half times the headline. Third, the feature that makes the app defensible costs extra, and what it costs is not stable. Basic at $7.99 shows the checkbox; it does not record when anyone ticked it. Consent-date logging starts on Advanced at $12.99. Read a day earlier, on 24 August 2026, those same two plans were $6.99 and $9.99 with identical feature lists, so the step from checkbox to audit trail went from $3 to $5 overnight while the listing said nothing about it. For an app whose pitch is chargebacks and legal risk, an audit trail as a paid upgrade is worth knowing before you compare $7.99 against anything else. Fourth, be clear about what this can and cannot enforce. On a store that is not on Shopify Plus the checkbox lives in the cart and on express-checkout buttons, not inside Shopify's checkout, because Shopify does not open that page to apps below Plus. The listing is honest about the surfaces it does cover — cart drawers, Buy It Now, express checkout buttons, floating carts, PayPal and Apple Pay — but a shopper who reaches payment by another route has not passed a gate. Whether that is sufficient consent is a question for your own counsel rather than for an app listing. Finally, the data access. The listing states the app views device and activity data including geolocation, IP address, browser and operating system and browsing behaviour, and can view and edit customers, products, orders for the last 60 days, store analytics, web pixels and the Online Store script tags and theme. Geolocation is what the country targeting on Advanced and above runs on, so the scope is explicable, but an app installed for compliance reasons that itself processes IP addresses and browsing behaviour belongs in the same register as everything else you had to write down.

Their FAQ also states Shopify Plus is NOT required except for checkout customization and checkout upsells, which is a Shopify restriction; cart, product page, cart drawer, thank-you and post-purchase offers work without it. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with UpsellPlus?

The plans are capped by the revenue they are allowed to earn you, and the first paid step does not raise that cap: Free and the $49 Launch plan both stop at $500 of upsell revenue a month. The $49 buys offers and features, not headroom — headroom starts at $119. And crossing a ceiling is not something you decide: their FAQ says you are automatically upgraded to the next tier so the offers keep running, so a good week moves the invoice on its own. Read the feature list closely too, because the tier named Shopify Plus is not the same thing as the requirement — their FAQ says Plus is needed only for checkout customization and checkout upsells, so on a standard Shopify store the checkout half of a checkout-upsell app is not what you are buying. The last gap is at the top: the plan card says Scale stops at $5,000 a month and the comparison table on the same page says Unlimited, and above it sits an Enterprise tier with no published price at all.

Volza

Is Volza worth it?

Volza is genuinely best for import-export businesses and sourcing teams that want global customs-level trade data plus verified buyer/supplier contacts at a fraction of enterprise pricing. Skip it if you only need US shipment data with fast daily updates (ImportGenius refreshes daily), or you're not doing import/export — this is a niche intelligence tool.

How much does Volza cost?

(read 2026-09-01 on volza.com/pricing) Three paid annual plans and a free trial. Startup is $1,500 a year: 182 countries (44 export and 50 import detailed databases, 160 export and 158 import mirror databases, 7 export and 7 import one-side databases, premium countries excluded), data from 2014 onward, 6,000 searches, full shipment view, 360,000 full-shipment download credits and 2 users. SME is $4,500 a year: 200 countries, adds the statistical databases (46 export, 48 import), unlimited searches under fair use, 1,040,000 download credits and 10 users. Corporate is $9,600 a year: the same 200-country coverage, unlimited searches under fair use, 2,400,000 download credits and 15 users. The free trial runs 7 days with no card, is advertised as "$50 On sign up + Unlimited Volza credits", shows the last three years in full view with a six-month preview, and carries no full-shipment download credits. An annual and a 2-year value plan are offered as billing terms. The page also states a refund promise: if you find no profitable opportunity, Volza will help you find one or refund in full. What is the catch with Volza?

Three honest catches. The entry plan is narrower than the marketing implies: $1,500 a year covers 182 countries and two users, while the 200-country coverage and ten seats start at $4,500. Downloads run on a credit allowance — 360,000 a year on Startup — and an earlier reading of the catalogue put the cost per record at one credit for US or India shipments and up to ten in thinner markets; that per-country rate is not stated on the current pricing page and we could not re-verify it on 1 September 2026, so treat it as a question for sales rather than a fact. And the update cycle is slow, with some datasets taking up to two months to refresh, which suits structural questions far better than reactive ones. There is a learning curve too; it rewards analysts, not casual users.

Is VWO worth it?

How much does VWO cost?

Re-read on 20 September 2026: vwo.com now answers HTTP 301 and redirects to wingify.com — vwo.com/pricing/ to wingify.com/pricing/, vwo.com/free-trial/ to wingify.com/free-trial/ — and the pricing page is titled "Pricing & Plans | Wingify Platform", with the products named Wingify Testing, Wingify Personalization and Wingify Insights and a site-wide banner announcing that AB Tasty and VWO have united. The ~$314/mo for 10k MTUs this dossier carried until 4 September 2026 was a published figure the vendor has since withdrawn. Two things are new on the page. What is the catch with VWO?

VWO applies page changes through its SmartCode — their own page says the asynchronous SmartCode “loads page changes asynchronously when the web page loads” — so a variant left running in the editor is rendered by VWO rather than built into your site. Fine while you pay, gone when you stop. Their server-side testing changes the arithmetic here, because those changes live in your own stack; the client-side ones do not.

Warn

Is Warn worth it?

Warn is genuinely best for shopify merchants who know exactly which notice they need — a Prop 65 label, a shipping-delay alert, an age-verification disclaimer, a we-no-longer-ship-here message — and want it on the right products, collections or countries without touching theme code, for $6.99 a month or nothing at all if one plain warning will do. Skip it if you are on a standard Shopify plan and specifically want the checkout blocked or a warning shown on the Checkout page: both are Plus Plan features and the Plus Plan is for Shopify Plus stores, so the capability the app's name advertises is not available to you at any price here. Also skip it if you sell off Shopify, or if what you actually need is consent and privacy management — cookie banners, consent records, data-subject requests — rather than a notice on a page..

How much does Warn cost?

(prices read 2026-09-20 on apps.shopify.com/product-notes) Billed in USD, every 30 days, and the ladder has three steps rather than the two the app's own summary suggests. Free gives you one textual warning across unlimited products, with the styling, per-product targeting and per-country targeting included. Premium is $6.99 a month or $41.94 a year, and the annual figure really is half of twelve monthly payments. It lifts the cap to unlimited warnings, notes and pop-ups, adds cart and checkout warnings, targeting by product or collection, and US-state geo-targeting on top of country targeting — but the plan is labelled for all stores EXCEPT Shopify Plus. Plus Plan is $12.99 a month or $77.94 a year, again exactly half of twelve monthly payments, and it is the Shopify Plus plan: the same feature list, plus warnings shown on the Checkout itself and the rule that lets a warning block checkout when configured. Both paid plans carry a 7-day free trial. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with Warn?

The app is called Warn: Warnings Checkout Blocks, and blocking checkout is the one thing most readers of this listing cannot buy at the advertised price. Checkout blocking, and showing a warning on the Checkout page at all, sits on the Plus Plan at $12.99 a month — and that plan says, in the App Store's own words, that it is for Shopify Plus stores. The $6.99 Premium plan says the opposite: for all stores except Shopify Plus. So the two tiers are not a small ladder and a big one, they are two different audiences, and which one you may buy is decided by your Shopify subscription rather than by how much warning you need. If you are on a standard Shopify plan and came here to stop a checkout, read the plan labels before you install. The second thing to be clear about is what the app does and does not take off your hands. It renders the notice, targets it by product, collection or country, and styles it to your store. It does not tell you what Proposition 65, a GDPR withdrawal notice or an age-verification disclaimer has to say in your jurisdiction, and it does not keep that wording current when the rule changes. The compliance language stays your problem and your liability; this is the display layer for it.

Is Way worth it?

How much does Way cost?

What is the catch with Way?

Is WhatConverts worth it?

Is Wholesale Gorilla worth it?

How much does Wholesale Gorilla cost?

What is the catch with Zendrop?

Their own pricing page and the App Store listing do not agree: the site sells Free, Pro and Plus with annual rates and no $29 tier, which means the price depends on where you sign up. And the 4.6 average covers a split verdict, with 83% five stars alongside 7% one star across 1,258 reviews — 84 people rating it bottom of the scale.

Read the full Zendrop review →

ZoomInfo

Is ZoomInfo worth it?

ZoomInfo is genuinely best for enterprise go-to-market teams that need the deepest US database, buyer-intent signals and conversation intelligence — and can absorb the contract. Skip it if you're an SMB or want flexible month-to-month pricing — the cost, credit burn and lock-in rarely pay off below enterprise scale.

How much does ZoomInfo cost?

Sales-gated, and re-verified as such on 2026-08-17: no public rates, no monthly billing and no free plan, with the pricing URL refusing plain requests and neither of our monthly captures retrieving a figure. Contracts typically start around $15k and the median runs near $32k a year, climbing once seats, credits and add-ons (intent data, international coverage) stack up — but those are third-party figures, not ZoomInfo's, and every deal is negotiated annually. Expect a multi-year push and price the credits, not just the seats. Always verify the live price.

What is the catch with ZoomInfo?

The contract is the most-cited frustration: annual lock-in with a strict 60–90 day cancellation window and 10–20% renewal increases. Credits burn fast, data can be stale (prospects who left years ago), and it's built for enterprise — overkill and overpriced for SMBs, with weaker accuracy outside the US.
